findings.title: Approved return refunds the customer but never reverses the affiliate commission that delivery already confirmed
findings.detail: functions/src/orders/status.ts:98-101 calls confirmCommissionsForOrder(orderId) the moment an order reaches 'delivered', which moves the commission row to status 'confirmed' and increments affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise — the withdrawable balance (commissions.ts:128-133). The docblock at functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11-14 justifies clearing at delivery on the grounds that "Returns are handled by the return flow". They are not: adminApproveOrderRequest (decisions.ts) contains zero references to 'commission' or 'affiliate' (grep -i returns nothing in the whole file). Its order write at line 116-122 only touches refundedPaise / paymentStatus / items[].returnStatus. Only performCancellation (cancel.ts:73-75) reverses commissions, and it deliberately skips rows that are no longer 'pending' — and cancellation is impossible after delivery anyway (TRANSITIONS.delivered = []). So once an order is delivered there is no code path anywhere that can claw a commission back.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer C was referred by affiliate A (5% rate). C places a Rs 10,000 order -> commissions doc created with commissionPaise=50000, A.pendingBalancePaise +50000. Admin marks the order 'delivered' -> row becomes 'confirmed', A.confirmedBalancePaise +50000, lifetimeEarningsPaise +50000. C returns the goods; admin approves the return, Rs 10,000 is refunded to C's wallet. The commission row stays 'confirmed' and A withdraws Rs 500 of real money on a fully refunded order. Repeatable at will by a colluding referrer/customer pair.
findings.fix: In adminApproveOrderRequest's transaction (or a helper mirroring cancel.ts:129-143), read the commissions rows for r.orderId up front and, for the refunded proportion, decrement affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise + lifetimeEarningsPaise and mark the row 'cancelled' (or write a negative clawback row when the balance has already been withdrawn). Alternatively delay confirmation past the return window instead of clearing at delivery.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable money defect. status.ts:98-101 calls confirmCommissionsForOrder on 'delivered', and commissions.ts:128-133 moves the row to 'confirmed' while incrementing affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise (the withdrawable balance per the architecture rules) and lifetimeEarningsPaise. returns/decisions.ts contains zero references to commission/affiliate — adminApproveOrderRequest only credits the customer wallet, writes a walletTransactions row, and updates orderRequests + order refundedPaise/paymentStatus/items[].returnStatus (lines 94-126). The only reversal code, performCancellation (cancel.ts:73-79), deliberately filters to status === 'pending' and is unreachable after delivery anyway (TRANSITIONS.delivered = [] at status.ts:20). Crucially, returns/requests.ts:39 requires o.status === 'delivered', so the return flow can only ever run AFTER the commission has been confirmed — the ordering guarantees no pending row is left to reverse. No other surface can compensate: grep for 'commission' finds nothing in scheduled/sweeps.ts, returns/, or wallet/, and firestore.rules:86-89 makes the commissions collection allow write: if false, so neither admin UI nor client can adjust it. The docblock at commissions.ts:11-14 justifying immediate clearance on the grounds that "Returns are handled by the return flow" is factually false about this codebase, which makes it an incompleteness rather than an intentional design choice. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic/UI, server-side and fixable (reverse or partially reverse the confirmed commission inside the approve transaction).

findings.title: Affiliate toggle on both customer screens always fails — the callable requires commissionRate that the client never sends
findings.detail: setAffiliateEnabled() calls httpsCallable('adminAllocateAffiliate') with the payload `{ uid }` only (customers.ts:57-60). The callable's zod schema in functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:20 is `z.object({ uid: z.string().min(1), commissionRate: z.number().nonnegative(), walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional() })` — `commissionRate` is REQUIRED, not optional. safeParse therefore fails and line 22 throws HttpsError('invalid-argument','Invalid payload.'). The other caller, admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:63, does send commissionRate, so only the customers-module toggle is broken. The revoke direction ('adminRevokeAffiliate') parses `{ uid }` only and works, so the toggle is one-way-broken.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Customers list (or a customer profile) and flips the Affiliate toggle ON for Yusuf Ali. The CF rejects with invalid-argument; the UI shows the cfError toast, `customer.affiliate` is never created, no referral code is allocated, and the toggle snaps back. Affiliate access can only ever be granted from the separate Allocate Affiliate page.
findings.fix: Either send a rate from the customers screens (e.g. `call({ uid, commissionRate: settings.defaultCommissionRate })`) or make the CF field optional with a server-side default: `commissionRate: z.number().nonnegative().optional()` and `const rate = normalise(parsed.data.commissionRate ?? DEFAULT_RATE)` — while preserving an existing affiliate's rate on re-enable.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:59 sends only `{ uid }` to adminAllocateAffiliate, but functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:20 requires `commissionRate: z.number().nonnegative()` — not optional, no .default(), and `rate` at line 24 is derived solely from parsed.data.commissionRate with no settings-based or server-side fallback. safeParse fails and line 22 throws HttpsError('invalid-argument') before the customer doc is even read, so no affiliate object, referral code, or role is ever written. Both call sites are live UI: CustomersListPage.tsx:131 and CustomerProfilePage.tsx:141 render Toggles wired to onToggleAffiliate -> setAffiliateEnabled, and both catch into a cfError toast. The revoke direction is fine (withdrawals.ts:49 parses `{ uid }` only), so the toggle is genuinely one-way-broken. The only working grant path is admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:58-65, which passes { uid, commissionRate, walletEnabled }. Not cosmetic (payload/schema mismatch, not styling), not unreachable, and not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL deferrals. Fixable either by having setAffiliateEnabled send a default commissionRate or by giving the zod field a .default() server-side.

findings.title: autoBestOffer reads promo-coupon field names the admin never writes, so the percent cap, min-cart and expiry are all silently unenforced on real money
findings.detail: `placeOrder` calls `autoBestOffer` whenever the client sends no coupon code (checkout.ts:349). For promotional `coupons` docs it reads `c.minOrderPaise` (line 228), `c.maxDiscountPaise` (line 233), `c.expiresAt` (line 226-227) and `c.noExpiry`. The admin writer (admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-138) writes `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise` and `validUntil`, and never writes `expiresAt`, `noExpiry`, `minOrderPaise`, `maxDiscountPaise` or `autoApply`. Every one of those reads is therefore `undefined`, so `Number(undefined ?? 0) === 0` disables the check. The sibling `computeCouponDiscount` (lines 143/172/140) uses the correct names — the bug is isolated to the auto-apply path. Note the code-comment at checkout.ts:131 says this class of mismatch was already fixed once for computeCouponDiscount; autoBestOffer was missed.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates coupon SAVE25: percent, 25%, Max discount ₹200 (discountPercent=25, discountMaxCapPaise=20000), Min cart ₹1500, targetUsers 'all'. A customer checks out a ₹10,000 cart with no coupon code. autoBestOffer sees minOrderPaise=undefined→0 (min cart bypassed) and maxDiscountPaise=undefined→0 (cap skipped), so it grants Math.round(1000000*25/100) = ₹2,500 instead of the capped ₹200. The order is written and charged with a ₹2,300 over-discount. The same undefined `expiresAt` means a coupon that expired hours ago (status still 'active' until the next 00:15 IST sweep) is still auto-applied.
findings.fix: In autoBestOffer read the same fields computeCouponDiscount does: `c.minCartValuePaise`, `c.discountMaxCapPaise`, `c.validUntil` (plus `validFrom`), and drop `noExpiry`/`minOrderPaise`/`maxDiscountPaise`. Better: extract one shared `evaluatePromoCoupon(c, subtotal)` helper used by both paths so they cannot drift again.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real and money-affecting. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:226-234 (autoBestOffer) reads c.expiresAt, c.noExpiry, c.minOrderPaise and c.maxDiscountPaise on promotional `coupons` docs. No writer anywhere in the repo produces those fields: admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-138 writes minCartValuePaise/discountMaxCapPaise/validUntil (and never autoApply/noExpiry/expiresAt), scripts/seed.ts:715-725 writes the same canonical names, packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:26-27 declares discountMaxCapPaise/minCartValuePaise, and functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts:36 sweeps on validUntil. Every read is therefore undefined, so Number(undefined ?? 0) === 0 disables the min-cart gate and the `if (cap > 0)` percent cap, and the expiry check no-ops. The sibling computeCouponDiscount (lines 140/143/172) uses the correct names — the comment at lines 132-134 documents this exact mismatch being fixed there once; autoBestOffer was missed. autoBestOffer additionally skips maxUsesTotal, maxUsesPerUser and firstOrderOnly, which computeCouponDiscount enforces. The path is reachable on both clients: the Flutter app sends couponCode: draft.coupon?.code (app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:108) which is null by default since the app has no auto-apply (only manual select/clear in widgets/coupon_apply.dart:87,149), and web sends null after the user hits the remove control at web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:337. The resulting discountPaise flows unchecked into summarise() (checkout.ts:411) and onto the order total, wallet debit and Razorpay amount — no downstream re-validation exists. On web it is worse than a silent over-discount: the server re-applies an offer the user explicitly removed, uncapped, so the charged total exceeds the total shown. Not a UI-only issue and not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL exclusions. (Aside: web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:39-47 shares the wrong names but is display-only; app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart reads the correct name via a fallback key list, so the app UI shows the capped amount while the server charges the uncapped one.)

findings.title: Web checkout offer list uses the same wrong coupon field names, so it auto-applies coupons that placeOrder then rejects
findings.detail: `PromoCoupon` (lines 20-34) declares `minOrderPaise`, `maxDiscountPaise`, `expiresAt`, `noExpiry` — none of which admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts writes. `promoDiscount` (line 42) therefore treats every promo coupon as min-cart-₹0, (line 47) uncapped, and (line 41) never expired. `listAvailableOffers` repeats it at lines 114-115 and `promoHeadline` at line 84 hides the cap. checkout/page.tsx:90 auto-applies `bestOfferForCart` into the draft and page.tsx:99 renders the list, while `placeOrder` re-validates with the CORRECT field names (checkout.ts:143/172) and throws HttpsError on mismatch.
findings.failure_scenario: Coupon SAVE25 = 25% off, max ₹200, min cart ₹1500. Customer with a ₹500 cart opens /checkout: the offer renders as "25% off · On any order", qualifies=true, and is auto-applied showing a ₹125 discount. They press Pay and placeOrder throws 'Your cart does not meet this coupon's minimum' — checkout is hard-blocked and nothing in the UI explains why. On a ₹10,000 cart the page shows a ₹2,500 discount but the server caps it at ₹200, so the amount charged is ₹2,300 more than the total displayed a moment earlier.
findings.fix: Change PromoCoupon to `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise`, `validUntil` and update promoDiscount/listAvailableOffers/promoHeadline accordingly (the Flutter app already reads both names defensively — see app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:55-56,65). Ideally type it as the shared `Coupon` instead of a hand-rolled loose interface.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts reads minOrderPaise / maxDiscountPaise / expiresAt / noExpiry, but admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-153 (saveCoupon) and scripts/seed.ts:707-731 write minCartValuePaise / discountMaxCapPaise / validUntil. A repo-wide grep shows minOrderPaise|maxDiscountPaise|noExpiry appear ONLY in offers.ts and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts autoBestOffer (lines 227-233) — no surface writes them (admin CouponFormPage's noExpiry is local UI state converted to validUntil:null). No normalization layer: web/src/lib/useCollection.ts:22 returns snap.data() raw and checkout/page.tsx:80 casts directly to PromoCoupon. The "server re-checks" defence fails: checkout/page.tsx:90 writes the auto-applied code into the draft, web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:218 sends couponCode, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:347-349 therefore takes the explicit-code branch computeCouponDiscount, which uses the CORRECT names at lines 143/172/141 and throws HttpsError 'Your cart does not meet this coupon's minimum'. The lenient autoBestOffer is only reached when couponCode is null. checkout.ts:135-137 even carries a comment that the names were previously wrong and were fixed server-side — offers.ts (and autoBestOffer) were left stale. Impact is functional, not cosmetic: hard checkout block on sub-minimum carts, and a charged total higher than displayed whenever the percent cap binds. Only inaccuracy in the claim: free_shipping promos won't auto-apply since bestOfferForCart requires discountPaise > 0.

findings.title: Web banner query filters placement == 'web' but the enum value and every writer use 'website', so no admin banner ever appears on the storefront
findings.detail: `useWebBanners` queries `where('placement','==','web')`. The canonical enum is `BANNER_PLACEMENTS = ['app','website']` (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:207), the seed writes 'app'/'website' (scripts/seed.ts:783-788), and the admin writes `placement: placementRef.current` which is only ever 'app' or a value loaded from an existing doc (admin/src/features/banner/routes/BannerFormPage.tsx:41,66,129). Nothing in the repo ever writes the literal 'web', so the query returns an empty set permanently. The Flutter app uses the correct literal ('app', app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:100).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin uploads a hero banner, sets Publish live, saves. The seeded 'website' banner also exists. Load the storefront home page: `banners.length === 0` at web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:48, so the hardcoded gradient fallback hero renders forever and HeroBanner is dead code. No error is shown, so the admin believes the banner is live.
findings.fix: Change web/src/lib/banners.ts:20 to `where('placement','==','website')` (matching BANNER_PLACEMENTS), or better, import the enum constant rather than a string literal.

verdict.reason: Verified; could not refute. web/src/lib/banners.ts:20 queries where('placement','==','web'), but 'web' is not in the domain: packages/shared/src/enums.ts:207 defines BANNER_PLACEMENTS = ['app','website'] and Banner.placement is typed BannerPlacement (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:74). A repo-wide grep for the literal 'web' among banner writers returns exactly one hit — the query itself. Every writer uses enum values: scripts/seed.ts:783-788 loops ['app','website']; admin/src/features/banner/routes/BannerFormPage.tsx:41,66,129 saves placementRef.current, which is only 'app' or a value loaded from an existing doc (no UI control sets anything else). Flutter uses the correct literal at app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:100. No fallback or server-side re-check exists: useCollection runs only this query, and the in-memory step just filters publishLive/imageUrl and sorts. Firestore rules (firebase/firestore.rules:54) allow the read, so nothing else masks it. Consequence is functional, not cosmetic: banners.length is permanently 0 at web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:48, so the ternary always renders the hardcoded hero and web/src/components/home/HeroBanner.tsx is unreachable dead code. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; fix is one token ('web' -> 'website'). Caveat on the reporter's scenario (not on the defect): since the admin form has no placement picker and defaults to 'app', admin-created banners are 'app'-placed, so fixing the literal alone surfaces the seeded 'website' banner (imageUrl is '' in seed) rather than admin-authored ones — a complete fix likely also needs an admin placement control.

findings.title: Customers-page "affiliate" toggle always fails: adminAllocateAffiliate is called without the required commissionRate
findings.detail: `setAffiliateEnabled(uid, true)` invokes the `adminAllocateAffiliate` callable with `await call({ uid })` — no `commissionRate`. The callable's zod schema at functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:19-22 is `z.object({ uid: z.string().min(1), commissionRate: z.number().nonnegative(), walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional() })` and `safeParse` failure throws `HttpsError('invalid-argument', 'Invalid payload.')`. `commissionRate` is NOT optional, so every enable-side call is rejected server-side before touching Firestore. Two admin surfaces use this helper: CustomersListPage.tsx:54 (`onToggleAffiliate`) and CustomerProfilePage.tsx:62. Only the revoke branch (`adminRevokeAffiliate`, schema `{ uid }`) actually works. The only working grant path is AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:55, which passes `commissionRate: Number(rate)`.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Customers → clicks the affiliate toggle on a non-affiliate customer. The callable rejects with invalid-argument; `cfError` renders "Couldn't enable affiliate". The customer is never granted `affiliate.enabled`, no referral code is minted, and no commission can ever accrue for them. Toggling OFF an existing affiliate works, so the control looks half-broken (one-way).
findings.fix: Pass a rate: `await call(enabled ? { uid, commissionRate: DEFAULT_RATE } : { uid })` (or prompt for the rate), or make `commissionRate` optional in the callable schema and default it server-side (e.g. `settings/affiliate.defaultCommissionRate`) when omitted.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed — I could not refute it. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:57-60 sends only `await call({ uid })` for BOTH branches, while /home/h/barkath/functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:19-22 parses the allocate payload with `z.object({ uid: z.string().min(1), commissionRate: z.number().nonnegative(), walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional() })` and throws `HttpsError('invalid-argument','Invalid payload.')` on safeParse failure. `commissionRate` is required (no `.optional()`, no `.default()`), and the handler dereferences it at line 23-24 to compute `rate`, so there is no server-side fallback, no settings-derived default, and no re-check that could rescue the call. The revoke branch schema is `{ uid }` only, so OFF works — the toggle is genuinely one-way.

Reachability verified: both call sites render live controls — CustomersListPage.tsx:130-131 (`onChange={() => void onToggleAffiliate(c)}` on an enabled-unless-pending toggle) and CustomerProfilePage.tsx:141 (`<Toggle ... onChange={() => void onToggleAffiliate()} />`), each computing `enabled = !customer.affiliate?.enabled` so the ON direction is hit whenever a non-affiliate is toggled. The only correct grant path is admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:57-66 (`allocateAffiliate({ uid, commissionRate, walletEnabled })`), which proves the required shape and that the customers.ts helper is the odd one out — not an intentional convention.

Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list (OTP mock, IFSC mock, referral retro-link, App Check) and not an architecture-rule artifact: allocation legitimately belongs in a Cloud Function (cross-user grant + code minting). Not cosmetic — the fix is in the API helper/data layer (pass a commissionRate, e.g. a default rate or one collected before calling), not in markup. Consequence stands: `affiliate.enabled`, `referralCode`, and the balance fields are never written, so no commission can ever accrue for a customer granted from these two surfaces.

findings.title: Auth listener has no error path — a failed admins-doc read locks the whole panel on a permanent spinner
findings.detail: `initAuthListener` does `const admin = await loadAdminDoc(user.uid)` with no try/catch, and `useAuthStore.setState({..., ready: true})` is only reached after that await resolves. `loadAdminDoc` (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:54) does `getDoc(doc(db,'admins',uid))`, and firebase/firestore.rules:190 only permits that read when the caller's token carries `role == 'super_admin'` or `role == 'sub_admin' && uid == adminUid`. Any signed-in Firebase user without an admin role claim therefore gets a `permission-denied` rejection, the async callback rejects unhandled, `ready` stays `false` forever, and RequireAuth (admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx:10) renders the full-screen spinner with no logout affordance. The same unguarded read exists on the login path (auth.ts:39) — it sits OUTSIDE the try/catch that wraps signInWithEmailAndPassword, and unlike the `!snap.exists()` branch at line 41 it never calls `fbSignOut`, so the failed sign-in leaves a live persisted Firebase session behind.
findings.failure_scenario: A Firebase Auth account exists without admin claims — e.g. `createSubAdmin` (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:34-38) succeeds at `auth.createUser` but throws at `setCustomUserClaims`, leaving an orphan account, or someone signs in at /login with any non-admin email/password account. Login shows a generic 'Could not sign in.' toast but the session persists. On the next visit/reload of the admin panel, onAuthStateChanged fires with that user, loadAdminDoc rejects with permission-denied, `ready` is never set, and the panel shows the boot spinner forever on every reload. There is no UI to sign out of that state.
findings.fix: Wrap the listener body in try/catch (and the getDoc in `signInAdmin`): on any error set `{admin: null, ready: true}` and call `signOutAdmin()` so the user lands back on /login instead of an unrecoverable spinner.

verdict.reason: Claim holds. (1) admin/src/features/auth/stores/authStore.ts:33 — `const admin = await loadAdminDoc(user.uid)` runs in an async onAuthStateChanged callback with no try/catch, and the only `ready: true` for the signed-in branch is at lines 35-38, after that await. A rejection kills the callback and onAuthStateChanged will not re-fire for the same user, so `ready` stays false permanently. (2) RequireAuth.tsx:10 renders a bare full-screen spinner while `!ready`, and admin/src/app/router.tsx:54-108 puts `/` plus the `*` catch-all (which redirects to `/`) behind RequireAuth, so the landing page spins forever. (3) The read genuinely can reject: firebase/firestore.rules:188-192 gates admins/{adminUid} on isSuperAdmin() || (role()=='sub_admin' && uid()==adminUid), so a signed-in user without a role claim gets permission-denied, not an empty snapshot — the `!snap.exists()` null fallback never runs. Independently, a reload while offline/flaky makes getDoc reject with 'unavailable' (admin/src/lib/firebase.ts uses the default memory cache, no cached doc on a fresh load), hitting the same lockup for a legitimate admin. (4) Persistence is default browserLocal (nothing overrides it in admin/src/lib/firebase.ts), so the bad session survives reloads. (5) The login-path half is accurate too: auth.ts:39 getDoc is outside the try/catch that ends at line 37, and unlike the not-exists/suspended branches (lines 41, 46) it never calls fbSignOut, so a denied read leaves a live persisted session behind a generic 'Could not sign in.' toast. Reachability: functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:34-38 creates the auth user before setCustomUserClaims with no rollback (orphan account), and web/src/lib/otp/mockOtpService.ts:65-67 shows non-admin email/password accounts exist in the same project. Only partial mitigation: /login is public (router.tsx:55) outside RequireAuth, so manually typing /login and signing in with valid admin creds recovers — nothing surfaces that, and it does not help the transient-error case. No error boundary or global unhandledrejection handler exists anywhere in admin/src. The fix is store logic (try/catch → set ready:true and sign out on failure), not a UI change, and it is not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items.

findings.title: OTP verify calls registerUser on every login; the `users/{phoneKey}` rule forbids updates, so every returning user is stuck on the OTP screen
findings.detail: `_verify()` unconditionally runs `await repo.registerUser(e164)` after a successful verification. `AuthRepository.registerUser` (app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:116) does `_db.doc('users/${digits}').set({...}, SetOptions(merge: true))`. On a doc that already exists, a merge-set is evaluated as an **update** by security rules, and firebase/firestore.rules:185 says `allow update, delete: if false;` (only `create` is allowed, line 184). So the write throws PERMISSION_DENIED, which is caught by the `catch (_)` at otp_screen.dart:106 -> the screen shows "Couldn't verify the code. Please try again." and never navigates. The web deliberately avoids this: web/src/components/auth/authActions.ts:89 calls `registerUser` only `if (mode === 'signup')`.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer registers once (users/919876543210 created). Next day they open the app, enter the same number, enter the correct dev OTP. Firebase sign-in succeeds, ensureCustomerDoc succeeds, then registerUser is denied -> error toast, still on the OTP screen. Tapping "Verify & continue" again now fails with "Incorrect code" because `_pending.remove(e164)` (auth_repository.dart:80) already consumed the code, and each resend repeats the same denial. The only escape is force-quitting the app so Splash restores the (already valid) session.
findings.fix: Only write the directory entry for a first-time registration: check `await repo.userExists(e164)` (or the `snap.exists` result already fetched in ensureCustomerDoc) and skip registerUser for existing numbers, and/or move it out of the navigation try-block so a directory failure can never block sign-in.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all links of the chain. otp_screen.dart:102 calls registerUser unconditionally inside the try whose catch (line 106) suppresses the error and skips the context.go navigation on line 104. auth_repository.dart:113-121 does a merge-set on users/{digits} with no internal catch and a fresh serverTimestamp (so never a no-op write). firestore.rules:181-186 allows only `create` (`allow update, delete: if false`), and a merge-set on an existing doc is evaluated as an update, so every login after the first is PERMISSION_DENIED; there is no blanket write rule at the top of the rules file. The path is reachable for returning users: the app has no signup/signin split — enter_mobile_screen.dart:42-50 sends an OTP and pushes the OTP route for any number, and `userExists` (auth_repository.dart:51) is defined but never called anywhere in app/lib. Sign-out exists (auth_provider.dart:64, invoked from profile_screen.dart:372), and reinstall/second device also hits it. Web deliberately guards this (authActions.ts:89 `if (mode === 'signup') await registerUser(e164)`), confirming the app is missing the guard. The retry trap also holds: verifyOtp removes the pending code (auth_repository.dart:80) before returning true and AuthRepository is a shared provider instance, so re-tapping yields "Incorrect code". Not covered by the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL mock-OTP exemption (that covers SMS delivery, not the users-directory write), and the fix is functional (guard registerUser on first-registration, or move it outside the navigation-blocking try), not UI.

findings.title: Quick-add "+" on the product card drops the variant, producing a cart line the checkout function always rejects as out of stock
findings.detail: `_AddButton.onTap` calls `cart.addProduct(product)` with no `variant:` argument. `CartLine.fromProduct` (app/lib/features/cart/data/cart_line.dart:70-81) then writes `variantId: null` and `pricePaise: p.sellingPaise`. The gating above it (`if (!product.inStock)`, line 284) uses `Product.inStock` (app/lib/features/catalog/data/product.dart:87), which for `hasVariants` products returns true from `variants.any((v) => v.inStock)` — i.e. the button is enabled precisely for variant products whose stock lives on the variants. But `functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:431-443` branches on `l.variantId`: with a null variantId it falls to `if (Number(p.stock ?? 0) < l.qty) throw HttpsError('failed-precondition', `${l.name} is out of stock.`)`. Product-level `stock` is 0 for every variant product — admin writes `stock: 0` on create (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:146), admin inventory adjusts only the `variants[]` entries (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:76-83), and the seed sets `stock: hasVar ? 0 : ...` (scripts/seed.ts:360). The web card does this correctly: `variantId: product.variants?.[0]?.id ?? null` (web/src/components/product/ProductCard.tsx:32).
findings.failure_scenario: Customer opens Home, taps "+" on a perfume that has 50ml/100ml variants (variant stock 10, product-level stock 0). A line `{productId:'p1', variantId:null, pricePaise:<variant-0 price>}` is written into the shared `customers/{uid}.cart` array. The bag shows the item with no size label. At checkout the `placeOrder` callable throws `failed-precondition: "<name> is out of stock."` and the ENTIRE order fails — no combination of retries can clear it, because the customer cannot see or edit the missing variantId. The same product added from the web produces `variantId:'v0'`, so the two clients also create two duplicate lines for the same product.
findings.fix: In `_AddButton.onTap`, resolve a variant before adding: `final v = product.hasVariants ? product.variants.firstWhereOrNull((x) => x.inStock) : null; cart.addProduct(product, variant: v);` — mirroring web ProductCard.tsx:32. Better still, for `hasVariants` products navigate to the details screen so the customer picks the size explicitly.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end. app/lib/core/widgets/product_card.dart:306 calls cart.addProduct(product) with no variant:, while the only other caller (product_details_screen.dart:659) passes variant: _variant defaulting to _firstInStockVariant() — the card is the outlier. CartLine.fromProduct (cart_line.dart:70-81) therefore writes variantId:null and pricePaise:p.sellingPaise. The enabling gate at product_card.dart:284 uses Product.inStock (product.dart:87 = hasVariants ? variants.any(inStock) : stock>0), so it is enabled precisely for variant products. Product-level stock is genuinely dead for variant products: admin saveProduct writes stock:0 only on create (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:146) and the edit `base` object (lines 98-135) never writes stock; buildSkuRows (admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:178-208) emits variantId:null rows ONLY for non-variant products so adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:68-85) never touches base stock on a variant product; seed.ts:360 sets stock: hasVar ? 0 : …. checkout.ts:437 even decrements product-level stock on variant sales, driving it negative. Server side, priceLines (checkout.ts:66-74) skips the variant branch and reports stock=p.stock=0, and checkout.ts:439 throws failed-precondition "<name> is out of stock." No fallback rescues it: the app's own precheck _stockByLine (app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:146-155) mirrors the same null-variant branch, so the bag's _CheckoutBar and the checkout pay bar block the ENTIRE bag (not just the line), and the bag has no variant picker — the only escape is deleting the line. Cross-surface mismatch with web/src/components/product/ProductCard.tsx:32 (variantId: product.variants?.[0]?.id ?? null) is confirmed, producing duplicate lines in the shared customers/{uid}.cart. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic, and fixable in one line.

findings.title: offers.ts reads coupon fields that nothing ever writes (minOrderPaise / maxDiscountPaise / expiresAt), so every promo constraint is ignored on the web
findings.detail: promoDiscount() gates on `c.minOrderPaise` (line 42), caps with `c.maxDiscountPaise` (line 47) and expires on `c.expiresAt`/`c.noExpiry` (lines 40-41). The only writers of the `coupons` collection are admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts (lines 126-135) and scripts/seed.ts (lines 715-725), and both write `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise` and `validUntil`. `minOrderPaise`, `maxDiscountPaise`, `expiresAt`, `noExpiry` and `autoApply` do not exist on any coupon doc, so `Number(undefined ?? 0)` = 0 → the minimum always passes, the percent cap is never applied, and expired coupons never drop out. listAvailableOffers (lines 115-123) has the same bug, so it marks every promo `qualifies: true`. The authoritative server path computeCouponDiscount() (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:143-174) reads the correct names and enforces all three.
findings.failure_scenario: Seeded promo WELCOME30 (flat ₹30, minCartValuePaise ₹150). Customer's cart is ₹100. Checkout auto-applies it (offers.ts sees min 0) and shows −₹30. Pressing "Place order" calls placeOrder with couponCode 'WELCOME30' → computeCouponDiscount throws 'Your cart does not meet this coupon's minimum.' The order can never be placed until the user notices the Remove link. Cap case: admin coupon 15% off, discountMaxCapPaise ₹200, cart ₹5000 → web shows −₹750 / "To pay ₹4250", server caps at ₹200 and charges ₹4800.
findings.fix: Rename the reads in promoDiscount/listAvailableOffers/promoHeadline to the fields the admin actually writes: `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise`, `validFrom`/`validUntil` (and drop `noExpiry`/`autoApply`, or add them to the admin writer). Same rename is needed in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts autoBestOffer(), which has the identical wrong names.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:39-48 and 113-123 read `minOrderPaise`, `maxDiscountPaise`, `expiresAt`, `noExpiry`, `autoApply`. A repo-wide grep shows those names exist ONLY in this file and in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts autoBestOffer() (lines 225-233) — no writer produces them. The only writers of the `coupons` collection, admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-135 and scripts/seed.ts:709-729, write `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise` and `validUntil`. So `Number(undefined ?? 0)` = 0 and the minimum, percent cap and expiry are all unenforced on web; listAvailableOffers marks every promo qualifies:true. No guard rescues it: web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:80-95 auto-applies bestOfferForCart into draft.coupon and placeOrder sends couponCode, which hits computeCouponDiscount (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:143-174) — that path reads the correct names and THROWS 'Your cart does not meet this coupon's minimum', blocking the order rather than silently correcting it; for percent coupons the server caps at discountMaxCapPaise so the charged total differs from the displayed one (a money defect, not cosmetic). Tellingly, computeCouponDiscount carries the comment 'field names must match what the admin writes ... they previously did not, so the minimum, the percent cap and the expiry were all silently unenforced' — the rename fix landed on the authoritative server path only and the web mirror was never updated. Only partial mitigation: the daily couponExpirySweep sets status='expired' and the web query filters status=='active', hiding most expired promos, but the project's own rule says the sweep is best-effort and compute-on-read is required; the min-cart and percent-cap breakages have no mitigation. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list.

findings.title: computeSummary has no free_shipping waiver, so the web total diverges from summarise() for any free-delivery coupon
findings.detail: Server summarise() takes a `waiveDelivery` flag (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:280) and computes `freeDelivery = waiveDelivery || subtotal<=0 || net>=threshold` (line 286); computeCouponDiscount sets it for `discountType === 'free_shipping'` (lines 165, 202) while returning discountPaise 0. Web computeSummary (line 105) only knows the threshold rule and has no waiveDelivery input at all — nor does AppliedCoupon (lines 69-73) carry the flag, and callApplyCoupon (line 183) only returns `{discountPaise, label}`, so the free_shipping signal is dropped end to end. free_shipping coupons exist in both `coupons` (seed.ts:704 'FREESHIP') and personal spin coupons (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:126).
findings.failure_scenario: Delivery settings: standardFeePaise ₹49, freeDeliveryOverPaise ₹999. Cart ₹500. Customer types FREESHIP → applyCoupon returns discountPaise 0, web shows "FREESHIP applied −₹0.00", Delivery ₹49, To pay ₹549. placeOrder waives delivery and charges ₹500 (and the Razorpay modal opens for ₹500, not the ₹549 just shown).
findings.fix: Return the coupon's discountType (or a waiveDelivery boolean) from applyCoupon, store it on AppliedCoupon, and add a `waiveDelivery` term to computeSummary's freeDelivery expression so it mirrors summarise() exactly.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:314 destructures only {discountPaise,label} from computeCouponDiscount, so the waiveDelivery flag set at lines 165/176/202 never crosses the callable boundary; placeOrder at 411-419 DOES pass it into summarise, which zeroes delivery (line 286). Web computeSummary (web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:105) applies only the freeDeliveryOverPaise threshold, AppliedCoupon (69-73) has no waiver field, and callApplyCoupon (183) is typed {discountPaise,label}. The path is not just reachable but deliberately surfaced: web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:86/94 render free_shipping coupons with the headline 'Free delivery' and listAvailableOffers pushes them with discountPaise 0, which checkout/page.tsx:102-105 applyOffer writes into draft.coupon; the typed-code path (page.tsx:151) is identical. Data exists — scripts/seed.ts:704 seeds FREESHIP with discountType 'free_shipping' (active, minCart 150), and functions/src/spin/execute.ts:126 mints personal free_shipping coupons. Result: the customer selects the offer labelled 'Free delivery', the summary still charges standardFeePaise, then placeOrder/createRazorpayOrder bill a lower amount than the one displayed. This is a pricing-logic divergence (the CF header at line 14 explicitly claims 'Pricing mirrors the web computeSummary exactly'), fixable by plumbing the flag through applyCoupon → AppliedCoupon → computeSummary — not a cosmetic change, and not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Same gap also exists in app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:199-202 and in server autoBestOffer, but the claim as filed against web is correct.

findings.title: Checkout clears the idempotency nonce before payment finishes, so any Razorpay failure/cancel + retry places a second order
findings.detail: placeOrder() sets `nonceRef.current = null` immediately after callPlaceOrder resolves (line 180), before createRazorpayOrder / openRazorpayCheckout / verifyPayment. Every failure branch after that point (throw at line 184 → catch at 215, dismissal at 193, unverified at 204) leaves the cart unchanged (`clear()` only runs at line 213) and leaves the CTA enabled. The next click generates a fresh crypto.randomUUID() (line 167), so the server's idempotencyKeys guard (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:370-390) sees a brand-new key and places a whole new order.
findings.failure_scenario: Wallet ₹500, cart ₹1200, Razorpay selected with useWallet on. Order placed → wallet debited ₹500, stock decremented. checkout.razorpay.com fails to load → openRazorpayCheckout throws 'razorpay-script-failed' → toast. User clicks "Place order" again → second order created, wallet debited another ₹500 (or as much as remains), stock decremented twice, two pending orders under My orders.
findings.fix: Only null the nonce on the success path (right before `clear()`), so every retry of the same attempt reuses the same placementNonce and the server returns the already-placed order instead of creating another.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:180 nulls nonceRef right after callPlaceOrder resolves, before createRazorpayOrder/openRazorpayCheckout/verifyPayment. All post-placement exits (dismiss 193-197, unverified 204-208, throw caught at 215 — e.g. 'razorpay-script-failed' thrown by openRazorpayCheckout in web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts) leave the cart intact (clear() only at 213) and re-enable the CTA (setPlacing(false) at 218). The next click mints a fresh crypto.randomUUID() at line 167. Server has no other guard: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:364-390 dedupes only on idempotencyKeys/{uid}__hash(nonce), and the cart-derived fallback signature applies only when placementNonce is absent (`parsed.data.placementNonce ?? 'auto:...'`), which the web client never omits. So a second full transaction runs: new order doc, stock decrement (428-442), wallet debit (446-449), coupon consumed, counter bumped. No pending-order resume path exists on web, and idempotencyKeys is CF-only per firestore.rules:232. The intended behaviour is documented by the Flutter sibling app/lib/features/checkout/payment_screen.dart:30,43-44, which keeps a stable per-screen _nonce so "re-pressing Pay resumes the same order" — web diverges. Fix is functional and one line: move the nonce clear next to clear() at 213 (a replayed placeOrder returns the same orderId, so the razorpay leg resumes correctly). Only overstatement in the claim: the retry re-reads the wallet inside the transaction, so it debits only the remaining balance rather than another full Rs 500 — the duplicate order and double stock decrement are real.

findings.title: Web return window is admin-configurable but the Cloud Function hardcodes 3 days, so in-window requests are rejected
findings.detail: `returnWindow()` computes eligibility from `settings/returns.windowDays` (default `DEFAULT_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7`, line 246) measured from `order.deliveredAt ?? order.placedAt` (line 263). The server, `functions/src/returns/requests.ts:42-46`, ignores `settings/returns` entirely: `const RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` and additionally hard-requires `o.deliveredAt` (`if (!deliveredAtMs || Date.now() - deliveredAtMs > RETURN_WINDOW_MS) throw ...`). scripts/seed.ts:208 seeds `windowDays: 7` and admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:279 defaults the field to 7, so the shipped configuration is guaranteed to disagree with the server. The Flutter app (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:202 `returnWindowDays = 3`) matches the CF; only web is the outlier.
findings.failure_scenario: Order delivered 5 days ago, `settings/returns.windowDays = 7` (the seeded/default value). The order detail page renders an enabled "Return item · 2 days left" button, the return page renders the full form, the customer picks a reason and submits -> requestReturnOrReplacement throws `failed-precondition: The 3-day return window for this order has closed.` -> the UI shows the generic "We couldn't submit your return just now. Please try again." and the customer retries indefinitely. Same failure for any delivered order whose `deliveredAt` is absent (legacy orders), where web falls back to `placedAt` and the CF hard-fails.
findings.fix: Make the CF read `settings/returns.windowDays` (falling back to 7) instead of the hardcoded `RETURN_WINDOW_MS`, and apply the same `deliveredAt ?? placedAt` fallback the web/app clients use — or, if 3 days is authoritative, drop the settings-driven `returnWindow()` on web and read the same constant.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; I could not refute it. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/returns/requests.ts:42-46 hardcodes `const RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` and rejects with `failed-precondition` — it never reads `settings/returns`. A repo-wide grep for `windowDays` shows the setting is read only by web (`web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:49 useReturnSettings` -> `settings/returns`) and written only by admin (`admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:279-296`, default 7); no Cloud Function reads it, so there is no server-side fallback or re-check that reconciles the two. `web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261-269 returnWindow()` uses `windowDays ?? 7`, and both the order detail page (`web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71,242` renders an enabled "Return item · N days left" link) and the return page (`.../return/page.tsx:26,45` renders the full form) gate on it, then `requestReturn()` (orders.ts:313) swallows the CF error and returns false, so a submission of a 4-7 day old delivered order fails with no actionable message. Seeds confirm the shipped config disagrees: scripts/seed.ts:208 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117 both set `windowDays: 7`. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic (the user cannot complete a return the storefront says is open), and the fix is server-side (read settings/returns.windowDays in the CF, and fall back to placedAt like web does for legacy orders lacking deliveredAt — functions/src/orders/status.ts:75 only started stamping deliveredAt at the delivered transition). The app (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:201-212, returnWindowDays = 3) does match the CF, so web+admin vs. server is the genuine mismatch.

findings.title: autoBestOffer reads promotional-coupon field names that nothing ever writes, so minimum-cart, percent cap and expiry are all silently unenforced on auto-applied coupons
findings.detail: `autoBestOffer` (checkout.ts:215-259) evaluates docs from the top-level `coupons` collection using `c.minOrderPaise` (line 228), `c.maxDiscountPaise` (line 233), `c.expiresAt` (line 226), `c.noExpiry` (line 227) and `c.autoApply` (line 225). The only writer of that collection is `admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-152` (`saveCoupon`), which writes `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise`, `validUntil`, `active`, `status`, `maxUsesTotal`, `maxUsesPerUser`, `firstOrderOnly` — and never writes `minOrderPaise`, `maxDiscountPaise`, `expiresAt`, `noExpiry` or `autoApply`. Every one of those reads therefore resolves to `undefined` and the guard collapses to `Number(undefined ?? 0) === 0`. The sibling function in the same file, `computeCouponDiscount` (lines 143, 173, 140), reads the correct names, so the two code paths for the same collection disagree. `autoBestOffer` additionally never checks `maxUsesTotal`, `maxUsesPerUser`, `firstOrderOnly` or `usesCount` at all, yet placeOrder still increments the redemption counters at lines 604-614 — so the counters climb while the limits never bind.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates coupon MEGA20 = 20% off, `discountMaxCapPaise` = 20000 (₹200 cap), `minCartValuePaise` = 500000 (₹5,000 minimum), `maxUsesPerUser` = 1, `targetUsers` = 'all'. A customer checks out with a ₹50,000 cart and enters NO coupon code. placeOrder (line 349) falls through to `autoBestOffer`, which reads `minOrderPaise` → undefined → 0 (minimum skipped) and `maxDiscountPaise` → undefined → 0 → `cap > 0` false → cap skipped. Discount = ₹10,000 instead of the intended ₹200. The same customer repeats it on every subsequent order because the per-user limit is never consulted on this path. A ₹100 cart likewise auto-receives a coupon whose ₹5,000 minimum it does not meet.
findings.fix: In `autoBestOffer`, read the same field names `computeCouponDiscount` uses: `minCartValuePaise`, `discountMaxCapPaise`, `validUntil` (with `validFrom`), and drop `noExpiry`/`autoApply`/`minOrderPaise`/`maxDiscountPaise`. Better: have `autoBestOffer` build its candidate list by delegating each candidate to the same validation helper as `computeCouponDiscount` (catching the HttpsError to mean 'does not qualify'), so the two paths cannot drift again, and include the `maxUsesTotal` / `maxUsesPerUser` / `firstOrderOnly` checks.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. The canonical Coupon schema (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:19-42) uses minCartValuePaise / discountMaxCapPaise / validUntil; the only writers of the top-level `coupons` collection — admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts saveCoupon+setCouponActive and scripts/seed.ts:707-733 — write exactly those names and never write minOrderPaise, maxDiscountPaise, expiresAt, noExpiry or autoApply. A repo-wide grep for those five names returns only readers: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:225-233 and the web display mirror web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:39-47. So in autoBestOffer the minimum collapses to Number(undefined ?? 0)===0, the percent cap to cap>0 === false, and the expiry check never fires, while the candidate query where('status','==','active') does match real admin coupons. The path is reachable: placeOrder line 349 calls autoBestOffer whenever couponCode is null, and both clients send null when no offer is selected (web checkout page.tsx:176 `draft.coupon?.code ?? null`, app checkout_screen.dart:108 / payment_screen.dart:85). Nothing re-validates afterwards — summarise() only clamps discount to subtotal — yet lines 604-614 still increment coupons/{id}.usesCount and customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{id} for the auto-applied coupon whose maxUsesTotal/maxUsesPerUser/firstOrderOnly were never checked. The sibling computeCouponDiscount even carries a comment at lines 132-134 saying this exact field-name mismatch was already fixed there ("the minimum, the percent cap and the expiry were all silently unenforced") — autoBestOffer was missed. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic, and squarely money-affecting server-side logic.

findings.title: Any signed-in customer can read every other customer's invoice, and invoice filenames are sequential
findings.detail: `match /invoices/{fileName} { allow read: if request.auth != null; ... }` grants read on the whole invoices prefix to every authenticated user, with no ownership check. The object name is fully predictable: functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:54 writes ``const path = `invoices/${o.shortId ?? parsed.data.orderId}.html`;`` and shortId is a monotonically increasing counter value — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:422-425 reads `counters/orders` and builds ``const shortId = `#BRK-${seq}`;``. The rendered HTML (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:43+) contains the buyer's name, full delivery address, phone, line items and totals. Clients never actually need this rule: the CF hands back a tokenised `https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/...?alt=media&token=...` download URL (invoice.ts:61) which bypasses rules entirely, so the permissive read grant buys nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer A signs in (any real account) and calls `getDownloadURL(ref(storage, 'invoices/#BRK-1041.html'))`, then 1042, 1043 … Because shortIds are sequential and the rule only checks `request.auth != null`, A downloads every other customer's invoice — name, phone, home address, and purchase history for the entire store.
findings.fix: Deny direct client reads on `invoices/**` (`allow read: if false`) and keep serving the tokenised download URL the CF already returns; or, if direct reads are wanted, store invoices under `invoices/{uid}/{orderId}.html` and gate on `request.auth.uid == uid`.

verdict.reason: Real, exploitable defect. firebase/storage.rules:20 grants read on the entire invoices/ prefix to any authenticated user (`allow read: if request.auth != null`), despite the comment above it stating "owner or admin read" — the intended check is simply missing (compare exports/adminAvatars on lines 17/30 which do call isAdmin()). Object names are fully enumerable: functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:54 writes `invoices/${o.shortId ?? orderId}.html` and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:422-425 derives shortId from the monotonic `counters/orders` seq (`#BRK-${seq}`, base 48000) — no random component. The HTML body (invoice.ts:44) contains customerName, full deliveryAddress (line1/line2/city/pincode), customerPhone, line items and totals, so any signed-in customer can walk #BRK-N and harvest the store's entire customer PII + purchase history. No fallback or server-side re-check exists: Storage rules are the only gate for direct SDK reads. The grant is also unnecessary — adminGenerateInvoice is admin-only (admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:143) and both clients render the stored tokenised firebasestorage.googleapis.com URL (web .../invoice/page.tsx:108, app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:246), which bypasses rules; a grep for getDownloadURL/ref(storage,...) across web/src, admin/src and app/lib shows no client ever builds an `invoices/` reference (the unused packages/shared/src/collections.ts:84 helper even emits a mismatched `.pdf` name). firebase.json:6-7 confirms this rules file is deployed. Fix is a one-line rule change to `allow read: if isAdmin();`. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic, not an architecture-rule tradeoff.

findings.title: Server auto-apply reads promo-coupon fields the admin never writes (minOrderPaise/expiresAt/maxDiscountPaise)
findings.detail: `autoBestOffer()` (lines 221-238) — the path `placeOrder` takes whenever the client sends no explicit `couponCode` — reads promotional `coupons` docs using `c.minOrderPaise`, `c.expiresAt`, `c.maxDiscountPaise` and `c.discountValue`. The only writer of that collection, `admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts` `saveCoupon()`, writes `minCartValuePaise`, `validUntil`, `discountMaxCapPaise`, `discountValuePaise`/`discountPercent`. Every guard therefore reads `undefined`: `minOrderPaise ?? 0` → the minimum-cart rule is skipped, `expiresAt` is never set → the expiry check is skipped (`validUntil` is what the sweep in functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts:37 uses, and that sweep only runs daily so `status` is stale for up to 24h), and `maxDiscountPaise ?? 0` → the percent cap is never applied. The explicit-code path (`computeCouponDiscount`, lines 143/140/172) uses the correct names, so only the auto-apply path is wrong. `autoBestOffer` also never checks `maxUsesPerUser`/`maxUsesTotal`/`firstOrderOnly` even though placeOrder still increments the counters at lines 604-613.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates SAVE50: 50% off, discountMaxCapPaise = ₹200, minCartValuePaise = ₹5,000, validUntil = yesterday (status still 'active' because the daily sweep hasn't run). A customer checks out a ₹1,000 cart with no coupon entered. autoBestOffer sees minOrderPaise=undefined→0 (min ignored), expiresAt=undefined (expiry ignored), maxDiscountPaise=undefined→0 (cap ignored) and applies ₹500 off. The order is placed at ₹500 instead of ₹1,000 and coupons/{id}.usesCount is incremented for an expired, unqualified coupon.
findings.fix: In `autoBestOffer` read the same field names `computeCouponDiscount` uses: `minCartValuePaise`, `validUntil` (null = no expiry), `discountMaxCapPaise`, `discountValuePaise`. Also run the same `maxUsesTotal`/`maxUsesPerUser`/`firstOrderOnly` guards before auto-applying, or factor both paths through one shared validator.

verdict.reason: Real, reachable money defect. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:226-233 (autoBestOffer) reads c.expiresAt, c.minOrderPaise, c.maxDiscountPaise and c.discountValue from promotional `coupons` docs. The only writers of that collection — admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts saveCoupon() (lines 120-151) and scripts/seed.ts:707 — write validUntil, minCartValuePaise, discountMaxCapPaise, discountValuePaise/discountPercent, matching the authoritative Coupon type in packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts. A repo-wide grep finds no writer of minOrderPaise/maxDiscountPaise/expiresAt/discountValue/autoApply/noExpiry on that collection at all, so `minOrderPaise ?? 0` skips the minimum-cart rule and `maxDiscountPaise ?? 0` skips the percent cap entirely — neither is mitigated anywhere. The path is reachable: placeOrder calls autoBestOffer whenever couponCode is null (checkout.ts:347-349), and both clients send `draft.coupon?.code ?? null` (web checkout/page.tsx:178, app checkout_screen.dart:108) with web auto-apply firing only once (autoTried ref), so a removed/absent offer hits the server path. The `status == 'active'` filter plus the daily couponExpirySweep (sweeps.ts:36, which keys off validUntil, not expiresAt) only bounds the expiry half of the bug to a <=24h staleness window; it does nothing for the ignored minimum or the ignored cap. Nothing downstream re-validates — summarise() takes the discount as given, and lines 604-613 increment coupons/{id}.usesCount and customers/{uid}/couponUsage even though autoBestOffer never checks maxUsesTotal/maxUsesPerUser/firstOrderOnly. The comment at lines 132-134 shows this identical field-name bug was already fixed in computeCouponDiscount and missed in autoBestOffer. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and not cosmetic. (The client mirror web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts has the same wrong names, but the server fix is the functional one.)

findings.title: publishedAt is never stamped when a product goes draft → published, so "New arrivals" is broken for the create-draft-then-publish workflow
findings.detail: Both storefronts derive New Arrivals from publishedAt: web/src/lib/catalog.ts:43-56 (`liveAtMillis` = publishedAt ?? createdAt, window = 3 days) and app/lib/features/catalog/data/product.dart:120-124 (same fallback). The only writes to publishedAt in the whole repo are products.ts:160 (`serverTimestamp()` at create, regardless of the chosen status), products.ts:209 (duplicate → null) and products.ts:294 (CSV import → null). `grep -rn publishedAt admin/src functions/src` shows no other writer. The edit path (`updateDoc(doc(db,'products',values.id), base)` at line 165) writes `base`, which contains `status` but no `publishedAt`, and `setProductArchived` (line 52) flips status to 'published' without touching it either. So flipping status from draft to published never moves publishedAt.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates a product on 1 Jul with Status = Draft (publishedAt = 1 Jul). Photos and copy are finished on 20 Jul and the admin sets Status = Published and saves. publishedAt stays 1 Jul, so `isNewArrival` is false immediately and the product never appears in the web home "New arrivals" rail or the app's newArrivals list. Same for CSV-imported products (publishedAt null → falls back to the import-day createdAt).
findings.fix: In `saveProduct`, when `!isNew` and the status is transitioning to 'published' while the stored doc's publishedAt is null or the stored status was not 'published', include `publishedAt: serverTimestamp()` in the update (the form already holds `existingRef.current`). Do the same in `setProductArchived` when restoring to 'published'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts the update branch (line 165) writes `base`, which includes `status` but never `publishedAt`; `setProductArchived` (lines 52-57) likewise flips status to 'published' without stamping it. The only publishedAt writers are create (line 160, serverTimestamp regardless of chosen status), duplicate (line 209, null) and CSV import (line 294, null). There is no server-side fixup: functions/src contains no Firestore document triggers at all (no onDocumentWritten/onDocumentUpdated; 'onProductWrite' appears only in a comment at functions/src/index.ts:8). Both storefronts derive the rail solely from publishedAt with a createdAt fallback — web/src/lib/catalog.ts:43-63 (liveAtMillis = publishedAt ?? createdAt, NEW_ARRIVAL_DAYS=3) and app/lib/features/catalog/data/product.dart:120-142 with catalog_repository.dart:190-193 — and neither reads the separate `newArrivals` collection (zero hits in web/src and app/lib). The path is reachable: ProductFormPage.tsx:92 seeds status from the existing doc and :350-356 exposes a Published/Draft/Archived select, so a draft-created product edited to Published days later keeps its creation-day publishedAt and never enters the 3-day window; CSV/duplicate products (publishedAt null) fall back to their import/copy createdAt. Rules allow the write (firestore.rules:51 canWrite('products')), so stamping publishedAt on the draft/archived→published transition is a straightforward client-side fix. Not cosmetic, not on the known-intentional list, and the file's own comment (lines 119-122, "New arrivals is automatic — derived from the publish date") states the intent the code fails to honour.

findings.title: Removing a sub-category chip in the category form skips the in-use guard that the sub-categories screen enforces, stranding products
findings.detail: SubCategoriesPage.tsx:60-67 guards deletion: `askDelete` calls `countSubCategoryProducts(category.id, s.id)` and refuses when any product is attached ("Deleting a sub-category strands its products outside every storefront query"). CategoryFormPage performs the exact same mutation on the same embedded `subCategories` array — line 266 `setSubs((arr) => arr.filter((x) => x.id !== s.id))` — with no count check at all, and `onSave` (line 139) writes the whole array through `saveCategory` → `updateDoc`. Products keep their `subCategoryId`/`subCategorySlug`, but the sub no longer exists on the category doc.
findings.failure_scenario: Category "perfumes" has sub "attar" with 12 published products. Admin opens Edit category to change the tint, clicks the × on the "attar" chip (a stale chip they think is a typo), and saves. The 12 products are untouched but 'attar' is gone from `categories/perfumes.subCategories`, so: web ListingView's sub-category facet (ListingView.tsx:58-80) no longer lists it, the admin Product form's Sub-category dropdown (ProductFormPage.tsx:333) can no longer select it — so re-saving any of those 12 products fails required-field validation — and the app's `productsInCategory(subCategorySlug: 'attar')` path is unreachable from the UI.
findings.fix: Make the chip's × call the same `countSubCategoryProducts(id, s.id)` guard used in SubCategoriesPage.askDelete (await it, toast and abort when > 0), or drop sub-category editing from the category form entirely and route it to the guarded screen.

verdict.reason: Tried to refute and could not. Verified end to end: (1) Reachability — admin/src/app/router.tsx:70 maps `/categories/:id` to CategoryFormPage, so the Edit form with removable sub-category chips is live. (2) The chips are seeded from the stored doc, not just newly typed subs — CategoryFormPage.tsx:40 `useState(seed?.subCategories ?? [])` and :66 `setSubs(c.subCategories ?? [])`; every existing sub gets an × wired to `setSubs((arr) => arr.filter((x) => x.id !== s.id))` with zero checks. (3) onSave passes `subCategories: subs` into saveCategory, which does a plain `updateDoc(doc(db,'categories',values.id), base)` with `base.subCategories = values.subCategories` — full array replacement, persisted. (4) The guard genuinely exists on the sibling surface and is documented as a data rule: SubCategoriesPage.tsx:58-67 `askDelete` calls `countSubCategoryProducts(category.id, s.id)` and refuses ("reassign them first"), with the comment "Deleting a sub-category strands its products outside every storefront query". Same mutation, same doc, one guarded and one not. (5) No fallback or server-side re-check: `countSubCategoryProducts` is referenced only by SubCategoriesPage; firebase/firestore.rules:50 is `allow write: if canWrite('categories')` with no payload validation; no Cloud Function touches category writes. (6) Downstream impact is real — web/src/components/catalog/ListingView.tsx (~51-60) builds the sub-category facet solely from `category.subCategories`, and admin ProductFormPage.tsx:333 builds the required Sub-category Select from `category?.subCategories ?? []`, so affected products render with an unmatched option. Not a KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not cosmetic (it persists to Firestore), and consistent with the architecture rules (direct write is correct; the missing piece is the client-side guard). One minor overstatement in the report: ProductFormPage validation checks `!subCategoryId` (line 169) and the value is still loaded from the product (line 120), so re-save would not hard-fail validation — the Select just shows no matching option. Core defect stands; fix is to run the same `countSubCategoryProducts` guard on chip removal or diff removed subs in onSave.

findings.title: Save handler throws an uncaught TypeError (dead Save button) when a bumped SKU disappears from the live product snapshot
findings.detail: `deltas` is keyed by `SkuRow.key` (`${p.id}` or `${p.id}_${v.id}`, api/inventory.ts:183/198) and is never reconciled against `rows`, which is recomputed from the live `useInventoryProducts()` subscription on every snapshot. Line 62 does `const r = rowByKey.get(key)!;` with a non-null assertion, and the whole `payload` build (lines 58-64) sits OUTSIDE the `try` block that starts on line 65. If a key in `deltas` no longer has a row, `r` is `undefined` and `r.productId` throws. Nothing catches it: the `catch` on line 75 is never reached, no toast fires, `setSaving` was never called, and `changedCount` (line 46) still counts the stale key so the button keeps showing e.g. "Save adjustments (1)".
findings.failure_scenario: Admin A opens /inventory/adjust and clicks + on variant SKU `p9_v2`. Admin B (or the same admin in another tab) deletes product p9, or edits p9 to drop variant v2, or flips a simple product to hasVariants (which changes its key from `p9` to `p9_v1`). The live listener pushes the new snapshot, the row vanishes from the table, but `deltas['p9_v2']` remains. Admin A clicks Save -> TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'productId'). No error toast, no navigation, no adjustment saved, and every subsequent click on Save does the same nothing.
findings.fix: Build the payload inside the try block and skip/report unknown keys: `const r = rowByKey.get(key); if (!r) return null;` then filter nulls (and prune `deltas` of keys missing from `rows` in an effect, warning the admin that a SKU changed).

verdict.reason:
The claim holds up on inspection. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/inventory/routes/AdjustStockPage.tsx:58-64 builds the payload with `const r = rowByKey.get(key)!;` — a bare non-null assertion, no guard, no filter — and that whole block sits above the `try {` on line 65, so the `catch` on line 75 and the `finally { setSaving(false) }` cannot run. `deltas` (line 31) is plain component state keyed by `SkuRow.key` and is never reconciled when `rows` changes; `rows` is recomputed on every snapshot from `useInventoryProducts()` (inventory.ts:171-175), which is a genuine live `onSnapshot` subscription (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:110-123, snapshot replaced wholesale on each update, and on listener error the previous data is retained so `rows` never transiently empties for a benign reason).

I looked for the usual escape hatches and found none:
- No reconciliation effect, no `useEffect` pruning `deltas`, no `rows`-derived filter before the `.map`. `changedCount` (line 46) counts `deltas` only, so the button label keeps showing the stale count and stays clickable.
- The trigger is reachable, not hypothetical: hard delete is wired to the UI — `deleteProduct` (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:44-45, `deleteDoc(doc(db,'products',id))`) is called from ProductsListPage.tsx:129. The variant-key cases are also reachable, since a key is `${p.id}_${v.id}` when `hasVariants && variants.length` else `p.id` (inventory.ts:183/198), so dropping a variant or toggling `hasVariants` in the product editor re-keys or removes the row while a delta is outstanding.
- No server-side rescue: the throw happens before `adjustStock()` is ever called, so the `adminAdjustStock` callable never sees the request.

This is not cosmetic — the Save handler dies with an uncaught TypeError, no toast fires, nothing is saved, and every later click repeats it, leaving the admin with a permanently dead Save button until a reload. It is a small, contained fix (drop or skip keys with no matching row, or move the payload build inside the try). The only reservation is likelihood: it needs a concurrent catalog mutation while the adjust page is open with a pending delta, so it is a narrow race rather than a routine path.

findings.title: Stock is committed by the callable before the ledger batch, so a ledger failure reports total failure and the retry double-applies the stock delta
findings.detail: `adjustStock` first awaits the `adminAdjustStock` callable (line 84), which transactionally commits the stock change, and only then builds and commits the client-side `stockAdjustments` batch (line 115). There is no compensation. Any rejection after line 88 - `batch.commit()` failing on a network blip/offline/rules denial, or the callable itself rejecting *after* the transaction because `writeAudit` on functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:90 throws - propagates to AdjustStockPage.tsx:75, which shows the generic `toast.error('Could not save adjustments.')`, keeps the page mounted and keeps `deltas` fully populated. The callable is a relative `+delta` mutation with no idempotency key, so pressing Save again applies the delta a second time.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sets +50 on SKU BRK-77 (stock 10) and clicks Save. The transaction commits stock 10 -> 60, then `batch.commit()` rejects (Wi-Fi drops for two seconds, or writeAudit throws). Toast says "Could not save adjustments." The +50 stepper is still on screen, so the admin clicks Save again. Stock is now 110, and only one ledger row (before 60, after 110) exists. Real stock is inflated by 50 with no record of why.
findings.fix: Either move the stockAdjustments ledger writes into the same Cloud Function transaction (the CF already computes before/after), or send a client-generated idempotency key with the callable so a retry is a no-op; at minimum clear `deltas` / block the retry and surface "stock was adjusted but history could not be written" instead of a blanket failure.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and found no guard, fallback, or second writer. adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:54-88) is a purely relative +delta transaction with no idempotency key in its zod schema and no de-dup record, and writeAudit runs AFTER the transaction commits (line 90) — so a throw there (or a lost/timed-out callable response) rejects the call with the stock already changed. admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:115 then commits the stockAdjustments ledger as a separate client batch with no compensation; grep confirms stockAdjustments is written from nowhere else, so a failure there leaves stock moved with zero history. AdjustStockPage.tsx:75-79 catches, shows a generic toast, and neither clears `deltas` nor navigates (navigate is success-only, line 74), so re-clicking Save re-sends the identical relative payload and double-applies. Firestore rules (firestore.rules:213-217) permit the ledger create (adminUid == auth uid), so this is not a permanently-broken path — it is a rare-but-real at-least-once window. Two caveats that weaken but do not kill the claim: the reporter's "Wi-Fi blip makes batch.commit() reject" trigger is wrong (the Web SDK queues writes offline and resolves on reconnect rather than rejecting), and the code comment at lines 59-71 shows the client-side ledger is a deliberate choice. But the deliberate choice was about round trips, not about retry safety, and the non-idempotent relative mutation plus retained deltas is a genuine, fixable data-integrity defect (fix: write the ledger inside/adjacent to the CF transaction, or send a client-generated request id the callable can de-dup on).

findings.title: adminAdjustStock silently skips SKUs it cannot resolve, and the client's no-results fallback then writes a fabricated history row and toasts success
findings.detail: Inside the transaction, a missing product doc is skipped with `if (!snap.exists) return;` (line 60) and a variant id not present in `p.variants` is skipped by `if (!d) return v;` (line 78). In both cases nothing is pushed to `results`, yet the function still returns `{ ok: true, count: adjustments.length }` (line 98) - `count` is the number of SKUs *requested*, not applied, so the caller cannot detect the skip from it either. On the client, api/inventory.ts:102-110 treats a missing entry in `moved` as "an older callable build is still deployed" and falls back to `known`/`Math.max(0, known + a.delta)` computed from the stale local `products` array, writing a stockAdjustments row that asserts a stock change which never occurred. AdjustStockPage.tsx:73 then toasts "Stock adjusted for N SKUs" and navigates away. The legacy-build fallback and the real-skip case are indistinguishable, so a genuine no-op is never reported.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Adjust stock, sets +10 on product p12. Before the save round-trip lands, p12 is deleted (or its variant v3 is removed by a concurrent product edit). The transaction hits `!snap.exists` / `!d` and does nothing; `results` is empty. The client writes stockAdjustments {productId:'p12', before:4, delta:10, after:14} and shows "Stock adjusted for 1 SKU". Inventory is unchanged, and the Stock history modal now shows a change that never happened.
findings.fix: Have the CF report skips explicitly (e.g. return `skipped: [{productId, variantId, reason}]` and/or throw `not-found` when nothing was applied), and on the client only emit a ledger row for SKUs present in `results`; surface any skipped SKU to the admin instead of falling back to locally-cached stock.

verdict.reason: The code reads exactly as claimed and I could not find a guard, re-check, or other surface that covers it. functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:60 (`if (!snap.exists) return;`) and :79 (`if (!d) return v;`) skip SKUs without recording anything, while :98 returns `count: adjustments.length` (requested, not applied) and writeAudit at :95 logs the same requested count — so neither the return value nor the audit log can distinguish applied from skipped. On the client, admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:102-110 branches per-entry (`const r = moved.get(key)`, then `r ? r.before : known` / `r ? r.after : Math.max(0, known + a.delta)`), so the shim documented at :99-100 as a legacy-build compatibility path also swallows a genuine per-SKU skip from the current build and persists a stockAdjustments doc asserting a stock change that never occurred; AdjustStockPage.tsx:73 then toasts success. Key construction matches on both sides (`${productId}|${variantId ?? ''}`, server pushes variantId:null for the base row), so there is no benign key-mismatch explanation — the fallback fires only on a real skip. Not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, and no architecture rule sanctions it. Two things lower severity from the reported scenario: useInventoryProducts is a live onSnapshot subscription (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:96-120) so a deleted product usually vanishes from `rows` first, and AdjustStockPage.tsx:62's `rowByKey.get(key)!` non-null assertion would throw before the callable is invoked; the fabricated-row path therefore needs the delete/variant-removal to land while the callable is in flight. It is still reachable (products are hard-deleted in admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:44, multi-admin panel), the bad data is persisted to Firestore rather than merely displayed (so not cosmetic), and the fix is small — skip the ledger row when `moved` has no entry, or return an applied/skipped list from the callable.

findings.title: Commission confirmation on 'delivered' runs outside the status transaction and can never be retried
findings.detail: The status transition commits in db.runTransaction (lines 63-95). Only afterwards, on a separate round trip, does line 99 call confirmCommissionsForOrder(orderId) and line 100 stamp affiliateCommissionStatus. confirmCommissionsForOrder itself opens a second transaction (commissions.ts:112) that can fail with ABORTED/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. If it throws, the callable rejects — but the order is already status 'delivered' and TRANSITIONS.delivered === [] (line 20), so a retry of adminChangeOrderStatus throws 'Cannot move delivered -> delivered'. There is no scheduled reconciliation either: functions/src/index.ts exports only couponExpirySweep, and sweeps.ts has no commission logic. The audit log at line 103 is also skipped on that path, so the transition leaves no trace. Secondary issue on line 100: the affiliateCommissionStatus write is fired for every delivered order, including ones with no referrer (checkout.ts:518 initialises it to null), and its error is swallowed by .catch(() => undefined).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin marks order #BRK-48219 delivered. The status transaction commits; the follow-up commission transaction hits contention on customers/{affiliateUid} (that doc is also written by every other order of that affiliate) and fails after retries. The admin sees "Couldn't update the status" and clicks Delivered again -> failed-precondition. The commission row stays 'pending' forever, the affiliate's pendingBalancePaise is permanently inflated and the money is never withdrawable, with no admin UI or job able to fix it.
findings.fix: Move the commission clearance into the same transaction as the status write (read the commission rows and affiliate docs before any write), or make the transition idempotent — allow 'delivered' -> 'delivered' as a no-op re-entry that re-runs confirmCommissionsForOrder — and only stamp affiliateCommissionStatus when the order actually carries a commission.

verdict.reason: Verified as a real, unrecoverable money defect. functions/src/orders/status.ts commits the status change in db.runTransaction (63-95), then calls confirmCommissionsForOrder(orderId) at line 99 on a separate round trip, which opens its own transaction (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:112). Because TRANSITIONS.delivered === [] (status.ts:20), a throw at line 99 leaves the order at 'delivered' with no way to re-trigger: retrying the callable hits 'Cannot move delivered -> delivered', and the admin UI (admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:88) exposes no other lever. Grep confirms confirmCommissionsForOrder has exactly one caller repo-wide, functions/src/index.ts exports only couponExpirySweep, and functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts is coupon-only, so no reconciliation job exists. No other surface repairs it either: returns/decisions.ts and affiliate/withdrawals.ts have zero commission logic, and cancel.ts only reverses still-pending rows and is unreachable from 'delivered'. Net effect: the commission row stays 'pending' forever, affiliate.pendingBalancePaise stays inflated and the money never reaches confirmedBalancePaise (the withdrawable balance per the architecture rules); the writeAudit at line 103 is also skipped on that path. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not cosmetic/UI, and cheaply fixable since confirmCommissionsForOrder is already idempotent (commissions.ts:124 re-checks status === 'pending'), so it can be folded into the status transaction or made re-runnable for an already-delivered order.
