Confidence is medium only because the trigger requires a transient transaction failure (Firestore already retries internally); the secondary point about affiliateCommissionStatus being stamped 'confirmed' on referrer-less orders is accurate but low-impact, since packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:82 is the only reference and no client reads the field.

findings.title: Invoice button is permanently dead for an orders-only sub-admin: adminGenerateInvoice is gated on payments.view, not orders
findings.detail: Every other action on the Order detail screen requires the orders module: adminChangeOrderStatus (status.ts:31) and adminAssignRider (shipment.ts:22) both call requireModule(req, 'orders', 'edit'). adminGenerateInvoice instead calls requireModule(req, 'payments', 'view'). 'orders' and 'payments' are separate keys in MODULE_KEYS (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:258-259), and the admin UI gates the Orders screen on the orders module only (Sidebar.tsx:12 checks modulePermissions[item.module].view). The mismatch cuts both ways: it is also a 'view' permission authorising two writes — ref.update on the CF-only-write orders collection (invoice.ts:62) and a publicly tokened Storage object (line 57).
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin is created with orders {view,edit} and no payments permission — the normal fulfilment operator. They open /orders/{id}, click Invoice, and get 'Missing payments.view permission.' every time, with no other way to produce an invoice for the customer. Conversely a read-only analyst with payments.view (and nothing else) can call adminGenerateInvoice directly and mutate invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt on any order plus publish its customer name, phone and address to a public Storage URL.
findings.fix: Change line 19 to requireModule(req, 'orders', 'edit') (or accept either orders.edit or payments.edit), matching the module the screen is gated on and the write the function performs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:19 guards adminGenerateInvoice with requireModule(req,'payments','view'), while the two sibling actions on the same Order detail screen use requireModule(req,'orders','edit') (status.ts:31, shipment.ts:22). requireModule (guards.ts:42-57) has no fallback path — non-super_admins without payments.view always get 'Missing payments.view permission.' 'orders' and 'payments' are independent MODULE_KEYS and the sub-admin form toggles them separately, so an orders-only fulfilment operator is a normal configuration; the admin UI renders the Invoice button unconditionally (OrderDetailPage.tsx:176 — only the sidebar gates, and it gates on orders.view), so the button is reachable and permanently dead for that role. adminGenerateInvoice is the only producer of invoiceUrl (checkout.ts:522 seeds it null; web and app only read it), so there is no other way to produce an invoice. Additionally, invoice.ts:19 is the ONLY requireModule call in the entire functions codebase using the 'view' action — every other privileged callable uses edit/create/approve — and it authorises two writes (public-tokened Storage object at line 57, ref.update on orders at line 62), so a payments.view-only analyst can mutate any order and publish customer name/phone/address. The seeded ops sub-admin happens to have both orders and payments, which masks the bug in seed data but does not fix it. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item; fix is a one-line server-side guard change, not a UI change.

findings.title: adminAllocateAffiliate / adminRevokeAffiliate rewrite the whole affiliate map outside a transaction, clobbering concurrent commission increments
findings.detail: Both callables do a plain `ref.get()` (line 27 / 53) and then `ref.update({ affiliate: { ...existing, ... } })` (line 32-42 and line 55) — a non-atomic read-modify-write of the entire `affiliate` map. Every other writer of that map uses field-path increments: accrueCommission (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:93-97) does `'affiliate.pendingBalancePaise': FieldValue.increment(...)`, confirmCommissionsForOrder does the same for pending/confirmed/lifetime (commissions.ts:129-134). A whole-map set based on a stale read silently reverts any increment that landed in between.
findings.failure_scenario: Affiliate has pendingBalancePaise = 0. Admin taps the affiliate toggle (revoke) at the same moment a referred customer places an order: the checkout transaction increments pendingBalancePaise to 25000, then adminRevokeAffiliate writes back `{...existing(stale, pending=0), enabled:false}` — the ₹250 commission row exists in `commissions` but the affiliate's pending balance is 0, so it can never be confirmed into confirmedBalancePaise (the withdrawable balance).
findings.fix: Wrap both callables in db.runTransaction (read the customer doc inside the tx) and/or write only the fields that change using field paths — `'affiliate.enabled': false`, `'affiliate.commissionRate': rate` — instead of replacing the whole map.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:26-42 (adminAllocateAffiliate) and :51-55 (adminRevokeAffiliate) do `await ref.get()` then `await ref.update({ affiliate: {...existing, ...} })` with no transaction — writing the top-level `affiliate` key replaces the whole map from a stale read. Every other writer of that map uses field-path atomics that this reverts: commissions.ts:93-97 (pendingBalancePaise increment), commissions.ts:129-134 (pending/confirmed/lifetime), orders/cancel.ts:139 (pending decrement), affiliate/referral.ts:52-53 (referredCount increment), affiliate/requests.ts:88 (hasPendingWithdrawal). Refutation attempts all failed: (1) not handled by a transaction — the SAME file does the identical whole-map rewrite correctly for approveWithdrawal (:66-90) and rejectWithdrawal (:102-118) by reading via tx.get inside runTransaction, so allocate/revoke are the only two non-transactional ones, and the transactional form is clearly the intended pattern; (2) no reconciliation exists — grep shows every consumer of confirmedBalancePaise (app affiliate_withdraw/dashboard/wallet screens, web account/affiliate pages, admin AffiliateListPage/CustomerProfilePage, and the server-side eligibility check at requests.ts:39) reads the stored field directly; nothing ever re-derives balances from the `commissions` collection, so a clobbered balance is permanent and unrecoverable; (3) reachable — admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:58 calls adminRevokeAffiliate with {uid}, and admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:63 calls adminAllocateAffiliate with a rate, hitting the `existing` spread branch on re-enable/rate-edit; (4) the enabled-check in readReferringAffiliate (commissions.ts:44-45) is exactly the read that the interleaving beats; (5) not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not UI/cosmetic, not an architecture-rule exception (money code should be the most atomic). Impact is broader than reported: an allocate racing approveWithdrawal restores stale confirmedBalancePaise/withdrawnBalancePaise, re-crediting already-paid-out money; a revoke racing createWithdrawalRequest reverts hasPendingWithdrawal to false, defeating the single-pending-request guard. Only mitigation is the narrow get→update window (tens of ms), making it rare rather than deterministic — but it is a real, money-affecting, two-line fix (switch to 'affiliate.enabled' / 'affiliate.commissionRate' field paths, or wrap in runTransaction).

findings.title: The `payments` collection has no writer — the admin Payments page and GST-invoice export are permanently empty in production
findings.detail: `usePaymentsList()` subscribes to `collection(db,'payments')`. A full grep of `functions/src` for `payments` returns exactly one hit — `requireModule(req,'payments','view')` in `orders/invoice.ts:19` — i.e. no Cloud Function ever creates or updates a `payments/{id}` document. `placeOrder` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:504-509) and `verifyRazorpayPayment` (checkout.ts:726-729) only stamp `paymentStatus`/`amountPaidPaise`/`razorpayPaymentId` on the ORDER doc. `firestore.rules:76-79` makes `payments` `allow write: if false`, so no client can write it either. The only writer in the whole repo is `scripts/seed.ts:684` (`db.doc('payments/'+orderId).set(...)`). Consequently the `partial_refund`/`refunded` branches in `paymentStatusPill` (payments.ts:23-26) are dead — `adminApproveOrderRequest` increments `orders.refundedPaise` and flips `orders.paymentStatus`, never the payment doc.
findings.failure_scenario: On a real (non-seeded) project: a customer completes a Razorpay checkout, `verifyRazorpayPayment` sets order.paymentStatus='captured'. An admin opens /payments -> the table renders 'No payments yet.' and the header reads '₹0 this month · 0 failed'. Clicking 'GST invoices' toasts 'Nothing to export.' Every captured payment in the business is invisible to the admin.
findings.fix: Write a `payments/{orderId}` doc from `placeOrder` (status 'pending'/'captured' for fully-wallet orders) and update it in `verifyRazorpayPayment` (status 'captured', gatewayRef=razorpayPaymentId); update it to 'refunded'/'partial_refund' inside the `adminApproveOrderRequest` transaction alongside the `orders.refundedPaise` increment.

verdict.reason: I tried hard to find a writer and could not. Verified: (1) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:11 subscribes to `collection(db,'payments')` and /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx has no orders-derived fallback — it only uses `useOrdersList()` to map orderId -> shortId for labels (line 27), so with zero payment docs the table renders 'No payments yet.', stats compute 0, and both CSV exports hit `toast.info('Nothing to export.')` (line 56). (2) /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts `placeOrder` writes only the order doc (tx.set(orderRef, order) at :546, with paymentStatus/amountPaidPaise fields inline) and `verifyPayment` (:725) only does `ref.update({paymentStatus:'captured', razorpayPaymentId, razorpaySignature, amountPaidPaise…})` on orders/{id}. No payments doc anywhere. (3) /home/h/barkath/functions/src/index.ts exports callables only — there are zero `onRequest`/webhook/document-trigger functions (the header comment explicitly says all doc triggers were removed), so no gateway webhook could be materialising the ledger. The only `payments` string in functions/src is `requireModule(req,'payments','view')` in orders/invoice.ts:19. (4) The similarly named `pendingPayments` collection (functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:43,73,103) is a separate wallet-top-up collection, not this one. (5) /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:76-79 is `allow write: if false`, so no client (web/app/admin) can create them either — I found no client-side writes in web/, app/ or admin/ regardless. (6) The only writer in the repo is /home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:684 `db.doc(\`payments/${orderId}\`).set(...)`, so the page only ever looks populated on a seeded/emulator project. `Payment` is a first-class modelled entity (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:130, collections.ts:13, MODULE_KEYS 'payments', nav entry, security rules) — this is not an intentionally-unused concept, and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Writing a payments ledger doc is squarely CF territory under the architecture rules (money), so it is a real, fixable server-side gap, not a UI/cosmetic issue.

findings.title: Return window is hardcoded to 3 days server-side but the storefront gates on the admin-configurable `settings/returns.windowDays` (default 7)
findings.detail: `requestReturnOrReplacement` hardcodes `RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` and rejects anything older with 'The 3-day return window for this order has closed.' The web return page (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:23-25) gates on `returnWindow(order, returnSettings?.windowDays)` where `DEFAULT_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7` (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:246), and the admin writes that value in admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296. Both `scripts/seed.ts:208` and `scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117` seed `windowDays: 7`. The CF also hard-requires `o.deliveredAt` while `returnWindow()` falls back to `order.placedAt` when `deliveredAt` is missing, widening the gap. The admin's 'Return window (days)' input therefore controls nothing on the server, and nothing at all on the app (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:202 hardcodes 3 too).
findings.failure_scenario: Order delivered 5 days ago, settings/returns.windowDays = 7 (the seeded default). Web /account/orders/{id}/return renders the full form and says returns can be raised within 7 days. The customer picks a reason and submits -> the CF throws failed-precondition -> `requestReturn` returns ok:false -> the page shows the generic "We couldn't submit your return just now. Please try again." The customer retries forever and never learns the real reason.
findings.fix: Read `settings/returns.windowDays` inside `requestReturnOrReplacement` (falling back to 7, treating <=0 as returns-disabled) instead of the 3-day constant, and mirror the `deliveredAt ?? placedAt` fallback the web uses; make app/lib/.../order.dart read the same setting.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. functions/src/returns/requests.ts:42 hardcodes RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 days and never reads settings/returns (grep over functions/src shows only settings/affiliate, settings/delivery, settings/tax are read server-side — so reading admin settings in a CF is an established pattern that returns simply missed). Meanwhile web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:24-25 gates on returnWindow(order, returnSettings?.windowDays) with DEFAULT_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7 (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:246), admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296 persists windowDays (0-90), and both scripts/seed.ts:208 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117 seed windowDays: 7 — so the doc exists with 7 in every environment. An order delivered 4-7 days ago passes the web gate, renders the full form, then the CF throws failed-precondition; requestReturn (orders.ts:313-320) has a bare `catch { return false }` so the user only ever sees the generic "We couldn't submit your return just now." The gap is widened further because returnWindow() falls back to order.placedAt when deliveredAt is missing while the CF hard-requires deliveredAt. No guard, fallback, or re-check closes this; it is not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; and it is functional (a legitimately eligible return is unconditionally rejected), not cosmetic. The app's own returnWindowDays=3 agrees with the CF, which only means the admin's configurable input controls nothing anywhere.

findings.title: Coupon 'Category restriction' is written to Firestore but no surface enforces it, so a category-limited coupon discounts any cart
findings.detail: CouponFormPage.tsx:328-349 renders category chips and saveCoupon persists `applicableCategories: values.applicableCategories` (coupons.ts:130) as category slugs. Grepping every consumer of that field across the repo returns exactly one hit — app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:108, which uses it only to build a display string ('Perfume only'). `computeCouponDiscount` and `autoBestOffer` in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts never read it, and web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts never reads it. Also note the admin stores `c.slug` while products carry `categoryId`/`categorySlug`, so even a future check would need the slug form.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates PERFUME20 (20% off) and restricts it to the 'perfume' category to clear that stock. A customer puts only ₹5,000 of dates and dry fruits (categoryId 'grocery') in the cart and enters PERFUME20. computeCouponDiscount validates code, active, min cart, uses, and applies ₹1,000 off with no category check. The margin-protecting restriction the admin configured is a no-op.
findings.fix: Enforce it server-side in computeCouponDiscount/autoBestOffer: `priceLines` already resolves each product, so reject (or restrict the discount base to) lines whose `categorySlug`/`categoryId` is not in `applicableCategories` when that array is non-empty. Mirror the check in web offers.ts.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Verified end-to-end:

WRITE SIDE (real, not decorative): /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx:327-349 renders a "Category restriction" chip group with explicit copy ("Applies to every category." / "Limited to N categories."), seeds from `c.applicableCategories` (lines 81, 106), and passes `applicableCategories: selectedCats` (line 168) into `saveCoupon`, which persists it on both create and update paths (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:130, inside `base`, so it is written by setDoc AND updateDoc). It is a first-class field in the shared type (/home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:31).

READ SIDE (no enforcement anywhere): `grep -rn "applicableCategories"` across the whole repo (ts/tsx/dart) returns only: the shared type, scripts/seed.ts:720 (writes `[]`), the two admin files above, and app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:108 — which uses it purely to build a display string (`'${_cap(cat.first)} only'`) and never filters or zeroes the discount. The authoritative server path /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts `computeCouponDiscount` (lines 122-207) checks active/status, validFrom, validUntil, minCartValuePaise, maxUsesTotal, maxUsesPerUser, firstOrderOnly — and never reads applicableCategories (nor applicableProducts/excludedProducts). `autoBestOffer` (215-259) likewise. Web mirror /home/h/barkath/web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts has no category logic (its `PromoCoupon` shape doesn't even declare the field). No other callable validates coupons (only checkout.ts does), and firebase/firestore.rules:59 only gates read/write, not discount logic. So `applyCoupon` and `placeOrder` both apply the full discount to a cart containing zero items from the restricted category.

Not refutable on the usual grounds: it is not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; it is not cosmetic (the fix is server-side enforcement in computeCouponDiscount, not a UI change); the path is reachable from both app and web checkout; and the data is already on hand — priceLines already resolves `category: p.categorySlug` per line (checkout.ts:84, carried through to the order at 477/493), which is the same slug form the admin stores (`c.slug`), so the check is implementable with no schema change. Also note only `computeCouponDiscount` is the server-authoritative gate — the client mirrors would need the same rule to keep quoted totals honest.

findings.title: Admin "Grant spins" is cosmetic — executeSpin never gates on spinsRemaining
findings.detail: executeSpin reads `spinsRemaining` (line 93) and decrements it with a `Math.max(0, remaining - 1)` floor (line 110), but never blocks when it is 0 — the only gate is the campaign-level `spinsPerDay` daily cap counted from spinHistory (lines 74-88). The comment on line 108 admits it: "the daily cap above is the real gate, so this never blocks". adminGrantSpins (functions/src/spin/grant.ts:31) is the sole writer, and both clients ignore the field: app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:37 derives spins left purely from `spinsPerDay - usedToday`, and web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:66-75 does the same. Every customer doc is created with `spinsRemaining: 0` (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:51, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:233), yet all of them can still spin.
findings.failure_scenario: Campaign has spinsPerDay=1. Admin opens a customer, types 5, clicks "Grant spins" (admin/src/features/customers/routes/CustomerProfilePage.tsx:175); the card shows 5 and toasts "Granted 5 spins". The customer still gets exactly 1 spin today, and the balance silently drops to 4. Conversely "Clear balance" (line 181) sets it to 0 and the customer still spins normally — the privileged action changes nothing.
findings.fix: Either enforce the granted balance in executeSpin (treat spinsRemaining as bonus spins beyond spinsPerDay, and reject when both the daily cap and the balance are exhausted), or remove the grant/revoke UI and the adminGrantSpins callable so admins are not told they changed something they did not.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. executeSpin (functions/src/spin/execute.ts) gates only on the campaign-level daily cap (lines 74-88: spinsPerDay minus spinHistory rows since IST midnight); it reads spinsRemaining at line 93 and decrements it at line 110 with a Math.max(0, ...) floor but never throws when it is 0 — the comment at 108-109 admits "the daily cap above is the real gate, so this never blocks". A repo-wide grep for spinsRemaining returns only: packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:126 (type), execute.ts (93,110), grant.ts (sole writer), admin/src/features/customers (display + grant button), and two comments. No client and no security rule gates on it: app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:37-50 and web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:66-75 both compute spinsPerDay − usedToday, and firebase/firestore.rules never mentions the field. adminGrantSpins is fully reachable (exported at functions/src/index.ts:35, called from admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:66, permission-gated and audited), so the privileged action is a no-op. It is not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, and it is not cosmetic — grant.ts's own docstring says "Spins are consumed by executeSpin and never reset daily" and e2e/tests/web/spin.spec.ts:8-13 documents the intended semantics as "the per-customer balance (customer.spinsRemaining), NOT the campaign's per-day limit", both contradicted by the implementation. The fix is server-side in execute.ts (gate on remaining, or treat granted spins as an allowance above the daily cap); no UI change needed. With seed spinsPerDay=3, a customer with spinsRemaining:0 still spins 3 times and "Clear balance" revokes nothing.

findings.title: Campaign `eligibility` is written by admin but never enforced by executeSpin
findings.detail: Both admin screens persist `eligibility` (admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:123 on create, :145 on save) with options all/new/existing/affiliates/segment (CreateCampaignPage.tsx:14-20). executeSpin validates only `status` (line 56) and the date window (line 59) — it never loads the customer's affiliate flag, order count or signup date. A repo-wide grep for `eligibility` returns only the shared type, the two admin files and seed.ts: no function, no web page, no Dart file ever reads it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates an "Affiliates only" wheel with a ₹500-off slice and activates it. Any signed-in customer opens Rewards (web) or the Spin screen (app) — activeCampaign() filters on status only — calls executeSpin and wins the affiliate-only coupon, which checkout then honours from customers/{uid}/coupons.
findings.fix: In executeSpin, after the status/window checks, load customers/{uid} and reject with failed-precondition when camp.eligibility is 'affiliates' and `affiliate.enabled != true`, 'new' and stats.totalOrders > 0, 'existing' and stats.totalOrders == 0; the clients should apply the same filter when choosing the active campaign.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed as a real, fixable server-side gap.

1. `/home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts` is the only server path that issues spin prizes. Its guards are: campaign exists (52-53), `camp.status !== 'active'` (56), date window (57-59), non-empty slices (61-62), and the per-day spin cap (74-88). The transaction reads `customers/{uid}` (line 91) but only for `spinsRemaining` — it never touches `camp.eligibility`, an affiliate record, `ordersCount`, or signup date.

2. `eligibility` really is persisted by admin: `/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:123` (create) and `:145` (save, with an `?? 'all'` fallback), typed `CouponTarget` = `['all','new','existing','affiliates','segment']` (`packages/shared/src/enums.ts:81`) and declared on `SpinCampaign` (`packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:109`). Grep for `eligibility` across .ts/.tsx/.dart returns only the shared type, the two admin route files, the admin api file, seed.ts, and an unrelated coupons-page string — no function, web page, or Dart file reads it.

3. Both client surfaces filter on status only, so a restricted campaign is offered to everyone: `web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:52` (`where('status','==','active')`) and `app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:22-26` (`activeCampaign()`, same filter).

4. The prize is genuinely spendable — no downstream re-check rescues it. `executeSpin` writes the coupon to `customers/{uid}/coupons` (execute.ts:127-140) with no `targetUsers` field, and `functions/src/orders/checkout.ts` honours personal coupons unconditionally: the manual-code branch (lines ~196-203) and `autoBestOffer`'s personal loop (240-256) apply only expiry and `minCartValuePaise`. The `targetUsers !== 'all'` guard at checkout.ts:224 applies solely to the global `coupons` collection.

5. Not intentional and not in the KNOWN list. The parallel field on regular coupons (`Coupon.targetUsers`) IS enforced server-side at `functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:224` and client-side at `web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:38,112` — so the codebase does treat targeting as an enforced concept; spin campaigns are the omission. The data needed for a fix exists (`customers/{uid}.ordersCount` per `packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:93`, plus the affiliates collection), and the minimal fix (reject/deny when `camp.eligibility` is not 'all' and the customer doesn't match) belongs squarely in a Cloud Function since it is a money-issuing, server-authoritative path.

Not cosmetic: no UI change is required, only a guard in execute.ts.

findings.title: Campaigns past their end date stay status 'active', so every client spin fails
findings.detail: deriveSpinStatus computes "Ended"/"Scheduled" purely from startsAt/endsAt (lines 72-76) but nothing ever persists status='ended' — the only status writer is setCampaignStatus (line 154), driven by the single Pause/Activate button (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:296), and grep shows no 'ended' write in functions/ or admin/ at all. Both clients select the campaign by status only: app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:22 (`where('status','==','active').limit(1)`) and web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:52. executeSpin, however, does enforce the window (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:57-59).
findings.failure_scenario: A 30-day campaign created with "Activate immediately" reaches its end date. Admin list shows it as "Ended" so nobody touches it. The app Spin screen still renders the wheel and says "1 spin left today"; every tap of "Spin now" round-trips to executeSpin and comes back failed-precondition "This spin campaign is not active right now" — a permanently broken screen with no way for the customer to know why.
findings.fix: Have the clients filter the window too (startsAt <= now <= endsAt), and/or flip status to 'ended' — either in a scheduled sweep like couponExpirySweep, or lazily in executeSpin when it detects now > endsAt.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this on four fronts and all failed.

1. Nothing ever persists status='ended'. `grep -rn "'ended'"` across functions/, admin/, web/, app/, scripts/ hits only the shared enum (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:175, SPIN_CAMPAIGN_STATUSES) and the read-side badge at admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:69. The only writer is `setCampaignStatus` (spinner.ts:153), called from exactly one place — CampaignDetailPage.tsx:259, the manual Pause/Activate toggle. functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts contains only `couponExpirySweep` (line 87) and touches `coupons` / user coupons; it never reads or writes `spinCampaigns` (`grep -rn spinCampaign functions/src` matches only functions/src/spin/execute.ts).

2. No client-side window guard exists. app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:22-26 selects `where('status','==','active').limit(1)` and app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_campaign.dart does not even parse `startsAt`/`endsAt` (the model fields are id/name/status/slices/spinsPerDay/rewardCouponExpiryDays only), so the app cannot filter on the window. web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:51-54 likewise queries `where('status','==','active')` with no date check; `grep -rn "endsAt" web/src` only matches the unrelated flash-sale helper (web/src/lib/flashSale.ts:23-24) — which proves the compute-on-read window pattern exists elsewhere but was not applied here.

3. The server does enforce the window: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:57-59 rejects with `failed-precondition` "This spin campaign is not active right now" when `now < startsAt || now > endsAt`. So after the end date (or before a future start date, the "Scheduled" case) the app renders the wheel and "spins left today" (spin_screen.dart:225-295, canSpin derived only from spinsLeftToday) and every tap fails at spin_screen.dart:66.

4. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not unreachable (every finite-window campaign reaches its end date; `createCampaign` at spinner.ts:112-118 always writes an endsAt), and not cosmetic — the fix is functional: filter/gate on the window client-side (compute-on-read, exactly as the coupon-expiry architecture rule prescribes) or add a sweep that flips status.

Only overstatement in the claim: the app does surface the server message via AppToast (spin_screen.dart:73-77), so the customer sees "This spin campaign is not active right now" rather than a silent failure. The functional defect — a permanently unspinnable wheel shown as available — stands.

findings.title: Approved returns refund the customer but never reverse the affiliate's confirmed commission
findings.detail: `adminApproveOrderRequest` credits the refund to the wallet, writes the ledger row and stamps the request/item — the whole file contains zero references to `commissions` or `affiliate` (grep count 0 across all 182 lines). Meanwhile functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11-14 documents the design as: "Commission clears at delivery rather than after `commissionClearanceDays` … Returns are handled by the return flow, which is the case the clearance delay was protecting against." That claim is false — the return flow does nothing. `confirmCommissionsForOrder` (commissions.ts:107) has already moved the commission from `pendingBalancePaise` into `confirmedBalancePaise` on delivery, and `confirmedBalancePaise` is the withdrawable balance (requests.ts:39-40), so the money is immediately payable. cancel.ts:71-74 deliberately only reverses rows still `pending`, so no other path claws it back either.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer B (referred by affiliate A at 5%) orders ₹20,000 of merchandise. Admin marks it delivered → A's confirmedBalancePaise += ₹1,000. B raises a return; admin approves it → B is refunded ₹20,000 to wallet. A still holds ₹1,000 withdrawable and can immediately call requestWithdrawal for it. The business pays commission on goods it took back, with no ledger trace.
findings.fix: In the approve transaction, read `commissions` for `orderId` (query before the transaction, re-read each ref inside it), and for rows with status 'confirmed' write `status:'reversed'`/`cancellationReason` and `FieldValue.increment(-amount)` on `affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise` (and `lifetimeEarningsPaise`), pro-rating by the refunded fraction of the order for partial returns. Clamp at zero and record a shortfall if the affiliate already withdrew it.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds up. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/returns/decisions.ts (both adminApproveOrderRequest and adminRejectOrderRequest) contains no reference to `commissions` or `affiliate`; approve only credits the wallet, writes walletTransactions, stamps the request, increments orders.refundedPaise and flips the item's returnStatus. Nothing anywhere else compensates:

- grep for "commission" across functions/src shows only checkout.ts (accrue pending), orders/status.ts:97 (confirmCommissionsForOrder on delivery), orders/cancel.ts (reversal), affiliate/*. Zero hits in returns/.
- /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:71-75 filters `status === 'pending'` with the explicit comment "A commission only needs reversing while it is still pending — once it has cleared to the affiliate's confirmed balance it may already be withdrawn", so cancellation deliberately does not claw back confirmed rows.
- The ordering makes the gap unavoidable rather than a corner case: returns/requests.ts hard-requires `o.status !== 'delivered' → failed-precondition`, and delivery is exactly the transition that runs confirmCommissionsForOrder (commissions.ts:107-137, pending→confirmed). So by construction every return-eligible order already has its commission in `affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise`.
- confirmedBalancePaise is the withdrawable balance: affiliate/requests.ts:39-40 validates `amountPaise > confirmed` and nothing else, so the money is immediately payable via requestWithdrawal.
- No alternate surface can fix it manually: firebase/firestore.rules:86-89 makes `commissions` `allow write: if false` (CF-only), and admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts exposes no commission-reversal callable — only withdrawal approve/reject and allocate/revoke.

It is also not an accepted deferral: commissions.ts:11-14 asserts "Returns are handled by the return flow, which is the case the clearance delay was protecting against" — an assertion the code contradicts — and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. This is a money defect (business refunds the goods but still pays commission on them, with no commissions ledger row marking the reversal), server-side and fixable.

findings.title: Review moderation is gated only by isAdmin() in rules — the reviews module permission is client-side hiding with no server backing
findings.detail: The rules file explicitly states (lines 15-19) that every collection admins write directly is gated by `canWrite(module)`. `/reviews/{id}` breaks that contract: `allow update: if hasAppCheck() && isAdmin() && affectedKeys().hasOnly(['status','moderatedBy','moderatedAt','updatedAt','helpfulCount'])` — any sub-admin passes, with no `reviews` module check. `allow read` is likewise `isAdmin()` for every doc. Nothing else stops this: admin/src/app/router.tsx:79 registers `/reviews` under `RequireAuth` only, and RequireAuth performs no module check — Sidebar.tsx:11-12 merely hides the nav link. admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:50 writes the review status directly from the client (no callable, so no `requireModule`). Conversely the same transaction does `tx.update(pRef, {ratingCount, rating})` at reviews.ts:64 against `/products/{id}`, which rules gate with `canWrite('products')`.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin is created with only `dashboard.view` enabled. The Reviews link is hidden, but typing /reviews in the URL loads the full moderation queue (read allowed by isAdmin()) and 'Reject' on any pending review succeeds — no product write is needed for pending→rejected, so the rules accept it. Symmetrically, a sub-admin granted the whole `reviews` module but not `products` clicks 'Approve' and the transaction is rejected with permission-denied, because approving must write products.rating.
findings.fix: Change the reviews rule to `allow update: if canWrite('reviews') && affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` (and read to `isAdmin()` is fine), and allow the ratingCount/rating aggregate write on products when `can('reviews','approve')` — or move the aggregate update into a callable guarded by `requireModule(req,'reviews','approve')`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. firebase/firestore.rules:113 is the only admin *write* rule in the file gated by bare isAdmin() — every other collection admins write directly (lines 48-59: settings, content, categories, products, flashSales, newArrivals, banners, spinCampaigns, pincodes, coupons) uses canWrite(module), and the comment at lines 15-19 states that as the contract. Nothing backstops it: grep over functions/src finds no review-moderation callable (only checkout.ts and returns/decisions.ts mention 'review'), so there is no requireModule('reviews', ...) server-side; admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:31-65 writes the status straight from the client in a runTransaction. admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx checks only auth hydration and admin presence — it never reads modulePermissions — and router.tsx:79 mounts /reviews under it unconditionally, so the sole enforcement is the canView filter in admin/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:11-12, i.e. nav hiding. 'reviews' IS a defined module key (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:258 in MODULE_KEYS), so canWrite('reviews') would be well-defined; its absence is an omission, not an intentional 'no matrix entry' case. The asymmetry also checks out: reviews.ts:64 does tx.update(pRef, {ratingCount, rating}) on /products/{id}, gated by canWrite('products') at rules line 51, so a reviews-only sub-admin's Approve fails with permission-denied; while pending->rejected takes the wasCounted===willCount branch (pSnap null, early return) and touches only the review doc, so any sub-admin can reject. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, and the fix is a rules/permission change, not UI.

findings.title: Settings → Storefront return window is ignored by the server, which hardcodes 3 days
findings.detail: Admin writes `settings/returns.windowDays` via admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296 → saveReturns (api/settings.ts:84). The storefront honours it: web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261 `returnWindow(order, returnSettings?.windowDays)` with a 7-day fallback, used to show/hide the Return button (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71). But the callable that actually creates the return hardcodes `const RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` and rejects anything older, and the Flutter app hardcodes its own value too (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:202 `returnWindowDays = 3`). Nothing anywhere reads `settings/returns` on the server or in the app. Even the seeded default (scripts/seed.ts:208, `windowDays: 7`) already disagrees with the CF.
findings.failure_scenario: With the seeded default of 7 days (or an admin setting 14), a customer opens a delivered order 5 days after delivery. The web order page computes `open: true, daysLeft: 2` and renders 'Request return'. Submitting calls requestReturnOrReplacement, which throws failed-precondition 'The 3-day return window for this order has closed.' The customer sees a dead button; the admin's configured window has no effect at all.
findings.fix: Have requestReturnOrReplacement read `settings/returns` inside the transaction and use `windowDays` (falling back to 7) instead of the hardcoded 3 days, and make app/lib/.../order.dart read the same doc rather than the `returnWindowDays = 3` constant.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. functions/src/returns/requests.ts:42-46 hardcodes a 3-day window and never reads settings/returns; the admin writes windowDays via admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:84 (saveReturns) from StorefrontTab.tsx:296, and web reads it (web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:49 -> web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261, fallback 7) to gate the Return button on account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71 and the form at .../return/page.tsx:26. Both web and app submit through the same callable (orders.ts:315; app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:127), so any configured window >3 yields a button that throws failed-precondition. Seeds already conflict: scripts/seed.ts:208 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117 set windowDays: 7. No server-side compensating read exists, yet other callables DO read settings docs (settings/affiliate in affiliate/requests.ts:24; settings/delivery and settings/tax in orders/checkout.ts:355-356), showing this is an omission rather than an intentional design. Secondary mismatch: web falls back to placedAt when deliveredAt is missing while the CF hard-rejects a missing deliveredAt. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic, and fixable server-side (read settings/returns.windowDays with a 7-day fallback; app hardcodes 3 at order.dart:202 too).

findings.title: Top-products report reads itemsSummary, which checkout truncates to the first 4 line items
findings.detail: computeTopProducts iterates `o.itemsSummary ?? []`. The only writer of orders, functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:492, writes `itemsSummary: priced.slice(0, 4).map(...)` — it is an explicitly capped thumbnail strip, not the line-item list. The full line items are written on the same doc as `items` (checkout.ts:474-482, typed `Order.items` in packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:47) and older orders keep them in the orders/{id}/items subcollection. The reports module never reads either. admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35 already implements the correct embedded-array + subcollection fallback; reports does not use it.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer checks out with 6 distinct products (A..F). checkout writes itemsSummary=[A,B,C,D] and items=[A..F]. On Reports, products E and F contribute ₹0 revenue and never appear in Top products, no matter how expensive they are. Every order with >4 distinct products silently under-reports.
findings.fix: Iterate the canonical line items instead: `const lines = o.items ?? []` (plus the legacy orders/{id}/items fallback used by useOrderItems), and accumulate per productId from those. Never use itemsSummary for analytics.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end; could not refute. (1) functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:492 is the only production writer of orders and writes `itemsSummary: priced.slice(0, 4).map(...)` — an explicitly capped 4-element thumbnail strip; the full uncapped line items are built at checkout.ts:474-482 and written as `items` on the same doc. (2) packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:41-47 documents the split (`itemsSummary` thumbnails vs `items?` canonical, with legacy orders in orders/{id}/items). (3) admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:228 iterates `o.itemsSummary ?? []` and never reads `items` or the subcollection; computeTopProducts is live (called at admin/src/features/reports/routes/ReportsPage.tsx:72). (4) Escapes ruled out: no cart-line cap exists in the checkout Zod schema or transaction, so >4 distinct products is reachable; the only other `itemsSummary` writer is scripts/seed.ts:571; web readers use it only as thumbnails or with an items-first fallback (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:98, invoice/page.tsx:47); admin already has the correct embedded+subcollection reader at admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35 which reports does not reuse; not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; not cosmetic — it is analytics data correctness. Separately noted in the same loop: line 229 computes revenue from the current catalogue `offerPricePaise` instead of the order's captured `lineTotalPaise`, a second gap the same fix would resolve.

findings.title: Top-products revenue is priced from the live catalog price, not the order's line totals
findings.detail: `const priceOf = new Map(products.map(p => [p.id, p.offerPricePaise ?? 0]))` (line 223) and `revenue = (item.quantity ?? 0) * (priceOf.get(item.productId) ?? 0)` (line 229). The order line already carries the realised amount: OrderItem.lineTotalPaise / offerPricePaise, written at checkout (checkout.ts:479). Worse, for a variant product the product-level offerPricePaise is just the FIRST variant row's price — admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:205,235 sets `baseRow = variantRows[0]` and writes `offerPricePaise: toPaise(offerOf(baseRow))`. Coupon/spin discounts on the order are also ignored.
findings.failure_scenario: An abaya sold in S/M/L at ₹1,200/₹1,400/₹1,600 (S is variant row 0). 100 units of L sold last month → Top products reports 100 × ₹1,200 = ₹1,20,000 instead of ₹1,60,000. If an admin then edits the price to ₹999, the report for the ALREADY-CLOSED period retroactively drops to ₹99,900 — historical revenue changes when a price is edited. A product deleted from the catalog reports ₹0.
findings.fix: Compute revenue from the order line itself: `row.paise += item.lineTotalPaise ?? (item.quantity * item.offerPricePaise)`, using o.items (with the legacy subcollection fallback). Drop the products→price map entirely; the products query is then only needed for names.

verdict.reason:
Verified in code; I could not refute it.

1. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:223,229 — computeTopProducts builds priceOf from the LIVE catalog (p.offerPricePaise) and computes revenue = item.quantity * priceOf.get(item.productId). It iterates o.itemsSummary, and OrderItemSummary (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:10-16) carries only productId/productName/imageUrl/categoryTint/quantity — no money at all — so the live catalog price is the only price source. No guard, fallback, or server-side recompute exists: computeTopProducts is called once, from ReportsPage.tsx:72 with products.data from the live products collection, and its output feeds both the on-screen table and the CSV export (downloadReportCsv, lines 267-268), so this is data output, not cosmetics.

2. The realised amounts ARE on the same order doc the report already loads. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:473-482 embeds items with per-line mrpPaise, offerPricePaise, lineTotalPaise; admin already consumes it (admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:207 renders it.lineTotalPaise). useReportOrders fetches whole order docs, so o.items is already in hand — no extra reads needed.

3. The variant claim holds: admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:205 `const baseRow = (hasVariants ? variantRows[0] : filledRows[0])!` and line 229 `offerPricePaise: toPaise(offerOf(baseRow))` — the product-level price is literally variant row 0's price, so every variant sold is priced at that one row.

4. The consequences follow from the code: editing a product price retroactively mutates already-closed periods (report recomputed on read from the live catalog); a deleted product yields `?? 0`; order-level discountPaise/spinRewardPaise never touch the figure.

Extra corroboration the reporter missed: checkout.ts:492 writes `itemsSummary: priced.slice(0, 4)` — only the first four lines. For a 5+ line order the 5th item onward contributes zero to Top products regardless of price, making itemsSummary doubly wrong as the aggregation source.

None of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL exemptions apply. The fix is contained and functional: aggregate over o.items using lineTotalPaise, with a fallback to the orders/{id}/items subcollection for pre-embedding orders per the architecture rule.

findings.title: Dashboard revenue trend caps at 2000 oldest orders, zeroing out the most recent months
findings.detail: `query(ordersCol(), where('createdAt','>=',from), orderBy('createdAt','asc'), limit(2000))`. The sort is ASCENDING, so the limit keeps the OLDEST 2000 documents in the window and discards everything after them. The result is then bucketed into the 12 monthly / 30 daily bars. There is no indication to the user that the series is truncated.
findings.failure_scenario: Store does 300 orders/month. On the 12M range the query window holds ~3600 orders; the ascending limit(2000) returns only the first ~6.7 months. The bars for the last ~5 months — including the current month — render at heightPct 2 with ₹0, so the dashboard shows revenue having collapsed to zero. Growth makes the problem worse, not better.
findings.fix: Either aggregate server-side per bucket (getAggregateFromServer with sum('totalPaise') per month/day range, same pattern already used by sumTotalPaise at line 43), or page through the window with startAfter until exhausted. If a cap must stay, order DESCENDING so the newest data survives and label the chart as partial.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:247-256. useRevenueTrend issues exactly one query — query(ordersCol(), where('createdAt','>=',from), orderBy('createdAt','asc'), limit(2000)) — then buckets the returned docs into the 12 monthly / 30 / 7 daily buckets from planBuckets(). Ascending sort from the window start means limit(2000) keeps the OLDEST 2000 orders and silently drops everything newer; buckets past the cut stay at paise 0 and render heightPct 2 (line 261). No pagination loop, no aggregate query, no fallback, no truncation indicator — unlike sumTotalPaise/countOrders (lines 41-62) which use getAggregateFromServer and only fall back to a bounded client read. Nothing else corrects it: the sole consumer is admin/src/features/dashboard/routes/DashboardPage.tsx:35, and the Reports feature (admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:69-72) computes its own trend from a separate unbounded live listener ('orders:all:createdAt-desc'), so it neither covers nor justifies the dashboard series. Refutation attempts fail: not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; no architecture rule mandates it; the 12M path is the default on page load; and the defect is data correctness (rupee totals reported as zero), not cosmetic — fixable entirely inside this query/aggregation logic with no UI change. Only mitigation is scale: below ~2000 orders in the window the bug is dormant, and the sibling reports query reads the whole orders collection unbounded, so this 2000 cap is an outlier rather than a deliberate global policy.

findings.title: Dashboard counts cancelled orders as revenue; Reports excludes them — the two screens disagree
findings.detail: dashboard.ts sums totalPaise with no status filter: today's revenue (line 85), yesterday (86), lifetime for AOV (87), the 30/60-day AOV windows (90-93) and the trend bars (line 255) all include status=='cancelled' orders. reports.ts:100-101 does the opposite — `sumRevenue` filters `o.status !== 'cancelled'` and computeTrend skips them (reports.ts:194) — with the comment "Cancelled orders never realised revenue". Same collection, same field, two different answers in the same admin panel.
findings.failure_scenario: On a day with ₹1,00,000 booked and ₹40,000 cancelled, Dashboard "Today's revenue" shows ₹1.0L while Reports (7D) attributes ₹60,000 to that day. "Avg order value" on the dashboard is inflated further because the cancelled orders are in both the numerator (lifetime sum) and the denominator (countOrders([]) with no status filter).
findings.fix: Apply the reports rule to the dashboard: add `where('status','!=','cancelled')` (or subtract a cancelled-only aggregate) to every sumTotalPaise/countOrders call and to the trend reducer, so both surfaces use one definition of realised revenue.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts sums totalPaise with date-only constraints — sumTotalPaise (lines 41-52) is called at lines 85/86/87/90/92 with no status filter, and the trend loop at line 255 adds o.totalPaise for every doc. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts does the opposite: sumRevenue (line 100-101) filters o.status !== 'cancelled' and computeTrend line 194 skips cancelled, with the comment "Cancelled orders never realised revenue". Same 'orders' collection, same totalPaise field, same 12M/30D/7D bucketing, two different numbers in the same admin panel. Refutation attempts failed: functions/src/orders/cancel.ts performCancellation (lines 146-153) writes only status/cancelledAt/cancellationReason/cancelledByUid/paymentStatus — it never zeroes or adjusts totalPaise, so a cancelled order keeps its full amount; DashboardPage.tsx consumes useDashboardKpis/useRevenueTrend with no post-filtering; both surfaces label the metric "revenue" so it is not a deliberate gross-vs-net split (no comment or type says so); and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. It is aggregation logic, not UI/cosmetic, and is fixable (e.g. add a status constraint to the aggregate queries and the trend loop). One small overstatement in the claim: AOV is not "inflated further" since cancelled orders appear in both the numerator (lifetimeRevenue) and denominator (totalOrders) — but the cross-surface revenue disagreement itself is real.

findings.title: Reports opens four unbounded real-time listeners over entire collections with no limit or date filter
findings.detail: useReportOrders subscribes to `query(collection(db,'orders'), orderBy('createdAt','desc'))` — the whole orders collection, live, no limit; useReportProducts (line 52) reads all products; useReportCustomers (line 57) all customers; useReportOrderRequests (line 64) all orderRequests. Every order document now embeds its full `items` array (checkout.ts:495), so each doc is large. All KPI/trend/top-product maths is then done client-side in render (ReportsPage.tsx:70-72) over the full arrays on every keystroke-free re-render. The snapshots are held forever in the module-level `cache` map in hooks/firestoreCache.ts:32 — the listener detaches on unmount but the data is never evicted.
findings.failure_scenario: At 50,000 lifetime orders, opening Reports downloads 50,000 documents (tens of MB, 50k billed reads) before the first KPI appears, and the tab keeps that array resident for the session. Selecting the 7D preset still reads all 50,000 docs to compute a 7-day number, and every new order pushed by the listener re-runs computeKpis/computeTrend/computeTopProducts over the whole set.
findings.fix: Scope the queries to the active range (`where('createdAt','>=', rangeStart(range))`) so the read grows with the window, not the store's lifetime; use getDocs rather than onSnapshot for a report; and memoise the compute functions with useMemo on [data, range].

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code, no mitigation found. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:45-67 opens four useLiveCollection subscriptions with no where/limit/startAt: orders (orderBy createdAt desc), products, customers, orderRequests. The query never varies with the selected range, yet rangeStart() (line 24) already computes an exact lower bound that computeKpis/computeTrend/computeTopProducts then apply client-side via inWindow() — so the bound exists and is simply not pushed into the query; picking 7D still streams every lifetime order. Order docs embed the full items array (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:47), so per-doc payload is large even though reports only needs itemsSummary/totalPaise/createdAt. ReportsPage.tsx:70-72 calls the three compute functions bare in the render body with no useMemo anywhere under features/reports/, so every listener push rescans the full arrays. firestoreCache.ts:70-82 deliberately retains e.snapshot on unsubscribe and the module-level cache map has no eviction, so the arrays stay resident. Additionally the claim understates it: reports uses key 'orders:all:createdAt-desc' vs the orders feature's 'orders:placedAt-desc' (features/orders/api/orders.ts:15) and 'products:all' vs PRODUCTS_KEY 'products:createdAt-desc', so it opens duplicate full-collection listeners rather than reusing the cached ones (only customers and orderRequests keys are shared). Refutation attempts failed: features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:41-94,121 uses getCountFromServer/getAggregateFromServer plus where('createdAt','>=') and limit(500/1000/2000), proving bounded reads are the intended pattern elsewhere; nothing in the architecture rules or the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list covers this; the fix is data-layer only (range-scoped query key + createdAt constraint + memoization) with no UI change. Confidence is medium rather than high only because this is a scale-dependent perf issue, not a correctness bug, and the unbounded live-collection pattern is codebase-wide (orders/products/payments/reviews lists are equally unbounded) — Reports is just the one place where the bound is trivially available.

findings.title: App's add/edit address screen has no state or pincode input, so app-created addresses persist `state: ''` and `pincode: ''`
findings.detail: The screen only collects a label, `Flat / building` (-> line1) and `Area` (-> city). At save it hardcodes `state: widget.existing?.state ?? ''` and `pincode: widget.existing?.pincode ?? ''` (lines 90-91), so any address created in the app has empty state/pincode forever (editing it in the app can never fill them either). The web form writing the same `customers/{uid}.addresses` array validates both as required — web/src/app/(shop)/account/addresses/new/page.tsx:15 `PIN_RE = /^\d{6}$/` and errors.state/errors.pincode. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:511 embeds the chosen address verbatim as `deliveryAddress`, and functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:44 renders `${addr.city} ${addr.pincode}`.
findings.failure_scenario: An app-only customer adds "Apt 1204" / "Kakkanad" and checks out. The order's `deliveryAddress.pincode` is "", `state` is ""; the generated invoice's Bill-to block prints the city with no pincode, the admin order screen shows an address with no PIN, and the parcel cannot be routed. The same customer's address created on the web has a valid pincode — the two surfaces produce structurally different records in the same array.
findings.fix: Add State and Pincode fields (6-digit validation, mirroring PIN_RE) plus name/phone as on the web form, and require them before enabling Save.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real functional defect. app/lib/features/checkout/add_address_screen.dart collects only label, line1 (Flat/building) and city (Area) — _valid (line 41) checks just those two — and hardcodes state: widget.existing?.state ?? '' and pincode: widget.existing?.pincode ?? '' at lines 90-91, so every app-created address persists empty state/pincode and in-app editing can never fill them (no pincode/state TextField exists anywhere in app/lib; grep for "pincode" in app/lib only hits model/serialisation code). This is the only address form in the app: app_router.dart:239 is the sole route and saved_addresses_screen.dart reuses the same screen for create and edit. Nothing repairs it downstream: address_repository.dart writes the empty strings verbatim into customers/{uid}.addresses, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts validates only addressId (z.string().min(1), line 329), looks the address up by id (line 398) and embeds it unchanged as deliveryAddress (line 511) — grep for "pincode" across functions/src yields a single hit, functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:44, which is a consumer (`${esc(addr.city)} ${esc(addr.pincode)}` in the Bill-to block), not a validator. The web form writing the same array requires both fields (web/src/app/(shop)/account/addresses/new/page.tsx:15 PIN_RE=/^\d{6}$/, plus errors.state/errors.pincode), so the two surfaces produce structurally different records in one array. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and not cosmetic — it is a data-integrity/cross-surface bug whose fix (adding State + Pincode fields with the web's validation) changes persisted order and invoice data.

findings.title: Edit profile never sets `profileComplete`, so a customer who skipped signup is sent back to Create Profile forever (including on the web)
findings.detail: `_save()` updates only `name`, `email` and `updatedAt`. It does not set `profileComplete: true` (nor recompute `searchIndex`), unlike both `AuthRepository.completeProfile` (auth_repository.dart:138-143) and the web's `completeCustomerProfile` (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts). Every downstream router decision keys off `profileComplete`: app splash via `isProfileComplete()` (auth_repository.dart:100-110), the app OTP screen via `ensureCustomerDoc`, and the web via `needsProfile: !profileComplete` -> `router.replace('/create-profile')` (web/src/app/(auth)/signin/page.tsx:72).
findings.failure_scenario: User taps "Skip" at signup, then later fills in their full name and email on Profile -> Edit profile and saves. `profileComplete` stays false. On their next app login the OTP screen routes them to Create Profile again with empty fields, and signing in on the web immediately redirects them to /create-profile even though the account already has a name and email.
findings.fix: Have `_save()` write `profileComplete: true` and the recomputed `searchIndex` alongside name/email (both fields are permitted by the customers update rule at firebase/firestore.rules:135-136), or reuse `AuthRepository.completeProfile`.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed — I could not find any guard, fallback or server-side re-check that rescues this.

1. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/profile/edit_profile_screen.dart:77-81 writes exactly `{name, email, updatedAt}`. `grep -rn profileComplete app/lib` returns only 4 hits (auth_repository.dart:92, 106, 138, 214) — nothing in the profile feature, so no other app code sets it after an edit.

2. The doc is created with an explicit `'profileComplete': false` (auth_repository.dart:214), so the name-based fallback in `isProfileComplete()` (`if (complete != null) return complete;` at :106-109) never fires — the field is non-null false, and the `name` fallback is dead for these users.

3. The Edit-profile entry point is ungated: profile_screen.dart:176 `context.push(Routes.editProfile)` is an unconditional icon tap, so a user who tapped Skip (create_profile_screen.dart:63-66) reaches it fine.

4. Downstream routing really does key off the flag:
   - app OTP: otp_screen.dart:101-104 `final complete = await repo.ensureCustomerDoc(e164); context.go(complete ? Routes.home : Routes.createProfile)` — `ensureCustomerDoc` returns the raw `profileComplete` (auth_repository.dart:92), no name fallback. Re-login sends them to Create Profile, which starts with empty controllers and has `PopScope(canPop: false)`.
   - web: authActions.ts:88-90 `needsProfile: !profileComplete` → signin/page.tsx:72 `router.replace(needsProfile ? '/create-profile' : '/')`.
   The app splash (splash_screen.dart:53-56) does OR in the local `AppPrefs.profileSkipped()` pref, but that is device-local and only covers the splash path — it does not cover the OTP path (fresh login / reinstall / other device) or the web at all.

5. The write is permitted, so this is fixable in place: firebase/firestore.rules:134 lists both `profileComplete` and `searchIndex` in the owner-update `onlyFields` allowlist — exactly what `AuthRepository.completeProfile` (auth_repository.dart:134-145) and web `completeCustomerProfile` (customerDoc.ts:107-114) write.

One correction to the claim's framing: the web's own edit screen, web/src/app/(shop)/account/profile/page.tsx:69-73, has the identical omission (no `profileComplete`, no `searchIndex`), so this is a shared gap in both edit surfaces rather than an app-only divergence from web. That makes the "cross-surface-mismatch" label slightly off, and it means the fix should ideally touch both, but it does not refute the defect — the failure scenario (skip at signup, later fill name/email in Edit profile, then get bounced to Create Profile on next app login and to /create-profile on web signin) is real, and the stale `searchIndex` additionally leaves the customer unfindable by name/email in admin search.

findings.title: Reviews screen is unreachable for any product with zero reviews, so no product can ever receive its first app review
findings.detail: `_reviewsSummary(context)` is the ONLY place in the whole app that pushes `/product/:id/reviews` (line 484 — confirmed by grep across app/lib), and it is rendered behind `if (p.ratingCount > 0)` at line 188. Inside it, line 488-489 reads `p.ratingCount > 0 ? 'See all N' : 'Write a review'` — the `'Write a review'` branch is unreachable dead code, because the widget only renders when ratingCount > 0. `products.ratingCount` is only ever incremented when an admin APPROVES a review (admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:59-64) or typed by hand in the product form (ProductFormPage.tsx:223); nothing else writes it, and the web has no review form at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin publishes a new product; `ratingCount` is 0 (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:200). A customer opens the product in the app — there is no 'Ratings & reviews' section and no link to `/product/{id}/reviews`, so `ReviewsScreen` and its fully-working `_WriteReviewSheet` are dead. Because ratingCount only rises after an approved review exists, and the only way to submit one is through that unreachable screen, the product is permanently stuck at 0 reviews. The entire reviews feature is inert for every new product.
findings.fix: Render the reviews section unconditionally (drop the `p.ratingCount > 0` guard at line 188) so the `'Write a review'` label at line 489 becomes reachable; keep the numeric summary block (lines 497-527) behind the ratingCount check if a zero-star block is undesirable.

verdict.reason:
The reachability core of the claim is confirmed, though one supporting fact in it is wrong.

CONFIRMED:
- /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/catalog/product_details_screen.dart:484 is the only push of '/product/:id/reviews' in the entire app (grep over app/lib returns exactly one hit; the only other navigation in that file is line 557, to a related product). No orders screen and no notification deep link reaches it — /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:166-183 handles only 'product' | 'category' | 'home'.
- That push lives inside _reviewsSummary, rendered only under `if (p.ratingCount > 0)` at product_details_screen.dart:188. So for any product with ratingCount == 0 there is no in-app path to ReviewsScreen or its working _WriteReviewSheet.
- The dead-code evidence points to unintended gating rather than design intent: line 487-489 has `p.ratingCount > 0 ? 'See all N' : 'Write a review'` whose false branch can never render, and /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/catalog/reviews_screen.dart:124 (`if (ratingCount == 0) return const SizedBox.shrink();`) plus the :158 empty state "No reviews yet. Be the first to review this product." were written for the zero-review case. Web, which the app is meant to mirror, renders ReviewsSection unconditionally (web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:346) and gates only the star badge on ratingCount > 0 (line 424) while the 'Write a review' button always renders. The app diverges by gating the whole section including the write entry point.
- ratingCount is indeed written only by admin review approval (admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:59-64) and the admin product form (ProductFormPage.tsx:223 / products.ts:131), defaulting to 0 on create (products.ts:200).

WHAT THE CLAIM GETS WRONG (reduces severity, not existence): "the web has no review form at all" is false — web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:436-442 renders a full ReviewForm behind an always-visible 'Write a review' button, so a product is not permanently stuck at zero: a web customer can post the first review, admin approves, ratingCount becomes 1, and the app section then appears. Admin can also hand-set ratingCount. So "the entire reviews feature is inert for every new product" overstates it.

Still a real, fixable functional defect: app-only customers can never submit the first review for a product, and the fix is a reachability change (render the section / write link when ratingCount == 0), not a cosmetic tweak.

findings.title: Timeout-recovery path touches BuildContext after an await with no mounted check, and throws from inside a catch block
findings.detail: `_placeOrder` awaits `_repo.placeOrder` with a 120s callable timeout (checkout_repository.dart:274). On `deadline-exceeded`/`unavailable` it calls `_recoverTimedOutOrder`, whose FIRST statement is `final uid = context.read<AuthProvider>().uid;` (line 147) — before any `mounted` check (the only `if (!mounted)` is at line 153, after the await). `State.context` dereferences `_element!`, which is null once the element is unmounted, so this throws. Worse, it throws from inside the `on FirebaseFunctionsException catch` block, so the following `catch (_)` at line 134 does NOT catch it — the error escapes `_placeOrder` entirely as an unhandled async exception and `_placing` is never reset. Unlike PaymentScreen (payment_screen.dart:218 wraps the body in `PopScope(canPop: !_processing)`), CheckoutScreen has no pop guard, so the user can freely back out during the 120s window.
findings.failure_scenario: User taps 'Place order · ₹1,299' on Checkout; the callable stalls (cold start + poor network). While it is in flight the user taps the back arrow (checkout_screen.dart:227 `context.pop()`), unmounting `_CheckoutScreenState`. 120s later the call fails with `deadline-exceeded`; `_recoverTimedOutOrder` runs, `context.read<AuthProvider>()` dereferences a null element and throws a TypeError that no handler catches. The order may in fact have committed server-side, but the recovery lookup never runs, so nothing tells the user and nothing clears the bag.
findings.fix: Capture the uid before the await (alongside `cart`/`draft` in `_placeOrder`) and pass it into `_recoverTimedOutOrder`, or add `if (!mounted) return false;` as the first line of `_recoverTimedOutOrder`. Additionally wrap the checkout body in `PopScope(canPop: !_placing, ...)` the way PaymentScreen already does.

verdict.reason:
Verified in code; I could not refute it.

1. Mechanism is real. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:116-128 — the `on FirebaseFunctionsException catch (e)` branch calls `await _recoverTimedOutOrder(cart, draft)` with no `mounted` check first, and `_recoverTimedOutOrder` (lines 145-156) starts with `final uid = context.read<AuthProvider>().uid;` at line 147. `State.context` returns `_element!` and `StatefulElement.unmount()` nulls `state._element`, so after the screen is popped this throws (FlutterError in debug, null-check TypeError in release). The only `if (!mounted)` is at line 153, after the Firestore await. Notably `cart` and `draft` ARE correctly captured as locals at lines 95-96 before the await — only the AuthProvider read was left on `context`, so this is a one-line fix (capture uid up front or guard with mounted).

2. The Dart semantics claim holds: a throw inside a `catch` clause is not caught by the sibling `catch (_)` at line 134, so the error escapes `_placeOrder`. `_placeOrder` is passed bare as `onPressed` at line 832, so the Future is discarded and the error becomes an unhandled async error (logged via the zone/FlutterError handler — so "crash-risk" slightly overstates it; the real damage is the lost recovery).

3. Path is reachable with a long window: /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:274 sets `HttpsCallableOptions(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120))`, and the recovery exists precisely because a deadline says nothing about whether the transaction committed (repo comment lines 292-298). CheckoutScreen has no pop guard — grep shows PopScope only in checkout/payment_screen.dart:218, checkout/order_confirmation_screen.dart:94 and auth/create_profile_screen.dart:144 — while the back button at checkout_screen.dart:227 calls `context.pop()` unconditionally even when `_placing` is true.

4. No compensating guard elsewhere: `findOrderByNonce` swallows its own errors but is never reached, and nothing else clears the cart or reconciles the committed order. The consequence is money-adjacent: an order that did commit leaves the bag intact and the customer uninformed, and a fresh CheckoutScreen mints a new `_nonce` (line 41), so the server-side idempotency key no longer protects against a duplicate order. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, and the fix is functional, not UI.

findings.title: placeOrder auto-applies the best coupon server-side, but the app never applies it to the draft — displayed total is higher than what is charged and a spin coupon is silently consumed
findings.detail: `_placeOrder` sends `couponCode: draft.coupon?.code` (line 108), which is null whenever the customer has not tapped 'Apply'. Server-side, `placeOrder` treats a null code as an instruction to auto-apply: `couponCode ? computeCouponDiscount(...) : await autoBestOffer(uid, subtotalPaise)` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:347-349). `autoBestOffer` scans `customers/{uid}/coupons` and marks the winner used (`status:'used'`, checkout.ts:567-572) and increments promo counters. The web client compensates for this: checkout/page.tsx:84-95 has a `useEffect` that auto-applies `bestOfferForCart` into the draft on mount ('Auto-applied best offer'), so its summary matches. The app only renders a passive `CouponRewardBanner` that requires an explicit tap (coupon_apply.dart:85-95); nothing writes the auto-offer into `CheckoutDraft`, so `computeSummary` shows no discount.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer holds a spin reward 'SPIN200 · ₹200 off · min ₹500'. They open Checkout on a ₹1,000 COD cart and ignore the gold banner. The pay bar reads 'Place order · ₹1,000' and the summary shows no Discount row. `placeOrder` runs `autoBestOffer`, applies SPIN200, creates the order at ₹800, and flips the spin coupon to `status:'used'`. The customer sees ₹1,000 on checkout, ₹800 on confirmation, and their one-time spin reward is gone without them ever choosing to spend it.
findings.fix: Mirror the web behaviour: on Checkout, once offers have loaded and `draft.coupon == null` and subtotal > 0, auto-apply `listAvailableOffers(...).firstWhere(qualifies && discount>0)` into `CheckoutDraft` once (guarded by a `_autoTried` flag so a manual removal is respected). Alternatively send an explicit `couponCode: ''`/opt-out flag so the server does not auto-apply behind the UI.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:347-349 explicitly treats a null couponCode as "auto-apply the best available offer" (autoBestOffer, L215-259), and on commit it flips the winning personal coupon to status:'used' with usesCount+1 and writes a spin_reward ledger row (L568-573, L590-600). The web compensates: web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:84-95 has a one-shot useEffect writing bestOfferForCart into the draft ('Auto-applied best offer') so its summary matches. The app does not: grep for setCoupon across app/lib returns only explicit user gestures (coupon_screen.dart:48/69/312, coupon_apply.dart:87/149) — nothing auto-applies. checkout_screen.dart:284-290 computes the summary from draft.coupon (null) so no Discount row, and L104-111 sends couponCode: draft.coupon?.code = null, so the server applies the spin coupon anyway. order_confirmation_screen.dart:91 intentionally renders placed.amountPaise ("what placeOrder actually charged"), so the customer sees a different, lower total than checkout showed, and their one-time spin reward is consumed without them tapping Apply. Not cosmetic: real Firestore state (coupon status:'used', usesCount, wallet ledger) changes without user intent. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Two caveats that do not refute it: (1) the Razorpay path is not overcharged — payment_screen.dart:127-137 opens the gateway with rzp.amountPaise from the server-created order, so the money collected is correct; the defect is the displayed-vs-charged mismatch plus the silent coupon burn. (2) The web mitigation is display-only and one-shot (autoTried ref), so clearing the coupon on web also lets the server re-auto-apply — the root policy is shared, but the app-side omission at checkout_screen.dart:108 is a genuine, fixable cross-surface divergence.

findings.title: findOrderByNonce returns totalPaise as the order amount while the normal path returns payablePaise — recovered orders overstate the COD amount due by the wallet amount
findings.detail: The normal `placeOrder` return maps `amountPaise` from the callable's `summary.payablePaise` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:619, i.e. total AFTER the wallet debit). The just-added recovery path builds `PlacedOrder` from the order document with `amountPaise: (data['totalPaise'] as num?)?.toInt() ?? 0` (line 313) — `totalPaise` is the pre-wallet total (checkout.ts:503; the post-wallet figure is `totalPaise - walletUsedPaise`). `OrderConfirmationScreen` renders this value verbatim as '₹X due on delivery' / '₹X paid' (order_confirmation_screen.dart:92, 204-205). The CF's own idempotency replay has the same defect: it returns `prior.amountPaise`, which was stored as `summary.totalPaise` (checkout.ts:555 vs 619), so payment_screen's retry path is affected too.
findings.failure_scenario: COD order: subtotal ₹1,000, wallet balance ₹400 applied → totalPaise ₹1,000, walletUsedPaise ₹400, payablePaise ₹600. `placeOrder` times out but commits. `_recoverTimedOutOrder` finds it via `findOrderByNonce` and routes to confirmation, which displays '₹1,000 due on delivery' instead of ₹600 — telling the customer to hand the delivery agent ₹400 more than they owe. Same wrong figure appears after a cancelled-then-retried Razorpay payment, where the CF replay returns totalPaise.
findings.fix: In `findOrderByNonce`, compute `amountPaise: (totalPaise - walletUsedPaise).clamp(0, totalPaise)` reading both fields from the order doc. Also change the CF replay return (checkout.ts:386) to store/return `payablePaise` so the replay shape matches the first-placement shape.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; I could not refute it. (1) Normal path: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:619 returns amountPaise: summary.payablePaise (post-wallet), mapped straight into PlacedOrder at checkout_repository.dart:287. (2) Recovery path: checkout_repository.dart:313 uses data['totalPaise']; the order doc (checkout.ts:496-504) stores totalPaise (pre-wallet) plus separate walletUsedPaise and amountPaidPaise, and has NO payablePaise field — so the recovered figure is overstated by walletUsedPaise. (3) Reachable with wallet applied: checkout_screen.dart:809-832 keeps COD with payable>0 on this screen and calls _placeOrder with useWallet: draft.useWallet; the pay bar shows payablePaise ("Place order · ₹600"), then on deadline-exceeded _recoverTimedOutOrder (checkout_screen.dart:145-155) pushes the recovered PlacedOrder to confirmation. (4) No downstream guard/re-derivation: order_confirmation_screen.dart:92 uses widget.order?.amountPaise verbatim in _amountChip (lines 204-206, "₹X due on delivery" / "₹X paid"); its only order-doc read is for cashbackPaise. (5) The CF replay half is real too: the idempotency doc stores amountPaise: summary.totalPaise (checkout.ts:555) and the replay branch returns Number(prior.amountPaise) (checkout.ts:386), inconsistent with :619 (it also omits paymentMethod). The actual Razorpay charge is safe because createRazorpayOrder recomputes o.totalPaise - o.walletUsedPaise server-side (checkout.ts:666) — only the displayed/returned amount is wrong. Not cosmetic: the fix is data-layer (compute totalPaise - walletUsedPaise, both fields present; align the CF idempotency/replay value), no widget changes, and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Caveat that doesn't rescue it: in the fully-wallet-paid case the two paths still disagree, just in the opposite direction (recovery shows totalPaise "paid", normal path shows ₹0).

findings.title: Spin-coupon discount is counted twice in the order detail and invoice totals
findings.detail: `placeOrder` derives spinRewardPaise FROM discountPaise, it is not an additional reduction: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:352-353 `const spinRewardPaise = userCouponId && userCouponSource === 'spin' ? Math.max(0, discountPaise) : 0;` and the order doc is then written with `discountPaise: summary.discountPaise` (checkout.ts:497) and `spinRewardPaise` (checkout.ts:498), where `summarise()` returns the same discountPaise it was given unchanged (checkout.ts:302).
