The app treats them as two independent reductions and adds them: `deductionPaise => discountPaise + spinRewardPaise + walletUsedPaise` (order.dart:189) and `discountsExWalletPaise => discountPaise + spinRewardPaise` (order.dart:194). Those getters drive the only money-reduction line on both money screens: order_detail_screen.dart:396-400 ("Discounts applied") and invoice_screen.dart:179-180 (the single deduction line on the tax invoice).
findings.failure_scenario: Customer wins a spin coupon and redeems it for Rs 100 off a Rs 1000 order. Firestore stores discountPaise=10000 and spinRewardPaise=10000 (same money). Order detail shows 'Discounts applied -Rs 200.00' and the invoice shows 'Discount + Spin reward -Rs 200.00', i.e. double the discount the customer actually received, while 'Total paid' still shows the real total - the invoice no longer reconciles.
findings.fix: Treat spinRewardPaise as a labelling flag, not an amount: make `deductionPaise => discountPaise + walletUsedPaise` and `discountsExWalletPaise => discountPaise`, and use `spinRewardPaise > 0` only to choose the label ('Spin reward' vs 'Discount'). Alternatively stop writing the duplicate value in checkout.ts and make spinRewardPaise a disjoint component.

verdict.reason:
Verified end-to-end; I could not refute it.

Server side (/home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts): `const spinRewardPaise = userCouponId && userCouponSource === 'spin' ? Math.max(0, discountPaise) : 0;` (line 352-353) derives the value FROM discountPaise. `summarise()` returns `discountPaise` untouched (line 302 `return { subtotalPaise, discountPaise, ... }`), and the order doc is written with BOTH `discountPaise: summary.discountPaise` and `spinRewardPaise` (lines 497-498). `appliedCoupon.discountPaise` is also `summary.discountPaise`, so discountPaise definitively already contains the spin coupon's money. The CF's own comments confirm spinRewardPaise is a derived tally, not a second reduction: line 350-351 "Spin/wheel coupon savings realised at checkout feed the wallet 'Rewards' tally (a running total of reward value, not a spendable balance credit)" and line 587-589 on the ledger row "It records reward *value* earned, not a balance movement, so balanceAfterPaise is the balance after this order (unchanged by the reward)". It only increments `wallet.breakdown.rewardsPaise` (line 451), never `wallet.balancePaise`.

Reachability: real, not a dead path. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:135 writes `customers/{uid}/coupons` docs with `source: 'spin'`, and both `computeCouponDiscount` (returns `userCouponSource: c.source`) and `autoBestOffer` propagate that source, so any spin coupon (explicitly entered or auto-applied) produces discountPaise == spinRewardPaise != 0.

Client side (/home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:189 and :194) adds them as independent reductions, and those getters are the sole money-reduction lines on both money surfaces: /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:396-400 ("Discounts applied" uses discountsExWalletPaise) and /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:179-180 (single deduction line, label built at :229-233 as "Discount + Spin reward"). The invoice prints line items, then that deduction, then tax, then "Total paid" (order.paidPaise, taken straight from amountPaidPaise/totalPaise), so the printed tax invoice genuinely fails to reconcile by exactly the spin discount.

No guard, fallback or normalizer exists: grep for spinRewardPaise across functions/admin/web shows no other writer or sanitiser (seed.ts always writes 0). This is not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, and it is not cosmetic — it is a wrong money figure on a tax invoice; the fix is in the data-model getters (drop spinRewardPaise from both sums), not in layout.

Only caveat: the claim's category label "cross-surface-mismatch" is slightly off — web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:54 makes the same `discountPaise + spinRewardPaise + walletUsedPaise` mistake, and web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:155-156 shows a separate "Spin reward" row alongside the discount row, so the web double-counts too. That broadens the defect rather than refuting it.

findings.title: seed writes spin-slice `discountPercent` as a fraction (0.15) while admin/app/web/CF all treat it as an integer percent
findings.detail: scripts/seed.ts:747 seeds slice `s2` as `{ prizeType:'percent_discount', discountPercent: 0.15, displayLabel:'15% off' }`. Every reader treats the field as whole percent: admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:73 (`percent: s.discountPercent`) and rowToSlice writes `Number(r.percent)` straight from a `%` number input; functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:170-171 computes `Math.round(subtotal * pct / 100)`; web/src/components/wallet/actions.ts:122 renders `${c.discountPercent}% off`; and the app parses it through `_int()` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_campaign.dart:48 and app/lib/features/coupons/data/user_coupon.dart:102), where `(0.15).toInt() == 0`. `executeSpin` copies the slice value verbatim onto the issued coupon (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:132).
findings.failure_scenario: On the seeded dataset a customer spins and lands on the '15% off' slice. `executeSpin` writes `customers/{uid}/coupons/{id}` with `discountPercent: 0.15`. My Coupons renders `UserCoupon.headline` as "0% off" (0.15 truncated by `_int`), the checkout offer list (app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:63) computes `pct = 0` so the coupon shows a ₹0 discount, and the server applies `Math.round(subtotal * 0.15 / 100)` ≈ ₹0.15 on a ₹1000 cart instead of ₹150. Web shows "0.15% off".
findings.fix: Change scripts/seed.ts:747 to `discountPercent: 15` (and audit any other seeded percent fields for the same 0..1 vs 0..100 scale). Optionally have `SpinSlice.fromMap`/`UserCoupon.fromDoc` round rather than truncate so bad data degrades visibly instead of silently becoming 0.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; found no guard, fallback, or normalization anywhere. Whole-percent is the repo-wide convention: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:170-171, :191, :232, :250 all compute Math.round(subtotalPaise * Number(c.discountPercent) / 100); web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:46,61 does the same; app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:63-64 does `pct = _num(...); d = (subtotalPaise * pct / 100).round()` with `_num` (lines 32-38) returning `v.toInt()`. Admin writes whole percent from a `%` number input (admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:91 `Number(r.percent)`; admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:101 default slice `discountPercent: 10` for '10% off'). The seed itself uses whole percent everywhere else (scripts/seed.ts:357 product discountPercent; :775 flash-sale `discountPercent: 30`). scripts/seed.ts:747 writes `discountPercent: 0.15` with `displayLabel:'15% off'` — the only fractional value in the codebase. functions/src/spin/execute.ts:132 copies `slice.discountPercent` verbatim onto customers/{uid}/coupons/{id} with discountType 'percent', with no scaling and no re-derivation from couponTemplateCode, so the bad value reaches the money path: a Rs 1000 cart yields Math.round(100000*0.15/100) = 150 paise (Rs 1.50) instead of Rs 150, and the app truncates 0.15 to 0 (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_campaign.dart:3,48; app/lib/features/coupons/data/user_coupon.dart:102) so the offer computes a zero discount. Functional money defect, not cosmetic. Same mistake appears a second time in the same file: scripts/seed.ts:703 seeds public coupon EID15 with `pct: 0.15` (written at :714), hitting the checkout.ts:170 global-coupon path. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, and no test depends on the fractional value (e2e/tests/admin/coupons.spec.ts:40 only checks codes exist; the web coupon specs seed discountPercent: null). One-line fix in each place (0.15 -> 15).

findings.title: Wishlist grid renders every saved product as "Out of stock" and its quick-add button is permanently inert
findings.detail: `WishlistItem.toProduct()` (wishlist.dart:81-95) rebuilds a `Product` from the denormalised wishlist snapshot but never passes `stock`, `hasVariants` or `variants`. `Product`'s constructor defaults them to `stock = 0`, `hasVariants = false`, `variants = const []` (app/lib/features/catalog/data/product.dart:50-53), and `Product.inStock` is `hasVariants ? variants.any(...) : stock > 0` (product.dart:85) — so every wishlist-derived Product is `inStock == false`. WishlistScreen feeds exactly this object to `ProductCard` (wishlist_screen.dart:83-88). ProductCard reacts to `!product.inStock` by painting the white dimming scrim + red "Out of stock" badge (product_card.dart:181-207) and `_AddButton` short-circuits to an inert `Icons.block_rounded` container with NO onTap (product_card.dart:281-292). The wishlist snapshot doc genuinely has no stock field (web writes the same shape, web/src/lib/wishlist.ts:38-55), so the data must be re-read from `products/{id}` — the web wishlist page sidesteps this by using its own WishlistCard that has no stock state at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer taps the heart on an in-stock perfume (stock 40), opens Profile ▸ Wishlist. The card is greyed out with an "Out of stock" badge and the green quick-add `+` is replaced by a dead block icon. Tapping it does nothing — the item can only be bought by opening the detail page. The same product on Home/Category shows in-stock and adds to bag fine.
findings.fix: Either persist `stock`/`hasVariants` in the wishlist snapshot payload (both app and web writers) and pass them through `toProduct()`, or have WishlistScreen resolve each id against the live `products` docs (e.g. `CatalogRepository.productsByIds`) before handing them to ProductCard.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all links. wishlist.dart:81-95 builds Product without stock/hasVariants/variants, so product.dart:54-55 defaults them to 0/false/[] and product.dart:87 makes inStock always false. wishlist_screen.dart:83-88 is the sole consumer and passes that object directly to ProductCard, which at product_card.dart:179-213 paints the dimming scrim + "Out of stock" badge and at 284-295 returns an inert Icons.block_rounded container with no onTap. No fallback exists: WishlistRepository.watch maps docs straight through, WishlistProvider never reads products/{id}, and the web writer (web/src/lib/wishlist.ts snapshotOf) stores no stock field, so the data is genuinely absent. Seeded products do have stock (scripts/seed.ts:360), so the same product is in-stock and quick-addable on Home/Category. The only re-read is on the detail page (product_details_screen.dart:49-50 streams the real doc with the stale Product as initialData), which corrects itself there but does nothing for the wishlist grid — matching the claimed failure scenario. The toProduct() doc comment explicitly says the rebuilt Product is "enough to render a ProductCard and quick-add to the bag", so the state is unintended, not architectural. It is a dead interactive control (functional), not purely cosmetic, and is not among the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL exclusions.

findings.title: Categories tab re-subscribes an unbounded whole-catalog listener on every keystroke of the category search box
findings.detail: Both `stream: _repo.categories()` (line 73) and the nested `stream: _repo.categoryCounts()` (line 97) are constructed inside `build()`. The search field's `onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _query = v)` (line 178) rebuilds the whole screen on every character typed, producing new Stream objects each time, so both StreamBuilders tear down and re-listen. `CatalogRepository.categoryCounts()` (app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:65) is `products.where('status','published').snapshots()` with NO `limit` — a full-collection real-time listener over the entire published catalog. Filtering is purely in-memory (`_filter`, line 53), so re-subscribing gains nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: User opens Categories, taps search and types 'sweets' (6 characters). Each keystroke re-issues both listens; the app performs 6 extra full reads of the `categories` collection AND 6 extra full reads of every published product document just to filter a locally-held list. On a 2,000-product catalog that is ~12,000 extra document reads for one search term, plus the grid flashing back to `_CategoriesSkeleton` (line 79) each time `snap.hasData` resets to false.
findings.fix: Make both streams `late final` fields (as `SearchScreen` already does at app/lib/features/search/search_screen.dart:49-50) so they are created once per State, and add a bounded/aggregate strategy for `categoryCounts()` instead of listening to the whole `products` collection.

verdict.reason: Core mechanism confirmed. In app/lib/features/catalog/categories_screen.dart both `stream: _repo.categories()` (line 73) and `stream: _repo.categoryCounts()` (line 97) build a fresh stream object inside build(), and `onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _query = v)` (line 178) rebuilds on every character. Flutter's StreamBuilderBase.didUpdateWidget (flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/async.dart:111-119) unsubscribes and re-subscribes whenever stream identity changes, so each keystroke really does tear down and re-establish both listeners. CatalogRepository.categoryCounts() (data/catalog_repository.dart:65-69) is genuinely unbounded — it is the only query in that repository with no `limit` (products() max 120, productsInCategory() max 120, search() limit 25). Filtering is purely in-memory (_filter, line 53), so re-subscribing gains nothing. Decisively, the codebase already contains the correct idiom for this exact situation: search_screen.dart:47-50 hoists the same two streams into `late final` fields with the comment "Live catalog streams, subscribed once and filtered in-memory as the user types", and order_tracking_screen.dart:28-29 does likewise — so categories_screen is an oversight, not an intentional design choice, and it is not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items. Screen is reachable (app_router.dart:388). Two sub-claims are overstated but do not refute the finding: (a) the "grid flashes back to _CategoriesSkeleton" claim is FALSE — StreamBuilder.afterDisconnected/afterConnected use `inState(...)` (async.dart:436,453) which preserves the previous data, and the State is reused, so snap.hasData stays true; (b) the "~12,000 extra document reads" figure is likely inflated because Firestore mobile persistence resume tokens usually avoid re-billing a full query on rapid re-listen. The residual defect is still real and functional (repeated listener teardown/re-listen of an unbounded whole-catalog stream per keystroke, plus the inner counts StreamBuilder being fully disposed and losing its counts whenever an intermediate query matches zero categories, briefly rendering the always-zero stored `category.productCount`). Fix is a non-UI two-line hoist to `late final` fields.

findings.title: Rewards coupon "Apply" is a dead button — /bag never reads the ?coupon= param
findings.detail: `applyCode()` navigates to `/bag?coupon=<CODE>`. It is wired to both the manual code input (Apply button + Enter key, lines 227/232) and to every `CouponCard`'s Apply button (line 266). But `web/src/app/(shop)/bag/page.tsx` never calls `useSearchParams()` — a repo-wide grep for `useSearchParams`/`searchParams.get` returns only spin/result, addresses/new and orders/[id]/return. The bag page's only coupon path is its own local `code` state + `applyCoupon()` (bag/page.tsx:47-63), which is seeded from an empty `useState('')`. The query string is therefore parsed by nothing and silently discarded.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer wins SPIN-7Q2KX on the wheel, opens Account ▸ Rewards, taps Apply on the coupon card. The browser navigates to /bag?coupon=SPIN-7Q2KX, the bag renders with an empty "Enter coupon code" field, no coupon banner, and the order summary shows no discount. The coupon appears to have been applied (the click did something) but no `applyCoupon` callable ever ran.
findings.fix: In bag/page.tsx read the param (`const preset = useSearchParams().get('coupon')`) inside a `<Suspense>` boundary and, on mount, run the existing `callApplyCoupon(preset, lines)` path (or at minimum `setCode(preset)`), then strip the param via `router.replace('/bag')`.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; could not refute. (1) /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:95-99 — applyCode() only does router.push(`/bag?coupon=${encodeURIComponent(trimmed)}`), and it is the sole handler for the manual code input (Enter, line 227; Apply button, line 232) and for every coupon ticket (CouponCard onApply, line 266). Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not an architecture-rule artifact (callApplyCoupon already exists and is invoked correctly from the bag's own field), and not cosmetic: the click navigates but never runs callApplyCoupon, so no discount is ever applied. Fix is behavioural — have /bag read the `coupon` param and run its existing applyCoupon flow.

findings.title: Wallet history rows render a blank title for top-ups, cancellation refunds and spin cashback
findings.detail: The row is rendered with `title={tx.title}` and `TxRow` prints it raw (components/wallet/TxRow.tsx:44). `WalletTransaction.title` is declared non-optional (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:162), but three of the six writers never set it: functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:97-101 (source 'topup') writes only `description: 'Wallet top-up'`; functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:116-126 (source 'refund') writes only `description: 'Refund for cancelled order …'`; functions/src/spin/execute.ts:143-147 (source 'spin_reward' cashback) writes only `description: 'Spin & Win cashback'`. Only checkout.ts, adjust.ts and returns/decisions.ts set `title`. The Flutter app handles this explicitly — app/lib/features/wallet/data/wallet.dart:71-86 has `displayTitle` with a per-source fallback ('Added to wallet', 'Refund · #ORD-…', etc.) — so the two surfaces disagree on the same collection.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer tops up ₹500 (verifyTopUp writes the ledger row) and opens Account ▸ Wallet. The row shows the icon and "+₹500.00" with an empty bold title line and only the date underneath; the same transaction reads "Added to wallet" in the app. Identical blank rows appear for every wallet refund from a cancelled order and every spin cashback credit.
findings.fix: Mirror the app's fallback in the web reader — add a `txTitle(tx)` helper in components/wallet/actions.ts switching on `tx.source` (topup/refund/spin_reward/cashback/order_payment/withdrawal/admin_adjust) with `tx.title || tx.description || <source label>` — and/or add the missing `title` field to the three Cloud Function writers.

verdict.reason: Claim verified end to end. Three of the six walletTransactions writers omit the non-optional `title` field declared at packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:162 — functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:96-101 (source 'topup'), functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:115-126 (source 'refund'), functions/src/spin/execute.ts:142-147 (source 'spin_reward'); each writes only `description`. The web page (web/src/app/(shop)/account/wallet/page.tsx:188) passes `title={tx.title}` straight into TxRow, which prints it raw at web/src/components/wallet/TxRow.tsx:44 with no default or placeholder. I checked every possible fallback and found none: txVisual() in web/src/components/wallet/actions.ts:168 returns only icon/bg/fg/amountClass, the subtitle is built solely from date + orderShortId, and no Firestore trigger backfills the field. The remaining two surfaces reading the same collection BOTH guard against it — app/lib/features/wallet/data/wallet.dart:71-86 has `displayTitle` with per-source fallbacks, and admin/src/features/customers/routes/CustomerProfilePage.tsx:370 renders `{t.title || cap(t.source)}` — so this is an unambiguous cross-surface mismatch, not a deliberate style. The path is reachable (cancelOrder and adminChangeOrderStatus both hit the refund ledger write), and it is not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. It is not merely cosmetic: the row is the only identifier of a money movement in an immutable financial ledger, and the correct fix is server-side — set `title` in the three CFs the way checkout.ts, adjust.ts and returns/decisions.ts already do — requiring no UI change. Note scripts/seed.ts:536 does write `title`, which is why seeded local data masks the bug.

findings.title: Web withdrawal always pays the first bank account; no way to pick, default or delete one
findings.detail: The payout bank is fixed: `bankAccounts.find(b => b.isDefault) ?? bankAccounts[0]`, and `bank.id` is what gets sent to `requestWithdrawal` (line 66). The only bank write in the whole web app is banks/new/page.tsx:61, which hardcodes `isDefault: banks.length === 0` and appends. A repo-wide grep for `bankAccounts` in web/src returns only these three read sites plus affiliate/page.tsx:103 — there is no set-default, no delete, and no selector. Yet the UI offers "Change" (withdraw/page.tsx:156) and "Add new bank account" (affiliate/referral/page.tsx:111), both of which link to /account/banks/new. The Flutter app does have a picker: app/lib/features/affiliate/affiliate_withdraw_screen.dart:266 opens `_pickBank` whenever `banks.length > 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: Affiliate saves HDFC ••4821 (becomes isDefault), later closes that account and taps "Change" → adds ICICI ••9930. The new record is written with isDefault:false, so `find(isDefault)` still resolves to HDFC. The withdraw screen keeps showing HDFC, and Confirm withdrawal files a payout to the closed account. The customer can never route money to the new bank from the web.
findings.fix: Add a bank list/selector on the withdraw screen (local `selectedBankId` state seeded from the default, like the app), plus set-default and delete actions that rewrite the `bankAccounts` array — the customers update rule already whitelists `bankAccounts` (firebase/firestore.rules:135).

verdict.reason: Verified; the claim holds and nothing rescues it elsewhere. (1) web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:29 fixes the payout bank to `find(b => b.isDefault) ?? bankAccounts[0]` and line 66 sends `bankAccountId: bank.id`; there is no selector state and no bank-picker component anywhere in web (grep over web/src/components and web/src/lib hits only customerDoc.ts and wallet/actions.ts). (2) The only write to bankAccounts in the whole web app is web/src/app/(shop)/account/banks/new/page.tsx:61-69, appending `isDefault: banks.length === 0` via `bankAccounts: [...banks, record]` — nothing ever flips isDefault on an existing entry or removes one. (3) web/src/app/(shop)/account/banks/ contains only `new/` — no list page, so /account/banks 404s; both the "Change" link (withdraw/page.tsx:156) and "Add new bank account" (affiliate/referral/page.tsx:112) go to /account/banks/new, which can only append another non-default record. (4) No server-side rescue: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts accepts the client's bankAccountId and only checks `banks.find(b => b.id === bankAccountId)` exists, then snapshots that bank's IFSC/last4 onto the withdrawalRequests doc — the stale client pick is what admin pays out. (5) Not a cross-surface false alarm: the Flutter app avoids it with a per-withdrawal picker (app/lib/features/affiliate/affiliate_withdraw_screen.dart:266 `_pickBank` when banks.length > 1), and even the app never writes isDefault on an existing record (the sole occurrence in app/lib is the read at line 102) — so no surface can change the default, and a web-only affiliate is permanently locked to their first-saved bank. (6) Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item and not an architecture-rule artifact (bank list is an owner-owned array on customers/{uid}, direct-write by design). The failure is functional, not cosmetic: real money (netPayoutPaise) is filed against a bank account the customer can no longer change or delete from the web.

findings.title: Removing an applied coupon is a no-op server-side — placeOrder auto-applies the best offer anyway and burns a one-time reward
findings.detail: placeOrder sends `couponCode: draft.coupon?.code ?? null` (line 176). On the server, a null couponCode does not mean "no discount" — it triggers autoBestOffer() (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:349), which scans promo + personal coupons and applies the largest one, marks a personal coupon `status: 'used'` (line 567) and writes the spin-reward ledger row. The web "Remove" button (line 337) just clears the local draft, and the auto-apply effect is one-shot (`autoTried`, line 89), so the UI then shows and charges no discount while the server does.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer has a spin coupon SPIN100 (₹100 off, single use). Checkout auto-applies it, user presses Remove because they want to save it for a bigger order. Summary shows To pay ₹1000. placeOrder sends couponCode null → autoBestOffer picks SPIN100 → order total ₹900 and the coupon is flipped to 'used'. For Razorpay the modal then asks for ₹900, not the ₹1000 shown; the reward the customer explicitly declined is consumed permanently.
findings.fix: Send an explicit "no coupon" signal (e.g. a `noCoupon: true` flag or an empty-string sentinel the server treats as 'skip autoBestOffer'), so an intentional removal suppresses the server-side auto-apply.

verdict.reason: Confirmed end-to-end; no guard rescues the removal. (1) web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:176 sends `couponCode: draft.coupon?.code ?? null`; the Remove button (~line 336) only does `draft.set({ coupon: null })`, and the auto-apply effect is one-shot (`autoTried.current = true`, ~line 89, comment literally says "respect a manual removal"), so the client then shows and computes a zero discount. (2) functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:347-349 treats null as "pick the best offer": `couponCode ? computeCouponDiscount(...) : autoBestOffer(uid, subtotalPaise)`. autoBestOffer (line 215) scans active promos (targetUsers 'all', autoApply !== false) plus ALL active personal coupons under customers/{uid}/coupons and returns the largest. (3) The effects are server-side writes, not cosmetics: the personal coupon is flipped to `status:'used'` with usedOnOrderId (~line 567), wallet.breakdown.rewardsPaise is incremented, a spin_reward walletTransactions ledger row is written, and the order's totalPaise/discountPaise are the discounted values — the Razorpay order is then created from the server amount (callCreateRazorpayOrder on res.orderId), so the modal collects a different figure than the "To pay" the customer approved. (4) There is no opt-out channel: PlaceOrderSchema (line 331) is `z.string().nullable().optional()`, an empty string is falsy and also routes to autoBestOffer, and computeCouponDiscount throws not-found for any dummy sentinel, so no client can express "deliberately no coupon". The Flutter app has the identical shape (app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:108, checkout_repository.dart:260+), so this is a cross-surface gap rather than a web-only slip. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item and not mandated by the architecture rules (money logic correctly lives in the CF; the missing piece is an explicit-decline signal, e.g. a `noCoupon` flag honoured before autoBestOffer).

findings.title: Web never checks firstOrderOnly / maxUsesPerUser / maxUsesTotal / active, so it auto-applies coupons that placeOrder hard-rejects
findings.detail: promoDiscount() (lines 36-51) and listAvailableOffers() (lines 110-126) filter only on status/targetUsers/autoApply/expiry/min. The server's authoritative computeCouponDiscount() additionally rejects on `active === false` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:135), `usesCount >= maxUsesTotal` (line 149), per-user redemptions via customers/{uid}/couponUsage (lines 152-155) and `firstOrderOnly` against stats.totalOrders (lines 156-161) — each as a thrown HttpsError, not a silent skip. Because the checkout page auto-applies the best offer into draft.coupon (line 92) and then passes that code explicitly, the strict path always runs.
findings.failure_scenario: Seeded WELCOME30 has firstOrderOnly: true and maxUsesPerUser: 1. A returning customer with 3 past orders opens /checkout: WELCOME30 is auto-applied and shown as "Best offer applied". Every "Place order" click fails with 'This coupon is for first orders only.' — the customer cannot check out at all until they discover the Remove link, and the toast never says which coupon is at fault.
findings.fix: Mirror the server's eligibility rules client-side (skip coupons with active===false, usesCount>=maxUsesTotal, firstOrderOnly when the customer has prior orders), and on a placeOrder coupon error clear draft.coupon automatically so the retry can succeed.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute it and could not — the dead-end is real, though the report's chosen illustration is the one check that is currently inert.

Reachability, verified end to end:
- /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:85-95 auto-applies `bestOfferForCart(...)` into `draft.coupon` with no server round-trip, and :176 passes `couponCode: draft.coupon?.code` to `placeOrder`. `applyOffer` (:102-105) is likewise client-only. Only the manual code box (:146-160) goes through the `applyCoupon` CF. So the strict server path does run on an offer the client never validated.
- /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:59 allows any signed-in user to read `coupons`, so `promoCoupons` is genuinely populated — the path is not unreachable.
- /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:135-161 throws HttpsError (not a silent skip) on `active === false`, `usesCount >= maxUsesTotal`, `maxUsesPerUser` via `customers/{uid}/couponUsage`, and `firstOrderOnly`. /home/h/barkath/web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:36-51 and :110-126 check none of these. There is no fallback: page.tsx:215-217 just toasts `errMessage(e, ...)` — it does not clear the coupon or retry, so the customer is stuck on "Place order" until they find Remove.

The strongest reproducible instance is maxUsesPerUser, not firstOrderOnly: every admin-created coupon is written with `maxUsesPerUser: 1` (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:144) and the seed sets it too (scripts/seed.ts:717), while placeOrder increments `customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{couponId}` on every redemption (checkout.ts:604-613). So a customer who checks out once with an auto-applied promo hits 'You have already used this coupon.' on their very next checkout, with the same coupon re-auto-applied for them.

Correction to the report: the firstOrderOnly scenario as written does NOT fire. checkout.ts:158 reads `stats.totalOrders`, and nothing in the repo ever writes that field — customers carry `stats.ordersCount` (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:93, scripts/seed.ts:465), so the guard always sees 0. `active === false` is also near-redundant since admin keeps `status` in sync (coupons.ts:92-95, 135). maxUsesPerUser and maxUsesTotal are the live ones.

Related same-root mismatch worth folding into the fix: offers.ts gates the minimum on `minOrderPaise`, but admin and seed write `minCartValuePaise` (coupons.ts:128, seed.ts:716) and the server checks `minCartValuePaise` (checkout.ts:143) — so a below-minimum cart also auto-applies client-side and then hard-rejects at placeOrder. Note also that the server's own no-code `autoBestOffer` (checkout.ts:215-259) skips all of these limits, so the same coupon is silently allowed when no code is sent and hard-rejected when it is — the divergence is inside the server too, not only across surfaces.

This is functional, not cosmetic: the customer cannot complete an order.

findings.title: Return item picker silently submits the first eligible item when the customer never selects a radio
findings.detail: `itemId` initialises to `preItemId ?? ''` (line 84). When the customer arrives via the OrderCard "Return" link there is no `?itemId=` param, so `preItemId` is null and `itemId` is `''`. With more than one eligible item `showPicker` is true (line 125) and every radio renders unchecked. `submit()` then does `const targetItemId = itemId || selectedItem?.id;` (line 93), and `selectedItem` falls through to `eligible[0]` (line 90). Nothing forces a selection and no validation error is raised for an unpicked item — only the reason is validated (line 98).
findings.failure_scenario: Delivered order with 3 items. Customer clicks "Return" on the order card, the picker lists all 3 with none selected, they scroll past it, choose reason "Item damaged", and hit Submit. A return request is created against item #1 (the first in the array) instead of the item they meant. The toast says "Return request submitted." and the wrong item is stamped `returnStatus: 'requested'`, blocking a fresh request for it while the actually-damaged item is still marked returnable.
findings.fix: When `showPicker` is true, require an explicit selection: default `itemId` to `eligible[0].id` (and render that radio checked) or add `if (!itemId) { toast.error('Select an item to return.'); return; }` before the reason check.

verdict.reason:
Verified end-to-end; the claim holds.

1. Both entry points omit `?itemId=`: /home/h/barkath/web/src/components/account/OrderCard.tsx:56 (`href={`/account/orders/${order.id}/return`}`) and /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:243 (same href). A grep of web/src finds no caller anywhere that passes an itemId query param, so `preItemId` is always null in practice.

2. In the return page: `itemId` starts as `preItemId ?? ''` (line 84); `showPicker = !preItemId && eligible.length > 1` (line 125) so the picker renders with every radio unchecked (`checked={itemId === it.id}` against `''`); `selectedItem` falls through to `eligible[0]` (line 90); `submit()` does `const targetItemId = itemId || selectedItem?.id;` (line 93). The only guards are truthiness of targetItemId — never empty, since the component early-returns when `eligible.length === 0 && items.length > 0` (line 117) — and reasonKey (line 98). Nothing forces a selection.

3. No server-side rescue. `requestReturn` (/home/h/barkath/web/src/components/account/orders.ts:313) just forwards the payload. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/returns/requests.ts trusts `itemId` verbatim: it locates that exact line item (embedded array or legacy subcollection), computes refundAmountPaise from that item's lineTotal, writes the orderRequests doc with that itemSnapshot, and stamps `returnStatus: 'requested'` on it. It only rejects an item already in flight — it cannot detect that the wrong item was picked.

4. Not a KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not architecture-mandated, not cosmetic: the consequence is a wrong Firestore write (wrong item stamped requested, wrong refund amount, actually-damaged item still returnable). The fix is a logic guard in `submit()` (require an explicit selection when the picker is shown), not a UI redesign.

Side note that does not affect this verdict: the CF enforces a hard 3-day window from `deliveredAt` while the web gate uses the admin-configured window (default 7 days) — a separate mismatch, not a mitigation.

findings.title: Return page treats items with a missing returnStatus as already-returned, dead-ending legacy orders
findings.detail: `eligible` is `items.filter((it) => it.returnStatus === 'none' || it.returnStatus === 'rejected')` — an item whose `returnStatus` field is absent is excluded. Every other surface treats absent as eligible: `hasReturnableItem` in web/src/components/account/orders.ts:242 is `!x.returnStatus || x.returnStatus === 'none' || x.returnStatus === 'rejected'`, and the server (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:64) gates on `if (it.returnStatus && it.returnStatus !== 'none' && it.returnStatus !== 'rejected')`. The legacy `orders/{id}/items` subcollection path in `useOrderItems` exists precisely for pre-migration orders, which are the ones most likely to lack the field.
findings.failure_scenario: A pre-migration delivered order whose subcollection items have no `returnStatus` key. `useOrderItems` loads 2 items from the subcollection; `eligible` is empty while `items.length > 0`, so the page renders the terminal message "Every item in this order already has a return in progress. Check the order for its status." (line 117-123). No form, no way forward — even though the server would happily accept the request and the order detail badge shows no active return.
findings.fix: Change the filter to `!it.returnStatus || it.returnStatus === 'none' || it.returnStatus === 'rejected'`, reusing the existing `hasReturnableItem` predicate so all three surfaces agree.

verdict.reason: I tried to refute it and could not. The asymmetry is real, and every other surface deliberately treats an absent returnStatus as eligible: web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:80 uses `it.returnStatus === 'none' || it.returnStatus === 'rejected'` (absent -> excluded), while web/src/components/account/orders.ts:242 `hasReturnableItem` uses `!x.returnStatus || ...`, and functions/src/returns/requests.ts:64 gates on `if (it.returnStatus && it.returnStatus !== 'none' && ...)` after explicitly resolving the legacy `orders/{id}/items/{itemId}` doc (lines 58-62). Strongest corroboration: app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:321-323 coerces a missing/empty `returnStatus` to `'none'` — that defensive default exists because legacy docs can lack the field, and packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:113 carries `returnStatus: ItemReturnStatus; // was replacementStatus`, i.e. a rename, so pre-rename subcollection items would carry `replacementStatus` instead. Reachability holds end to end: the order-detail page gates the Return link on `returnBadge` (orders.ts:232, requires a truthy returnStatus), so a legacy delivered order with no returnStatus shows the "Return item" link (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:242-247); the return page then loads items through the legacy subcollection branch of `useOrderItems` (orders.ts:121-142), `eligible` is empty with `items.length > 0`, and page.tsx:117-123 renders the terminal "Every item in this order already has a return in progress" panel with no form — even though the CF would accept the request. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic (it blocks a write the customer is entitled to), and fixable by matching `hasReturnableItem`. Medium rather than high only because it is triggerable solely by pre-migration subcollection data (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:481 and scripts/seed.ts:658 always write `returnStatus: 'none'`), so no seed/e2e fixture exercises it — but the architecture rule explicitly requires readers to handle those old orders, and this reader does not.

findings.title: placeOrder writes the `variants` array twice from the same pre-write snapshot when a cart holds two variants of one product, dropping the first variant's stock decrement
findings.detail: `priced` maps 1:1 to the client's `lines`, and the cart keys lines by (productId, variantId) — see `web/src/lib/cart.ts:42-43` (`sameLine = a.productId === productId && a.variantId === variantId`) — so two variants of the same product are two separate lines with the same `productId`. Line 403 then does `Promise.all(priced.map(l => tx.get(db.doc('products/'+l.productId))))`, producing two independent snapshots of the *same* document, both holding the pre-transaction `variants` array. The forEach at 428-442 rebuilds `variants` from its own snapshot each iteration (line 433 `((p.variants) ?? []).map(v => ({...v}))`) and issues a second full-array `tx.update` at line 437. The two writes target one document in one transaction: the later whole-array write overwrites the earlier one, so only the last variant's decrement survives (and if the backend instead rejects two writes to one doc per transaction, checkout fails outright for such carts). Meanwhile `stock: FieldValue.increment(-qty)` is a transform and accumulates for both lines, so the top-level aggregate and the variants array also diverge. `orders/cancel.ts:88-96` restocks with the identical pattern and has the same defect in reverse.
findings.failure_scenario: Product P has variants S (stock 1) and M (stock 1). Customer adds 1× S and 1× M to the bag (two cart lines, same productId) and checks out. Both stock checks pass (each reads the original snapshot). The write for line S sets variants=[S:0, M:1]; the write for line M then sets variants=[S:1, M:0] and wins. Variant S is still shown as in stock and can be sold again — oversell of a physically shipped unit. Top-level `stock` drops by 2 while the variants array only reflects 1.
findings.fix: Deduplicate by productId before the transaction: group all lines of a product, read the doc once, apply every line's decrement to a single `variants` copy, and issue exactly one `tx.update` per product document (the same grouping `catalog/inventory.ts:35-41` already does). Apply the identical fix to the restock loop in `orders/cancel.ts:82-103`.

verdict.reason:
Tried hard to refute and failed on every avenue.

1. Reachability confirmed. Carts key lines by (productId, variantId): `web/src/lib/cart.ts:42-43` `sameLine = a.productId === productId && a.variantId === variantId`, and `addTo` pushes a new line when the variantId differs. Both clients send lines 1:1 with no merging — `web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:180` (`lines.map((l) => ({ productId: l.productId, variantId: l.variantId, qty: l.qty }))`) and `app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:236-242` (`_payload`). Seeded products genuinely have multiple variants per product: `scripts/seed.ts:326-340` gives every clothing product variants `s`/`m`/`l`. So "1× S + 1× M of the same product" is an ordinary cart.

2. No dedupe or guard anywhere. `priceLines` (`functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:52-91`) is a straight per-line loop that pushes one PricedLine per input line; nothing collapses duplicate productIds. `Line`/`PlaceOrderSchema` (lines 28-33, 327-335) impose no uniqueness. Line 403 `Promise.all(priced.map((l) => tx.get(db.doc('products/'+l.productId))))` therefore yields two independent snapshots of the same doc, and the forEach at 428-442 rebuilds the whole `variants` array from its own stale snapshot (line 433) and issues a second full-array `tx.update` at line 437.

3. The SDK itself documents the failure mode. In the installed client (`/home/h/barkath/node_modules/.pnpm/@google-cloud+firestore@7.11.6/.../build/src/bulk-writer.js:860-863`): `if (this._bulkCommitBatch.has(op.ref)) { // Create a new batch since the backend doesn't support batches with two writes to the same document.` — plus the assert at line 207, "Batch should not contain writes to the same document". Transaction/WriteBatch (`write-batch.js`, `transaction.js`) contain no such dedupe or guard, so both updates are queued and sent in one Commit. That means checkout for such a cart fails outright with an INVALID_ARGUMENT commit error (the reviewer's stated alternative branch); if the backend ever did accept it, the later whole-array write clobbers the earlier one while `FieldValue.increment(-qty)` accumulates for both, so `stock` and `variants[].stock` diverge. Either branch is a real functional defect, not cosmetic.

4. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, and not an architecture-rule intent (this is the money/atomic path CFs exist for). `functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:82-103` restock has the identical pattern (same-product multi-variant order lines → two full-array `tx.update`s on one doc), so a cancel/refund of such an order hits it too. Fix is to group `priced` by productId and emit one merged `tx.update` per product document.

findings.title: placeOrder validates and consumes coupons outside the transaction, so a single-use spin coupon can be spent on two concurrent orders
findings.detail: `computeCouponDiscount` / `autoBestOffer` run at lines 347-349, before `db.runTransaction` opens at line 372. They read `customers/{uid}/coupons/{id}` (line 180-186: `status !== 'active'` check) and the promotional coupon's `usesCount` / per-user counter (lines 149-155) with plain non-transactional gets. Inside the transaction the coupon documents are never re-read: line 568 does a blind `tx.update(...{status:'used'...})` on the personal coupon, and lines 605-613 blindly increment `coupons/{id}.usesCount` and `customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{id}.count`. Because neither coupon doc is part of the transaction's read set, two overlapping placeOrder invocations do not contend on it and both commit. The idempotency key at line 370 does not help — it is derived from the cart/addressId or a client nonce, and two different carts (or two different client nonces) produce different keys.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer wins SPIN-ABCDE (flat ₹500 off, `maxUsesPerCoupon: 1`, status 'active') from the wheel. They open the web checkout in two tabs with different carts, enter SPIN-ABCDE in both, and press Place order within the same second. Both calls read status 'active' at line 184 and both pass; both transactions commit; both orders receive the ₹500 discount and both write `status:'used'` on the same coupon doc. ₹500 is given away twice. The same window lets a promotional coupon with `maxUsesTotal: 100` be redeemed past 100, since `usesCount` is read at line 149 outside the transaction.
findings.fix: Move the coupon document read inside the transaction: after resolving the coupon id outside (a query cannot run in a transaction), `tx.get` the coupon doc (`customers/{uid}/coupons/{id}` or `coupons/{id}` plus `customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{id}`) as part of the read phase, re-assert `status === 'active'` / `usesCount < maxUsesTotal` / per-user count against those fresh values, and recompute the discount from them before any write.

verdict.reason: Verified in /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts. computeCouponDiscount/autoBestOffer are awaited at lines 347-349, before db.runTransaction opens at 372, and they use plain non-transactional gets (db.collection('coupons')... line 128; usesCount check line 149; userCouponUses db.doc().get() line 113; personal coupon query line 180 with status!=='active' check at 184). Inside the transaction tx.get is called only on idemRef (374), customers/{uid} (394), the product docs (403), the affiliate doc (406) and counters/orders (423) — no coupon doc is ever in the read set. Lines 567-572 and 604-614 are blind tx.update writes setting status:'used' and incrementing usesCount/couponUsage. Refutation attempts all fail: (1) the idempotency key at 364-370 is derived from addressId+paymentMethod+sorted lines or a client nonce, so two different carts / two nonces yield different idemRefs; (2) incidental contention does exist — every placeOrder reads AND writes counters/orders (423, 617), and a spin-coupon order reads and writes customers/{uid} (394, 456) — so Firestore serializes and retries one callback, but the retry re-runs only the callback body; the coupon status/usesCount validation lives outside it, so the stale discountPaise/userCouponId are reused and the coupon is marked used a second time. Serialization makes the double-spend deterministic rather than preventing it; (3) grep over functions/src shows the only other writer of coupon state is spin/execute.ts:138, which issues the coupon with maxUsesPerCoupon:1, usesCount:0, status:'active' — there is no order-created trigger, scheduled reconciliation, or rules constraint that re-validates redemption. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not cosmetic, and squarely within the 'CF only for money/atomic-multi-doc/counters' rule. Fixable by resolving the coupon ref outside and doing the authoritative status/usesCount read via tx.get inside the transaction (same for userCouponUses and the firstOrderOnly stats read at 157).

findings.title: createRazorpayOrder and verifyPayment never check the order's status, so a gateway payment can be captured against an already-cancelled order
findings.detail: `createRazorpayOrder` (lines 654-682) validates only `snap.exists`, `o.customerId === uid` and `amount > 0`; it never inspects `o.status` or `o.paymentStatus`. `verifyPayment` (lines 692-734) validates ownership, that `razorpayOrderId` matches, and short-circuits only when `paymentStatus === 'captured'` (line 713) — a cancelled order carries `status: 'cancelled'` and `paymentStatus: 'refunded'` or `'pending'` (set by `orders/cancel.ts:151`), neither of which is caught. verifyPayment then unconditionally stamps `paymentStatus: 'captured'` and `amountPaidPaise: totalPaise` (lines 725-731) on the cancelled order. Nothing anywhere reverses that: `performCancellation` refuses to run again (`cancel.ts:56-58` throws 'already cancelled'), so the gateway money has no path back to the customer.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer places a ₹4,000 razorpay order; `placeOrder` returns with paymentStatus 'pending' and the Razorpay sheet opens. The customer leaves the sheet open. An admin, seeing an unpaid order, cancels it from the Orders screen — `adminChangeOrderStatus` → `performCancellation` restores stock, refunds only the wallet portion, sets status 'cancelled'. The customer then completes payment in the still-open sheet; the client calls `verifyPayment`, the signature is valid, and the function writes paymentStatus 'captured' / amountPaidPaise 400000 onto the cancelled order. The customer is charged ₹4,000, receives nothing, and no refund is ever triggered. The same gap lets `createRazorpayOrder` be called again on an already-captured order and charge the customer a second time.
findings.fix: In `createRazorpayOrder`, reject when `o.status === 'cancelled'` or `o.paymentStatus === 'captured'/'refunded'`, and reuse an existing `o.razorpayOrderId` instead of overwriting it. In `verifyPayment`, reject (or auto-refund via the Razorpay refunds API) when `o.status === 'cancelled'` or `o.paymentStatus === 'refunded'` before writing the capture.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. placeOrder (checkout.ts:490) creates razorpay orders with status 'accepted' and paymentStatus 'pending', and 'accepted' is cancellable both by the customer (CANCELLABLE, line 627) and by admin (TRANSITIONS.accepted includes 'cancelled', status.ts:15) — so the cancel window fully overlaps the payment window. performCancellation writes paymentStatus: refundPaise > 0 ? 'refunded' : (o.paymentStatus ?? 'pending') (cancel.ts:151); for an unpaid order amountPaidPaise is 0, so it stays 'pending'. verifyPayment (checkout.ts:692-734) gates only on snap.exists, customerId === uid, razorpayOrderId match, and paymentStatus === 'captured' (713) — a cancelled order passes all four and gets paymentStatus 'captured' plus amountPaidPaise: totalPaise written at 725-731. Nothing undoes it: performCancellation throws 'This order is already cancelled.' (cancel.ts:56-58), there is no Razorpay webhook anywhere under functions/src (grep for razorpay hits only checkout.ts, wallet/topup.ts, wallet/adjust.ts, returns/decisions.ts; no webhook handler at all), and orders are CF-only-write so no other surface can correct it. createRazorpayOrder (654-682) similarly never inspects status/paymentStatus and will overwrite razorpayOrderId (679) to mint a second charge on an already-captured order. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not cosmetic/UI, and fixable with a status/paymentStatus precondition in both callables.

findings.title: adminChangeOrderStatus confirms affiliate commissions after the transaction commits, and the delivered→delivered transition is illegal, so a failure strands the commission as 'pending' forever
findings.detail: The status transition commits in the transaction at lines 63-95. Only afterwards, at line 99, does the handler call `await confirmCommissionsForOrder(orderId)` — outside that transaction and with no try/catch. `confirmCommissionsForOrder` (affiliate/commissions.ts:107-136) performs its own query plus a second transaction that touches the affiliate's customer doc, so it can fail on contention, a Firestore deadline, or a missing index. When it throws, the error propagates out of the callable, `ref.update({affiliateCommissionStatus:'confirmed'})` at line 100 never runs, and `writeAudit` at line 103 never runs either. The admin sees the call fail and retries — but the order is already 'delivered' and `TRANSITIONS.delivered = []` (line 20), so the retry throws 'Cannot move delivered → cancelled/delivered'. There is no other caller of `confirmCommissionsForOrder` anywhere in the codebase and no scheduled reconciliation (scheduled/sweeps.ts only sweeps coupons), so the commission has no second chance.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin marks order #BRK-48123 (₹10,000, referred by affiliate A, ₹500 pending commission) delivered. The status transaction commits; `confirmCommissionsForOrder` then contends with a concurrent `placeOrder` accruing on the same affiliate doc and aborts. The admin sees 'internal error', clicks Delivered again and gets 'Cannot move delivered → delivered'. Affiliate A's ₹500 stays in `affiliate.pendingBalancePaise` and never reaches `confirmedBalancePaise` — the withdrawable balance — so it can never be withdrawn, and no audit log records the delivery.
findings.fix: Either fold the commission clearance into the same transaction as the status flip (read the pending commission docs before opening it, as `performCancellation` already does at cancel.ts:37-40), or wrap line 99 in a try/catch that logs and still writes the audit entry, and add a self-transition or a reconciliation sweep so 'delivered' orders with `affiliateCommissionStatus === 'pending'` can be re-confirmed.

verdict.reason:
Verified in /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/status.ts. The state change commits in the transaction at lines 63-95; only afterwards, at line 99, is `await confirmCommissionsForOrder(orderId)` called — outside the transaction and with no try/catch (note line 100's stamp update IS defensively wrapped in `.catch(() => undefined)`, showing the author considered post-commit failure but left line 99 unguarded). If line 99 throws, the callable fails, so `affiliateCommissionStatus: 'confirmed'` (line 100) and `writeAudit` (lines 103-109) both never run.

Recovery paths I looked for and did not find:
- Retry of the same call is impossible: `TRANSITIONS.delivered = []` (line 20), so the in-transaction guard at lines 67-70 throws `Cannot move delivered → delivered`.
- `confirmCommissionsForOrder` has exactly one caller in the repo (grep over ts/tsx/dart: only functions/src/orders/status.ts:99 plus its definition at functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:107).
- No reconciliation job: functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts has a single `onSchedule` (`couponExpirySweep`, line 87).
- No other function writes order.status (grep for 'delivered' in functions/src hits only status.ts plus read-only checks in returns/decisions.ts and returns/requests.ts; shipment.ts never sets status).
- No manual admin fix: firebase/firestore.rules lines 86-89 make `commissions/{id}` `allow write: if false`, and admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts exposes no confirm/adjust-commission callable (only withdrawal payout).
- Callables are not auto-retried (`callableOpts` in functions/src/_lib/admin.ts sets only region/memory/cpu/concurrency).

So a failure at line 99 permanently strands the commission in `affiliate.pendingBalancePaise`, never reaching `confirmedBalancePaise` (the withdrawable balance per the architecture rules), and drops the audit entry. The commission transaction itself is atomic, so there is no torn write — the harm is the stranding plus the unrecoverable state machine.

Caveats that do not refute it: the reporter's "missing index" trigger is wrong (a single-field equality query on `orderId` needs no composite index), and admin-SDK transactions retry on contention, so the trigger is rarer than claimed. But deadline-exceeded, contention that exhausts retries on the affiliate customer doc, or any transient error still yields exactly the described outcome, and this is a money path with zero second chance. Cheaply fixable: wrap line 99 in try/catch leaving `affiliateCommissionStatus` pending, allow an idempotent delivered→delivered re-confirm, or add a sweep.

findings.title: Review moderation writes products/{id}, which is gated by the products module, so a reviews-only sub-admin cannot approve anything
findings.detail: `moderateReview` runs one transaction that updates BOTH the review (line 50, `tx.update(rRef, {status, moderatedBy, moderatedAt, updatedAt})`) and the product aggregate (line 64, `tx.update(pRef, { ratingCount: newCount, rating: newRating })`). firebase/firestore.rules:51 gates `products` writes on `canWrite('products')` — i.e. products.create|edit|delete — while `reviews` moderation is a separate module (`reviews` is its own MODULE_KEY, packages/shared/src/enums.ts:258). A Firestore transaction is all-or-nothing: if the product write is denied the review status update is rolled back too. The catch in the caller surfaces only a generic toast, so the moderator sees a failure with no explanation and the review stays pending.
findings.failure_scenario: Sub-admin granted `reviews: view/edit/approve` but not `products: edit` opens /reviews and clicks Approve on a pending review. The transaction commit is rejected with permission-denied on `products/{productId}`; the review remains 'pending' and the product rating never updates. Approving reviews is impossible for that admin.
findings.fix: Either move the rating-aggregate write server-side into a `moderateReview` callable that uses `requireModule(req,'reviews','approve')`, or extend the products rule to also accept `canWrite('reviews')` when the diff is limited to `['rating','ratingCount']`.

verdict.reason: Verified as a real defect. admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:64 updates products/{productId} inside the same runTransaction that flips the review status (line 50). firebase/firestore.rules:51 has the single products match, `allow write: if canWrite('products')`, with no admin-wide fallback; the reviews match allows update for any isAdmin(), so only the product half is denied — and since Firestore transactions are atomic, the review status update is rolled back with it. The aggregate write fires whenever `wasCounted !== willCount`, which is always true on pending->approved, so a reviews-only sub-admin can never approve. No compensating path exists: there is no review-moderation Cloud Function or trigger (grep over functions/src for 'review' hits only returns/decisions.ts and orders/checkout.ts), and no other admin surface writes ratingCount except the products form itself. The established pattern for cross-module writes is the opposite: inventory does NOT touch products directly — admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts calls the adminAdjustStock callable, which enforces requireModule(req,'inventory','edit') (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26). Reachability confirmed: navConfig.tsx:53 exposes /reviews gated on the 'reviews' module and router.tsx:79 routes it, while ReviewsListPage.tsx:58 swallows the permission-denied into a generic toast. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item and not cosmetic; fix is to move the aggregate into a Cloud Function gated on the reviews module (matching the counters/atomic-multi-doc architecture rule).

findings.title: Web checkout offer list uses the same wrong promo-coupon field names, so applying an offer makes placeOrder fail
findings.detail: `promoDiscount()` (line 42) and `listAvailableOffers()` (line 115) gate on `c.minOrderPaise`, `c.expiresAt`, `c.maxDiscountPaise` — none of which the admin writes (see `saveCoupon`, which writes `minCartValuePaise`, `validUntil`, `discountMaxCapPaise`). So every promo coupon is displayed as `qualifies: true` with `sub: 'On any order'` regardless of its real minimum, and expired ones are still listed. `web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:103` (`applyOffer`) then stuffs that offer straight into the local draft with no server round-trip, and `placeOrder` re-validates through `computeCouponDiscount`, which DOES read `minCartValuePaise` (checkout.ts:143) and throws. The Flutter app's equivalent (app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:53) reads both name variants, so app and web disagree about the same coupon doc.
findings.failure_scenario: Coupon FEST20 has minCartValuePaise = ₹2,000. Customer with a ₹600 cart opens web checkout: FEST20 is listed as qualifying with the full discount and is even auto-applied by `bestOfferForCart`. Tapping 'Place order' calls placeOrder, which throws failed-precondition 'Your cart does not meet this coupon's minimum.' The order can never be placed until the customer manually removes the auto-applied coupon.
findings.fix: Change `PromoCoupon` and both readers to `minCartValuePaise`, `validUntil`, `discountMaxCapPaise` (keeping the legacy names only as fallbacks, as offers.dart does), and validate a tapped offer through `callApplyCoupon` before storing it in the draft.

verdict.reason: Real defect, reproducible with seeded data. web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:42/115 read `minOrderPaise`, `expiresAt`, `maxDiscountPaise` for promo `coupons` docs, but admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:127-133 and scripts/seed.ts:715-725 write `minCartValuePaise`, `validUntil`, `discountMaxCapPaise`. So `min` is always 0 on web: every active promo renders as qualifying ("On any order"), the percent cap is ignored, and expiry is unchecked (violating the compute-on-read expiry rule). checkout/page.tsx:90-92 auto-applies the best offer and :102 applyOffer both write straight into the local draft, and :176 sends `couponCode` to placeOrder, which routes to functions/src/orders/checkout.ts computeCouponDiscount — line 143 reads `minCartValuePaise` and throws failed-precondition. The catch at page.tsx:215 only toasts and leaves the coupon applied, so the order cannot be placed. Seed coupon WELCOME30 has minCartValuePaise=₹150, so any cart under ₹150 hits this. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item; the Flutter equivalent (app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:53, _expiryMillis) already reads both field-name variants, confirming the cross-surface mismatch. Only partial mitigation: the server's autoBestOffer (checkout.ts:228,233) shares the same wrong names, but it is bypassed because web always sends an explicit code — and checkout.ts:132-134 documents that these exact field names were a known bug fixed server-side.

findings.title: Return window is hardcoded to 3 days server-side, ignoring settings/returns.windowDays that the admin sets and the web enforces
findings.detail: `requestReturnOrReplacement` hardcodes `RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` and rejects anything older (line 44). It never reads `settings/returns`. Meanwhile admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:295 lets an admin save `settings/returns.windowDays` (0-90, default 7) via `saveReturns`, and web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261 `returnWindow()` uses that value — falling back to `DEFAULT_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7` (line 246) — to decide whether to show the 'Return item' button and the 'N days left' copy (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71). The Flutter app hardcodes its own third value, `returnWindowDays = 3` (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart). So three surfaces disagree, and the admin setting is write-only.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sets the return window to 7 days (or leaves settings/returns unset, so the web default of 7 applies). An order delivered 5 days ago shows 'Return item · 2 days left' on the web account page. The customer fills in the reason and submits; requestReturnOrReplacement throws failed-precondition 'The 3-day return window for this order has closed.' No return can ever be created between day 3 and day 7. Conversely, setting windowDays = 0 to disable returns still lets the CF accept returns for 3 days.
findings.fix: Read `settings/returns.windowDays` inside `requestReturnOrReplacement` (defaulting to the same 7 the web uses) and use it for the window check; have the Flutter `Order.canReturn` fetch the same setting instead of its hardcoded 3.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. functions/src/returns/requests.ts:42-46 hardcodes RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 days and throws failed-precondition; it never reads settings/returns, and there is no other server-side guard (a repo-wide grep for windowDays shows the CF is the only surface that never reads it). The admin does write the value: admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296 saveReturns({id:'returns', windowDays, autoRefundToWallet}), typed in packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:83, and both scripts/seed.ts:208 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117 seed windowDays: 7. The web reads it (useReturnSettings -> returnWindow(order, returnSettings?.windowDays) at web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71, fallback DEFAULT_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7 at web/src/components/account/orders.ts:246) to gate the Return button, then submits through that same CF (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:315 httpsCallable('requestReturnOrReplacement')). So in the default seeded config (7 days) the web shows 'Return item · N days left' on days 4-7 and every such submit is rejected server-side; conversely windowDays = 0 (returns disabled) is still accepted by the CF for 3 days. Two secondary mismatches in the same guard reinforce it: web falls back to placedAt when deliveredAt is missing while the CF hard-rejects a missing deliveredAt, and the app hardcodes a third copy (app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:202 returnWindowDays = 3). This is a server-side logic defect (write-only admin setting plus guaranteed rejected submissions), not cosmetic UI, and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Fix is server-side: read settings/returns inside the transaction, defaulting to 7.

findings.title: The `payments` collection is never written by any Cloud Function — the admin Payments module only ever shows seeded rows
findings.detail: `usePaymentsList()` subscribes to `collection(db,'payments')` and PaymentsListPage renders/exports from it (including the 'GST invoices' CSV of captured payments, PaymentsListPage.tsx:56). Nothing writes that collection: grepping functions/src for `payments` yields only `requireModule(req,'payments','view')` in orders/invoice.ts. `placeOrder` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:546) writes only the order doc, `verifyPayment` (line 725) only patches the order, and `topUpWallet`/`verifyTopUp` only write walletTransactions. The single writer in the repo is scripts/seed.ts:684. The shared `Payment` type and the read rule `match /payments/{id} … isOwner(resource.data.customerId)` (firebase/firestore.rules:76) exist for documents nothing creates.
findings.failure_scenario: On a fresh (unseeded) project, a customer places and pays for 50 razorpay orders. The admin opens Payments: the list is empty, month-to-date total is ₹0 and 'failed' is 0, and 'Export GST invoices' reports 'Nothing to export' — while Orders shows all 50 as Paid.
findings.fix: Write a `payments/{id}` doc inside the placeOrder transaction and update it in verifyPayment (id/orderId/customerId/method/gateway/status/amountPaise/gatewayRef/createdAt), or drop the Payments module and derive it from `orders`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The only writer of the `payments` collection anywhere in the repo is scripts/seed.ts:684 (verified by grepping for `payments/`, `collection('payments')` and `COLLECTIONS.payments` across functions/, web/, app/lib, admin/, packages/). firebase/firestore.rules:76 sets `allow write: if false` for /payments/{id}, so no client can create them either — only a Cloud Function could, and none does: functions/src contains the string "payments" solely as the RBAC module key at orders/invoice.ts:19. placeOrder (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts) writes the order doc, idempotency key, timeline, coupon counters and wallet ledger rows but no payment doc; verifyPayment only patches the order (paymentStatus:'captured', razorpayPaymentId, razorpaySignature, amountPaidPaise); cancel/returns/wallet paths never touch it. No fallback exists in the UI: admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx uses useOrdersList() only to map orderId→shortId for display (line 27), and rows/stats/exports all derive from usePaymentsList() alone. The page is routed and reachable (admin/src/app/router.tsx:77). So on a fresh unseeded project the Payments list, MTD total, failed count and both CSV exports (including 'GST invoices') are permanently empty despite paid orders. Not cosmetic, not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and per the architecture rules this money ledger is exactly the kind of doc a CF should write — a real, fixable functional gap (missing payment-doc write in placeOrder/verifyPayment).

findings.title: firstOrderOnly coupon check reads customers.stats.totalOrders, a field no surface writes
findings.detail: `computeCouponDiscount` gates first-order-only coupons on `Number((cust.get('stats'))?.totalOrders ?? 0) > 0`. The shared `CustomerStats` type (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:93) and every writer — web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:62, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:244, scripts/seed.ts:465 — use `ordersCount`. `totalOrders` only exists as a locally-computed dashboard field (admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:23), never on a customer doc, so the expression is always 0 and the guard never trips. Compounding it, nothing ever increments `stats.*` after signup either (no `stats.` write exists anywhere in functions/src), so even the correctly-named `ordersCount` stays 0 — which is why admin/src/features/customers/routes/CustomersListPage.tsx:125 shows 'Orders: 0' for every real customer.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates WELCOME15 with targetUsers = 'new' (saveCoupon sets firstOrderOnly: true, maxUsesPerUser: 1). A customer with 40 previous orders enters WELCOME15 at checkout: the firstOrderOnly guard reads undefined → 0 → passes, and the discount is granted. Separately, that customer's row in the admin Customers list and its CSV export both report 0 orders.
findings.fix: Read `stats.ordersCount` in the guard, and increment `stats.ordersCount`/`ordersDelivered`/`totalSpentPaise`/`lastOrderAt` on the customer doc inside the placeOrder and adminChangeOrderStatus transactions.

verdict.reason: Verified and confirmed. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:158 reads `(cust.get('stats'))?.totalOrders`, but a repo-wide grep for `totalOrders` shows the only other hits are admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts (a locally computed KPI object, never persisted) and DashboardPage.tsx — no writer ever puts `totalOrders` on a customer doc. Every actual customer-stats writer uses `ordersCount`: packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:93 (CustomerStats), web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:61-71, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:243, scripts/seed.ts:464. So the expression is always `undefined ?? 0 = 0` and the `> 0` guard never trips — dead code in a money path. No compensating guard exists: `grep -rn 'customers/' functions/src` plus reading the checkout transaction (lines 385-600) shows checkout writes wallet, couponUsage, timeline and ledger rows but never touches `stats.*`, so a rename alone is insufficient — the fix needs the rename AND an increment. Worse than claimed, admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:120-137 `base` does not write `maxUsesPerUser` at all, so only `maxUsesTotal` and the per-coupon `couponUsage` counter apply; a customer with 40 prior orders redeeming a targetUsers='new' coupon (firstOrderOnly:true, e.g. seeded WELCOME30 at scripts/seed.ts:723) gets the discount on their first use. Reachable, affects order totals server-side, and not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. The admin 'Orders: 0' column is only the cosmetic symptom; the core defect is functional.

findings.title: Variant delete-safety downloads the entire products collection once per unit, so deleting a group with N units triggers N full-collection reads
findings.detail: `countProductsUsingUnit` does `getDocs(collection(db, 'products'))` — an unbounded, unfiltered read of every product document — and then scans `variants[].attributes` client-side. VariablesTab.tsx:119-126 calls it in a serial `for (const u of delTarget.units)` loop before deleting a variant, and AddUnitsModal.tsx:77 calls it again on every individual chip removal. There is no caching, no `limit`, and no reuse of the already-live products listener (`useProductsList` / PRODUCTS_KEY) that the admin app maintains elsewhere.
findings.failure_scenario: With a 2,000-product catalogue, an admin deletes the "Size" group which holds 8 units (XS…XXL). VariablesTab.confirmDelete awaits 8 sequential full-collection downloads = 16,000 document reads and tens of seconds of blocked UI before the delete happens (and it aborts on the first in-use unit, after already paying for the earlier scans). Removing 3 colour chips one at a time costs another 6,000 reads.
findings.fix: Fetch the products once (or read from the already-subscribed PRODUCTS_KEY cache via `getCachedList<Product>`), build a Set of all attribute values in use, and answer every unit check from that one pass; pass the whole unit-id list to a single `countUnitsInUse(ids)` helper for the group-delete case.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute; the code reads exactly as claimed and there is no mitigating guard anywhere.

/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/settings/api/variables.ts:67-78 — `countProductsUsingUnit` does `await getDocs(collection(db, 'products'))` with no `limit`, no `where`, no cache, no reuse of any live snapshot, then scans `variants[].attributes` in JS. Every call is a fresh billed server round-trip over the whole catalogue (a one-time `getDocs` is not served by an unrelated component's listener, and no products listener is even mounted on the Settings screen).

Call sites confirm the multiplication:
- /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/settings/routes/VariablesTab.tsx:120-126 — `for (const u of delTarget.units) { const inUse = await countProductsUsingUnit(u.id); ... }` — strictly serial, one full-collection download per unit in the group. Counting all units needs only ONE scan (build a Set of used unit ids from a single snapshot), so the extra N-1 scans are pure waste, not inherent to the check.
- VariablesTab.tsx:101 (`removeDirectUnit`) and :249 (group chip removal) and /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/settings/components/AddUnitsModal.tsx:77 each pay another full scan per individual chip.

Checked the usual refutation routes and none apply:
- Not handled elsewhere: `saveVariables` (variables.ts:38-52) is a plain `setDoc` merge on `settings/variables`; there is no Cloud Function and no rules-level in-use re-check, so the client scan is the only enforcement — it cannot simply be dropped, but it can be done once.
- Cache exists but is not usable as-is: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts exposes `getCachedList<Product>(PRODUCTS_KEY)` and products/api/products.ts:19-25 maintains `useProductsList`, but that entry is empty unless a products screen has been mounted, so naively reusing it would produce a false "not in use" and allow a bad delete. That makes the "reuse the listener" half of the claim weaker, but it does not excuse the N-times-per-delete loop.
- Not architectural intent (direct Firestore reads are fine; repeating the same unfiltered read N times is not), not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not unreachable (all three call sites are wired to live UI handlers), and not cosmetic — the fix is in api/variables.ts + the confirmDelete loop, no UI change required.

Scope note: the failure-scenario numbers are hypothetical (catalogue size unknown) and variant-group deletion is a rare admin action, and the loop short-circuits on the first in-use unit so worst case is bounded by the unit count. Real and cheaply fixable, but moderate rather than severe.

findings.title: Saving a product writes back the rating aggregate captured when the form opened, silently reverting review approvals
findings.detail: `rating`/`ratingCount` are initialised once from the seed/loaded doc (lines 96-97, 126-127) and unconditionally written on every save (lines 222-223 → products.ts:130-131, included in `base` for the `updateDoc` path). But those same two fields are a derived aggregate maintained transactionally by review moderation: admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:59-64 recomputes `ratingCount` and `rating` inside `runTransaction` on approve/reject. The product form's blind overwrite is not part of that transaction and has no read-back, so it is a classic lost update.
findings.failure_scenario: Product has 12 approved reviews (rating 4.3, ratingCount 12). Admin A opens the product edit form. Admin B approves a 5-star review → the transaction writes rating 4.36→4.4, ratingCount 13. Admin A fixes a typo in the description and clicks Save → rating 4.3 / ratingCount 12 are written back, dropping the new review from the aggregate. If B later rejects that review, `moderateReview` subtracts it a second time, leaving rating/ratingCount permanently below the true value.
findings.fix: Drop `rating`/`ratingCount` from `ProductFormValues` and from `base` in `saveProduct` on the edit path (leave them only in the `isNew` seed block), or make the fields write-only-when-dirty and perform the write inside a transaction that re-reads the current aggregate.

verdict.reason: The claim holds up on inspection. ProductFormPage.tsx captures rating/ratingCount at mount (lines 96-97) and only re-syncs from the server read when there was no cache seed (line 117 `if (!seed)` guards 126-127); existingRef is refreshed at line 115 but is used solely to preserve variant stock/weight/visibility. Lines 222-223 then feed those captured values into saveProduct, and products.ts:130-131 places them in `base`, which is passed to updateDoc unconditionally on the edit path (line 165) — no dirty check, no re-read, not in a transaction. The competing writer is real and reachable: reviews.ts:37-65 recomputes ratingCount/rating inside runTransaction on approve/reject (its own comment says the aggregate is a read-modify-write that must not be overwritten with a stale absolute value), invoked from ReviewsListPage.tsx:55,66. Nothing heals the drift: grep over functions/src finds no `rating` reference at all (no server-side recompute trigger), and firestore.rules:51 allows blanket admin writes to products with no field guard (rules 106-108 only validate a review's own rating on create). The follow-on corruption is also real, because moderateReview gates on the stored review status rather than on the aggregate, so a later reject subtracts a second time. Refutations considered and rejected: the fields are intentionally admin-editable ("admin-managed", products.ts:127-129), which justifies writing them when edited but not writing back an untouched stale value; the firestoreCache is in-memory and live, so the seed is fresh at mount, which narrows the window to "form open -> save" but does not close it (the form even keeps the products listener attached via useProductsList at line 73, so a fresher value is available and ignored). Severity is low — it needs a concurrent moderation during the form session, the same last-write-wins window the form has for other fields — but it is a genuine, non-cosmetic, fixable defect (write rating/ratingCount only when the admin actually changed them, no UI change required).

findings.title: bestSellerOrder is re-stamped with Date.now() on every save, reshuffling the storefront Best-sellers rail on unrelated edits
