findings.detail: `bestSellerOrder: values.isBestSeller ? Date.now() : null` sits in `base`, which is written on BOTH the create and the edit path (lines 138 and 165). The comment three lines above says "Order stamped when first flagged", but the code re-stamps unconditionally. web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:28-29 renders the rail as `products.filter(p => p.isBestSeller).sort((a,b) => (a.bestSellerOrder ?? 1e9) - (b.bestSellerOrder ?? 1e9))` — ascending, i.e. earliest-stamped first — and firestore.indexes.json carries a dedicated `status + isBestSeller + bestSellerOrder ASC` index for it.
findings.failure_scenario: Five best sellers are curated in a deliberate order. The merchandiser opens the first one (bestSellerOrder = 1 Jun) to fix a spelling mistake in its description and saves. Its bestSellerOrder becomes today's epoch — the largest value — so on the next home-page load it jumps from position 1 to position 5. Any routine edit silently reorders the rail, and there is no UI to restore the intended order.
findings.fix: Only stamp when the flag transitions off→on: `bestSellerOrder: values.isBestSeller ? (existing?.bestSellerOrder ?? Date.now()) : null`, passing the loaded product's current value through `ProductFormValues` (the form already keeps it in `existingRef.current`).

verdict.reason:
Verified end to end; I could not find any guard, fallback, or server-side re-check that saves the claim.

1. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:132 — `bestSellerOrder: values.isBestSeller ? Date.now() : null` is a member of `base`, and `base` is spread into the create `setDoc` (line 138-163) AND passed verbatim to `updateDoc(doc(db,'products',values.id), base)` on the edit path (line 165). There is no `isNew` conditional around it and no read of the product's existing `bestSellerOrder`. The comment at lines 121-122 ("Order stamped when first flagged") documents the opposite of what the code does.

2. The edit path is reachable and does not preserve the value: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:68 (`isNew = !routeId || routeId === 'new'`), :123 loads only `isBestSeller` from the existing doc, :218 puts it into the form values, :257 calls `saveProduct(values, isNew)`. `ProductFormValues` (products.ts:69-88) has no `bestSellerOrder` field at all, so the previously stored order is simply not carried through — it is unconditionally overwritten with `Date.now()` on every "Save changes", even when only the description changed.

3. Nothing else writes the field in a way that repairs it. Full-repo grep for `bestSellerOrder` hits only: shared type (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:106), the two admin sites that write `null` (duplicateProduct :203, importProducts :289), the index (firebase/firestore.indexes.json:29, `bestSellerOrder ASC`), scripts/seed.ts:382 (`i % 4 === 0 ? i : null` — small ints), and the single reader web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:29 (`.sort((a,b) => (a.bestSellerOrder ?? 1e9) - (b.bestSellerOrder ?? 1e9))`, ascending, sliced to 5). No Cloud Function trigger touches it (no hits under functions/), no firestore rule pins it, and the Flutter app never reads it.

4. Consequence is concrete and functional, not cosmetic: seeded/curated orders are small integers (1, 4, 8…) while a re-stamp writes ~1.7e12, so any routine edit sends that product to the end of the ascending sort — it can also fall out of the `.slice(0, 5)` rail entirely, i.e. a curated best seller stops being displayed. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, and it does not conflict with the architecture rules (this is a plain rules-gated admin write; the fix is to preserve the existing stamp when the product was already flagged, which needs no UI change).

findings.title: stockAdjustments create rule only checks isAdmin(), bypassing the inventory.edit module gate the rest of the file enforces
findings.detail: Every other directly-written admin collection is gated with `can(module, action)` / `canWrite(module)` (e.g. products on line 51 uses `canWrite('products')`), and the comment on lines 15-19 states this is deliberate so "a sub-admin with only dashboard.view" cannot write. The stockAdjustments rule requires only `isAdmin() && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid()` - no `can('inventory','edit')` check and no validation of before/delta/after/productId. The stock mutation itself is correctly protected (requireModule(req,'inventory','edit') in functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26), but the audit trail that admins read in StockHistoryModal is not. The collection is append-only (`allow update, delete: if false`), so forged rows can never be removed.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub_admin whose modulePermissions contain only {dashboard:{view:true}} opens the browser console and writes to stockAdjustments with their own uid: {productId:'p1', before:200, delta:-180, after:20, reason:'Damage', adminName:'Someone Else'}. The write succeeds. The Stock history modal for p1 now permanently shows a fabricated 180-unit shrinkage attributed to a chosen name, and it can never be deleted.
findings.fix: Change the rule to `allow create: if can('inventory','edit') && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid();` and add shape validation (numeric before/delta/after, adminName matching adminDoc().name).

verdict.reason:
Verified and could not refute. /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:213-217 is the only gate on this collection: `allow create: if isAdmin() && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid();` — `isAdmin()` (rules line 12) accepts any `sub_admin` claim regardless of modulePermissions, and there is no `can('inventory','edit')`/`canWrite(...)` call, unlike every other directly-written admin collection (rules lines 48-59, e.g. `canWrite('products')`). The file's own comment at lines 14-19 states this matrix exists precisely so "a sub-admin with only dashboard.view" cannot write these collections, so the omission is an inconsistency with the file's stated design, not an intentional exception.

No server-side re-check covers it: the ledger rows are written client-side, not by a Cloud Function. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:118-142 (`addLedger`) does `batch.set(doc(collection(db,'stockAdjustments')), {...})` after the callable returns, and its own comment says "The stockAdjustments ledger stays a client write". functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26 `requireModule(req,'inventory','edit')` protects only the product stock mutation and the auditLogs entry (auditLogs/complianceLogs are `allow write: if false`, rules 224-225) — it never touches stockAdjustments. So a sub_admin lacking inventory.edit cannot move stock, but can freely append fabricated history rows (arbitrary before/delta/after/reason/adminName/productId, only adminUid is constrained to their own uid), and `allow update, delete: if false` makes them permanent. Those rows are what getStockHistory (inventory.ts:148-153) feeds to the stock-history modal.

'inventory' is a real module key (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:257, MODULE_KEYS/ModuleKey), so the fix is a one-line rules change to `allow create: if can('inventory','edit') && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid();` — a genuine, fixable, non-cosmetic security defect, and not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items. Impact is limited (audit-trail forgery, not stock corruption) but real.

findings.title: Seeded ops sub-admin is granted a non-existent `returns` module, so the real `refunds` module is all-false — Refunds is hidden and approve/reject is permission-denied
findings.detail: `scopedPerms(['dashboard','orders','customers','payments','returns'])` builds permissions by iterating `MODULE_KEYS` and testing `modules.includes(m)` (seed.ts:46-50). `MODULE_KEYS` contains `'refunds'`, not `'returns'` (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:262, with the comment "was 'replacement', then 'returns' — renamed"). So the doc gets `modulePermissions.refunds = ALL_ACTIONS_FALSE` and the `'returns'` string is silently dropped. The admin sidebar gates on `admin?.modulePermissions?.[item.module]?.view === true` (admin/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:12), and both callables call `requireModule(req,'refunds','approve')` (functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:15 and :133).
findings.failure_scenario: Sign in to the admin panel as ops@barkath.app (sub_admin). The 'Refunds' nav item is missing entirely. Navigating directly to /refunds still renders the page (there is no route-level permission guard) and the list loads because firestore.rules:90-92 only requires isAdmin(); clicking 'Approve & refund' then fails with 'Missing refunds.approve permission.' The operator role intended to handle returns cannot handle any return.
findings.fix: Change the seeded module list to `'refunds'` (and add a route-level permission guard so a module the sidebar hides is not reachable by URL with working-looking buttons).

verdict.reason: Every link in the chain verified; nothing mitigates it. (1) /home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:46-50 — scopedPerms(modules: string[]) maps over MODULE_KEYS and tests modules.includes(m); the param is typed string[], not ModuleKey[], so TS cannot catch a bogus key and the unmatched string is silently dropped. (2) /home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/enums.ts:262 is 'refunds', // was 'replacement', then 'returns' — renamed to match the design. There is no 'returns' module key, so the ops doc gets modulePermissions.refunds = ALL_ACTIONS_FALSE. The comment makes the stale-rename origin explicit; intent is clearly to grant the refund queue (account is ops/Arjun Rao with orders+customers+payments). (3) No aliasing or fallback: admin/src/features/auth/stores/authStore.ts loads the doc verbatim, admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts helpers all iterate MODULE_KEYS, and functions/src/_lib/guards.ts requireModule does a raw perms?.[module]?.[action] lookup. (4) Enforcement is server-side, not cosmetic: functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:15 and :133 both call requireModule(req,'refunds','approve'), throwing "Missing refunds.approve permission." for sub_admins (super_admin short-circuits). (5) The claim's route/rules detail also holds: admin/src/app/router.tsx:78 registers /refunds with no per-module route guard, and firestore.rules match /orderRequests/{id} allows read for any isAdmin(), so the page loads and only approve/reject fails. Refutation angles tried and rejected: not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; production admins come from scripts/bootstrap-real.ts (full perms) or the Sub-Admin form (iterates MODULE_KEYS), so neither path reproduces it; e2e/tests/admin/returns.spec.ts signs in as super admin so no test masks or catches it. Severity caveat: blast radius is the emulator/demo seed fixture only — no production data path affected and no test currently fails — but it is a real, reachable, one-word fix ('returns' -> 'refunds' at seed.ts:121), and the seeded operator role genuinely cannot approve or reject any return. Also worth typing scopedPerms(modules: ModuleKey[]) so the compiler catches the next rename.

findings.title: `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet` is a dead toggle — no code ever reads it
findings.detail: The Storefront settings tab renders a Toggle bound to `autoRefundToWallet` and persists it via `saveReturns({ id:'returns', windowDays: days, autoRefundToWallet })` (StorefrontTab.tsx:296). Grepping the entire repo for `autoRefundToWallet` yields only: the shared type (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:84), this component, and the two seed scripts. `functions/src/returns/decisions.ts` never reads `settings/returns`; it always branches on `const toWallet = (r.refundMethod ?? 'wallet') === 'wallet'` (decisions.ts:77), and `requestReturnOrReplacement` hardcodes `refundMethod: 'wallet'` on every request (requests.ts, orderRequests payload). So `toWallet` is always true.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin turns 'Auto-refund to wallet' OFF and saves (toast confirms success). They then approve a return: `adminApproveOrderRequest` still credits `customers/{uid}.wallet.balancePaise` and writes a `walletTransactions` credit exactly as before. The setting has zero effect and there is no other refund path in the codebase.
findings.fix: Either have `adminApproveOrderRequest` read `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet` and, when false, leave the request at an 'approved, awaiting manual payout' state without crediting the wallet, or remove the toggle.

verdict.reason: Verified: `autoRefundToWallet` has zero readers repo-wide — only the shared type (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:84), the admin toggle/save (admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:280/285/296/329) and the two seed scripts. functions/src/returns/requests.ts:113 hardcodes `refundMethod: 'wallet'` on every created orderRequest, orderRequests is CF-only-write per firebase/firestore.rules:90 so no other surface can set 'gateway', and functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:77 branches solely on `(r.refundMethod ?? 'wallet') === 'wallet'` without ever loading settings/returns. Consequently the wallet credit + walletTransactions entry (decisions.ts:80-101) runs unconditionally regardless of the toggle, and no gateway-refund path exists anywhere in functions/src to serve as the 'off' branch. Refutation attempts failed: the sibling field windowDays IS consumed (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261, order detail and return pages), proving the settings/returns doc is otherwise live — only this flag is orphaned; it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; and it is not cosmetic, since the admin gets a success toast for a money-flow policy that never applies. The fix is server-side (read settings/returns in adminApproveOrderRequest and skip the wallet credit when false), not a UI change.

findings.title: GST invoice omits the COD surcharge line, so the printed line items do not sum to the printed Total
findings.detail: The totals table emits only Subtotal, Discount, Delivery, GST and Total (invoice.ts:46-50). The order total is computed as `totalPaise = net + deliveryPaise + codSurchargePaise + taxPaise` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:291) and `codSurchargePaise` is persisted on the order (checkout.ts:504-ish, `codSurchargePaise: summary.codSurchargePaise`). Because the surcharge is never printed, a COD invoice's visible arithmetic is off by exactly `codSurchargePaise`. This document is shipped to the customer as a tax invoice via `invoiceUrl` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108 and app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24).
findings.failure_scenario: settings/delivery.codSurchargePaise = 3000. A COD order: subtotal ₹890, discount ₹0, delivery ₹50, GST ₹0, codSurcharge ₹30 -> totalPaise = ₹970. The generated invoice prints Subtotal ₹890.00, Discount -₹0.00, Delivery ₹50.00, GST ₹0.00, Total ₹970.00 — the lines add to ₹940 and the customer/auditor sees an unexplained ₹30.
findings.fix: Add `COD charges${inr(o.codSurchargePaise)}` (rendered only when > 0) before the GST row, and consider an informational 'Paid by wallet' line for `o.walletUsedPaise`.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds up. `/home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:46-50` builds the totals table from exactly five fields — `o.subtotalPaise`, `o.discountPaise`, `o.deliveryPaise`, `o.taxPaise`, `o.totalPaise` — with no row for `codSurchargePaise`. Meanwhile `/home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:291` computes `totalPaise = net + deliveryPaise + codSurchargePaise + taxPaise`, and line 501 persists `codSurchargePaise: summary.codSurchargePaise` on the order doc (it is a required field on the shared Order type, packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:54). So for any COD order the printed lines are short of the printed Total by exactly the surcharge.

I tried each refutation route and none works:
- Not unreachable: `codSurchargePaise` is a real admin-configurable setting (admin/src/features/settings/routes/DeliveryTaxTab.tsx) and the seed sets it to ₹20 (scripts/seed.ts:176, 585). The only zeroing path is checkout.ts:296-301, which drops the surcharge solely when a COD order is fully wallet-paid — a narrow case, so nonzero persisted surcharges are the norm for COD.
- Not handled elsewhere: nothing else rewrites the invoice HTML; `adminGenerateInvoice` is the sole producer (admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:143) and it stamps `invoiceUrl` on the order (invoice.ts:62), which is what web (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108) and the app (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24) hand to the customer.
- Not intentional-by-convention: the order detail screen does render the line — web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:165-166 shows a "COD charge" row gated on `> 0`. The invoice is simply missing that row.
- Not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, and not merely cosmetic: this is server-side document generation in functions/, and the defect is arithmetic in a document labelled "Tax Invoice" that does not reconcile. The fix is a one-line conditional row in invoice.ts mirroring the existing `> 0` gate used on the order detail page, not a styling change.

findings.title: publishedAt is stamped at product creation even for drafts, so a product drafted more than 3 days before going live never enters New Arrivals
findings.detail: On create, saveProduct writes `publishedAt: serverTimestamp()` unconditionally (line 160) regardless of `values.status` ('draft' or 'published'). On update the `base` payload (lines 100-134) contains `status` but never `publishedAt`, so publishing a draft never refreshes it. Both storefronts derive New Arrivals purely from that timestamp: web/src/lib/catalog.ts:44-63 (`publishedAt ?? createdAt`, 3-day window) and app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:190-194 (`publishedAtMillis >= now - 3d`). The comment at products.ts:120-122 states new arrivals is automatic with no admin flag, so there is no manual override.
findings.failure_scenario: Buyer creates 20 Eid products as drafts on 1 July (each gets publishedAt = 1 July), finishes photography and flips them all to Published on 10 July. On both web and app the New Arrivals rail stays empty — the products are already 9 days past their recorded publish date and aged out before they were ever visible. There is no admin control to fix it short of deleting and recreating each product.
findings.fix: Write `publishedAt: values.status === 'published' ? serverTimestamp() : null` on create, and in the update path set `publishedAt: serverTimestamp()` when the status transitions from a non-published state to 'published' (leave it untouched otherwise).

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:160 stamps publishedAt=serverTimestamp() on create regardless of values.status, and 'draft' is a genuinely selectable status (ProductFormPage.tsx:350-356). The update path (line 165) writes `base` (lines 98-135), which contains `status` but never `publishedAt`, and setProductArchived (line 52) writes only status+updatedAt when republishing — so no admin surface ever stamps a draft→published transition. No server-side rescue exists: functions/src/index.ts:8-16 documents that onProductWrite and all product document triggers were intentionally removed, and the only functions-side product writer is catalog/inventory.ts (stock only); firestore.rules never touches publishedAt. Both storefronts derive the rail solely from that value with a createdAt fallback (web/src/lib/catalog.ts:43-56, app/lib/features/catalog/data/product.dart:120-125 + catalog_repository.dart:190-194), so the fallback does not compensate — it ages from creation too. isNewArrival is written false and unused by either rail, so there is no manual override. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and not a UI-only issue. One nuance: removing line 160 alone would not fix it (the createdAt fallback yields the same aging); the true missing behaviour is stamping publishedAt when status transitions to published, so the claim's line-160 framing is slightly imprecise while the defect and failure scenario are accurate.

findings.title: Deep-link type "Custom URL" is offered and required by admin but is a no-op in the app inbox
findings.detail: DEEP_LINK_TYPES exposes `url`, and NotificationCreatePage.tsx:80 hard-requires a value for it ("Enter a URL to link to.") before the broadcast can be sent; the CF stores it as deepLink {type:'url', target:'https://…'} (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:57). The app inbox parses the object correctly (app/lib/features/notifications/data/app_notification.dart:55-72) but its tap handler only switches on 'product', 'category' and 'home' — 'url' falls into `default: break;` (app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:179-181). No other surface consumes the notification deep link.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sends "Eid sale is live" with deep link Custom URL → https://barkath.in/eid. A customer taps the notification card in the app: it is marked read and absolutely nothing else happens — no navigation, no browser, no error.
findings.fix: Either handle type 'url' in _onTap (url_launcher is already a dependency, used by the Help centre) or drop 'url' from DEEP_LINK_TYPES so admins cannot pick a destination that no client can open.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end; nothing refutes it. admin/src/features/notifications/api/notifications.ts:113-123 declares DeepLinkType including 'url' and lists {value:'url', label:'Custom URL'}, with deepLinkNeedsTarget('url')===true. admin/src/features/notifications/routes/NotificationCreatePage.tsx:80 hard-blocks submit without a target ("Enter a URL to link to.") and line 209 renders the URL input, so an admin can and must supply one. functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts accepts deepLink as {type: string, target: string|null} (no enum restriction) and writes it verbatim onto broadcasts/{id} and every customers/{uid}/notifications/{id} — no server-side rewrite that would neutralise 'url'. app/lib/features/notifications/data/app_notification.dart:51-72 parses it correctly, and even maps a legacy bare-string deepLink to type 'url', so the path is reachable from two directions. app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:164-183 `_onTap` marks read then switches only on 'product' | 'category' | 'home'; 'url' hits `default: break; // url / none — no in-app destination`, and that is the card's only tap handler (_NotificationCard onTap: () => _onTap(...)). No fallback consumer elsewhere: grep for `deepLink` across the repo hits only functions/broadcast.ts, packages/shared types, admin (bell + api + create page) and scripts/seed.ts; the web inbox (web/src/app/(shop)/account/notifications/page.tsx and web/src/lib/notifications.ts) has zero deepLink/href references, so web doesn't consume it either. Not a KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not an architecture-rule allowance, and not cosmetic — the fix is behavioural (open the target externally or surface a failure) and trivially available: the app already depends on url_launcher (app/pubspec.yaml:38) and uses launchUrl(..., LaunchMode.externalApplication) in app/lib/features/support/help_centre_screen.dart:202. Only nuance: the `default:` comment shows the app author knowingly skipped it, but admin still requires a URL and the CF still persists it, so the feature is offered end-to-end and dead-ends silently.

findings.title: broadcasts.opened is written once as 0 and never updated, so the Opened column is always 0
findings.detail: The CF sets `opened: 0` at create; firestore.rules:221 makes broadcasts CF-write-only (`allow write: if false`) and no function ever updates the doc afterwards. The per-user inbox docs carry `broadcastId` (line 58) but the app's read-receipt path only flips `read` on customers/{uid}/notifications (app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:165 → markRead, permitted by firestore.rules:166-169) and never touches the broadcast aggregate. The admin list renders an "Opened" column from this field (NotificationsListPage.tsx:101).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sends a broadcast to 12,000 users; 4,000 open it in the app. The Push-notifications table permanently shows Sent 12,000 / Opened 0, so campaign effectiveness reads as zero for every broadcast ever sent.
findings.fix: Either aggregate opens server-side (a Firestore trigger on customers/{uid}/notifications update that increments broadcasts/{broadcastId}.opened when read flips to true) or remove the Opened column rather than displaying a metric that is structurally always 0.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:46 writes `opened: 0` at create and it is the only file in functions/src that touches the `broadcasts` collection; firebase/firestore.rules:221 sets `allow write: if false`, so no client can update it. The app's read-receipt path (app/lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:52-54 markRead → {'read':true,'readAt':...}) only updates customers/{uid}/notifications and never the aggregate, and the `broadcastId` field written at broadcast.ts:58 is never read by any code. functions/src/index.ts:1-16 documents that all document triggers were intentionally removed and none exist, and the only scheduled job is couponExpirySweep, so there is no fan-in path whatsoever. Admin reads and renders the field (NotificationsListPage.tsx:101). No compute-on-read fallback is even possible client-side: a collection-group query over notifications has no matching rules path. So the Opened column is permanently 0 for every broadcast. Not cosmetic (rendering is fine, the data pipeline is absent), not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and fixable within the architecture rules as a cross-user counter Cloud Function. Only hedge: the admin Broadcast type is prototype scaffolding (`opened?` "may be absent", unused statuses), so `opened: 0` could be an intentionally deferred analytics placeholder — but that is undocumented and the metric ships as real data.

findings.title: Spin cashback wallet ledger row records balanceAfterPaise: 0
findings.detail: Every other writer of customers/{uid}/walletTransactions stores the real post-transaction balance — wallet/topup.ts:98, wallet/adjust.ts:57, orders/cancel.ts:121, orders/checkout.ts:581, returns/decisions.ts:89. executeSpin hardcodes `balanceAfterPaise: 0` on the spin_reward credit even though it increments wallet.balancePaise by the same amount two lines earlier (line 114). The value is computable here: the transaction already has custSnap, so `Number(custSnap.get('wallet.balancePaise') ?? 0) + cashbackAmt` is available.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer with ₹800 in wallet wins ₹50 spin cashback. The wallet balance correctly becomes ₹850, but the ledger row for that credit claims the running balance was ₹0 — any reconciliation, export or future running-balance display over walletTransactions breaks at every spin-reward row, and the ledger contradicts the customer doc.
findings.fix: Compute the post-credit balance from the customer snapshot already read in the transaction and store it, matching the other five wallet writers.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed at /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:144. Inside the transaction, when a cashback slice is won the code increments `wallet.balancePaise` by `cashbackAmt` (line 114) but writes the ledger row with a literal `balanceAfterPaise: 0`, so the stored running balance is objectively false whenever the customer's pre-spin balance plus the cashback is non-zero.

I tried to refute it on four fronts and none held:
1. Handled elsewhere? No. Nothing back-fills or recomputes balanceAfterPaise — grep for `balanceAfter` across the repo hits only the six writers (spin/execute.ts, wallet/topup.ts:98, wallet/adjust.ts:57, orders/cancel.ts:121, orders/checkout.ts:581 and :595, returns/decisions.ts:89), the shared type, and scripts/seed.ts:527. Five of the six writers compute the real post-transaction balance from the customer doc they already read in the same transaction; only executeSpin hardcodes 0.
2. Intentional? No. The field is declared non-optional on `WalletTransaction` (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:153), and checkout.ts:588-590 carries an explicit comment reasoning about the correct value for a `spin_reward` row ("balanceAfterPaise is the balance after this order (unchanged by the reward)") — the semantics are deliberately maintained everywhere else, so 0 here is an oversight, not a convention. It is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list.
3. Unreachable? No. `cashback` is a valid prizeType in packages/shared/src/enums.ts, admin preserves it (admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:62), and scripts/seed.ts:748 seeds a live `₹50 cashback` slice with weight 10.
4. Cosmetic/UI? No. This is persisted money-ledger data written by a Cloud Function; the fix is a one-line server-side computation (`Number(custSnap.get('wallet.balancePaise') ?? 0) + cashbackAmt`, with custSnap already read at line 91) and touches no UI.

The one thing that tempers severity: no current reader consumes balanceAfterPaise — no Dart/TS/TSX file outside the writers and the type definition references it — so there is no user-visible breakage today. The harm is corrupt ledger data that contradicts the customer doc and will break any reconciliation/export/running-balance view. Real, fixable, low-impact defect.

findings.title: "Enable affiliate wallet access" toggle is a no-op — walletEnabled is sent, validated, then discarded
findings.detail: The Toggle drives `walletEnabled` state (line 33), which is forwarded through `allocateAffiliate({ uid, commissionRate, walletEnabled })` (line 55, api/affiliate.ts:58-65) into the callable. functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:20 accepts `walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional()` in the schema but line 23 destructures only `{ uid, commissionRate }` — the value is never written to the affiliate map (lines 32-42) and no field named `walletEnabled` exists anywhere on customer docs (repo-wide grep only hits `settings/paymentGateway.walletEnabled`, an unrelated checkout flag). The confirm dialog at line 130 even promises "and affiliate wallet access".
findings.failure_scenario: Admin allocates an affiliate with the wallet toggle OFF and confirms a dialog saying wallet access is withheld. The server grants full affiliate access anyway; the affiliate's wallet screen and requestWithdrawal work exactly as if it were ON. There is no state at all that reflects the toggle.
findings.fix: Either persist it (`affiliate.walletEnabled: parsed.data.walletEnabled ?? true` in adminAllocateAffiliate, and gate requestWithdrawal on it) or remove the toggle and the payload field plus the dialog copy that references it.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end. AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:33/55/115 drives `walletEnabled` into allocateAffiliate (api/affiliate.ts:58-65), which calls adminAllocateAffiliate. functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:20 validates `walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional()` but line 23 destructures only `{ uid, commissionRate }`; the affiliate map written at lines 32-42 never includes it, and packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:27-40 (AffiliateInfo) defines no wallet-access field at all — so there is nowhere for the value to be persisted. No compensating guard exists downstream: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:35-36 gates requestWithdrawal solely on `aff.enabled` (plus hasPendingWithdrawal/balance/min/bank). No other admin surface writes the field (AffiliateListPage.tsx has no wallet control), and every other repo hit for `walletEnabled` is the unrelated settings/paymentGateway checkout flag (web checkout page.tsx:117, app checkout_repository.dart:181, seed/bootstrap). Not covered by the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and not cosmetic — the confirm dialog at line 130 asserts wallet access is withheld while the server grants identical access either way.

findings.title: 'Auto-refund to wallet' toggle in Settings writes a field no code ever reads
findings.detail: `saveReturns({ id: 'returns', windowDays: days, autoRefundToWallet })` persists `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet`. Grepping every surface (functions/src, web/src, app/lib) for `autoRefund` returns only this writer, the type declaration (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:84) and the seeds. functions/src/returns/decisions.ts — the approval path — never loads `settings/returns`; it unconditionally takes `const toWallet = (r.refundMethod ?? 'wallet') === 'wallet'` (line 77) and `refundMethod` is itself hardcoded to `'wallet'` when the request is created (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:113). So the toggle can only ever be 'on' in effect.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin turns 'Auto-refund to wallet' off, expecting approved returns to stop crediting the wallet and to be settled manually. They see 'Return settings saved'. The next approved return still credits the customer's wallet and writes a walletTransactions ledger entry (decisions.ts:84-98), because no code path consults the flag.
findings.fix: Either read `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet` in adminApproveOrderRequest and branch the refund method on it, or remove the toggle from the Storefront tab until the server honours it.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. Repo-wide grep (all file types, incl. .dart and .rules, excluding node_modules) for `autoRefund` yields only: the writer admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx (280/285/296/329), the type packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:84, and the seeders scripts/seed.ts:208 + scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117. No reader in functions/src, web/src, app/lib, or firestore.rules. The approval path functions/src/returns/decisions.ts (adminApproveOrderRequest) reads only orderRequests/{id}, orders/{id}, customers/{id} and the legacy item doc — it never loads settings/returns — and decides via `const toWallet = (r.refundMethod ?? 'wallet') === 'wallet'` (line 77), while refundMethod is hardcoded to 'wallet' at creation in functions/src/returns/requests.ts:113. So there is no server-side guard or fallback that could honour the flag. The sibling field windowDays from the same doc IS consumed (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:261, web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:71, .../return/page.tsx:26), so this is specifically a write-only field, not an unused settings doc. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, no deferral comment. Behavioral (admin toggles off, sees 'Return settings saved', wallet is still credited and a walletTransactions ledger row written at decisions.ts ~81-100), and fixable server-side without any UI change — decisions.ts/requests.ts can consult settings/returns to set refundMethod.

findings.title: admins.lastActiveAt / lastLoginAt are rendered but nothing ever updates them
findings.detail: The Sub Admin table shows `timeAgo(a.lastActiveAt?.toDate?.())` and the profile sheet shows `Last login: {dateShort(admin.lastLoginAt?.toDate?.())}` (admin/src/features/account/AccountDialogs.tsx:95). Both fields are written exactly once, at creation: functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:44 sets `lastLoginAt: null, lastActiveAt: now`, and scripts/seed.ts:88-89 does the same. A full grep of admin/src, functions/src and scripts finds no other writer. The client cannot patch them either — firebase/firestore.rules:192 makes `/admins/{uid}` `write: if false` — and `signInAdmin` (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:18) performs no write on a successful login.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin created six months ago and signing in daily still shows 'Last active: 6 months ago' in the Sub Admin table, and their Profile dialog shows 'Last login: —' forever. A super admin auditing who is still using the console gets data that is guaranteed wrong, and cannot tell a dormant account from an active one.
findings.fix: Stamp `lastLoginAt`/`lastActiveAt` server-side — e.g. a small `touchAdminSession` callable guarded by requireAdmin that updates the caller's own admins doc, invoked from signInAdmin (and on route changes if 'last active' is meant to be live).

verdict.reason:
Verified and could not refute. Exhaustive grep for `lastActiveAt|lastLoginAt` across the whole repo (excluding node_modules) returns writers only at creation/seed time: functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:44 (`lastLoginAt: null, lastActiveAt: now` inside createSubAdmin), scripts/seed.ts:88-89, scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:59-60. The other subAdmins CFs (updateSubAdmin :68-71, suspendSubAdmin :93-96, deleteSubAdmin) never touch either field, and grep -rl "admins" over functions/src shows only _lib/guards.ts (read-only `db.doc('admins/'+uid).get()`), index.ts and subAdmins.ts — there is no scheduled sweep, no auth blocking function (`beforeSignIn`/blocking functions: zero hits), and no trigger recomputing activity from auditLogs.

The client cannot fill the gap either: firebase/firestore.rules:191 is `allow write: if false; // via createSubAdmin/updateSubAdmin/... CFs only` for /admins/{adminUid}, and admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts signInAdmin only does signInWithEmailAndPassword + getDoc(admins/{uid}) + getIdToken(true) — no write, no callable. (The rules do allow customers to self-patch lastActiveAt at firestore.rules:135, which shows the pattern exists for customers but was never wired for admins.)

So both consumers render permanently stale data: SubAdminListPage.tsx:144 `timeAgo(a.lastActiveAt?.toDate?.())` is frozen at account-creation time forever, and AccountDialogs.tsx:95 `Last login: {dateShort(admin.lastLoginAt?.toDate?.())}` renders "—" forever since the field is initialised to null and never written. This is not cosmetic — it is a missing state write; the fix is server-side (a touch/recordAdminLogin callable, or a rules-scoped self-update of just these two fields) with no UI change. It is also not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and does not violate the CF-only-for-money rule (the admins collection is already CF-write-only by design).

findings.title: Dashboard KPI aggregate fallback silently caps at 500/1000 docs, producing wrong lifetime revenue and AOV
findings.detail: sumTotalPaise catches ANY error from getAggregateFromServer and falls back to `getDocs(query(..., limit(500)))` (line 49); countOrders falls back to `limit(1000)` (line 59). The catch is unqualified, so a transient failure, an unsupported aggregate path, or the emulator case named in the comment all silently return a partial number with no error surfaced. The two fallbacks use different caps, so the AOV numerator and denominator are truncated inconsistently at line 110 (`lifetimeRevenue / totalOrders`). Note the fallback for the lifetime sum has no orderBy, so the 500 documents it picks are arbitrary.
findings.failure_scenario: Store has 3,000 orders averaging ₹2,000. Aggregates fail once → lifetimeRevenue = sum of an arbitrary 500 orders (~₹10,00,000), totalOrders = 1,000 (capped). Avg order value renders ₹1,000 — half the true value — and "Total orders" reads 1,000 instead of 3,000, with no error indicator anywhere on the page.
findings.fix: Only fall back for the specific unimplemented-aggregate error; otherwise rethrow so react-query surfaces isError. If a fallback runs, page through with startAfter until exhausted rather than truncating, or mark the KPI as approximate in the returned object so the card can say so.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts. `sumTotalPaise` (lines 41-52) wraps `getAggregateFromServer` in an unqualified `catch {}` and falls back to `getDocs(query(ordersCol(), ...constraints, limit(500)))` with no orderBy, so the 500 docs are arbitrary; `countOrders` (lines 54-62) falls back to `limit(1000)`. Nothing anywhere re-checks or surfaces the failure: the catch swallows the error, react-query resolves successfully (staleTime 30s caches the bad value), and /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/dashboard/routes/DashboardPage.tsx renders `k.totalOrders` and `avgOrderValuePaise` with only `kpis.isLoading` — no error branch. There is no alternative counter/stats doc for these KPIs (the only other aggregate calls in admin are in features/categories/api/categories.ts, unrelated), so the value is not "written by another surface". Line 110 divides the (≤500-doc) lifetime sum by the (≤1000-doc) count, mixing two different truncated populations, which is wrong in a way neither cap alone would be.

Reachability is not theoretical: Firestore sum()/average() aggregations need an index covering the aggregated field, and /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.indexes.json contains no orders index mentioning totalPaise (grep returns nothing) — the range-filtered sums (today, yesterday, 30d, 60d) can hit a permanent FAILED_PRECONDITION rather than a transient error, making the silent fallback the steady-state path. Even setting that aside, permission/offline/emulator paths reach the same catch. firebase ^10.13.0 does support sum(), so the "older SDK" justification in the comment is stale.

This is a data-correctness bug in the API layer (admin KPIs reporting materially wrong revenue/AOV/order counts), fixable without touching UI — e.g. narrow the catch, use a consistent cap, or propagate the error so react-query reports it. It is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and does not follow from any architecture rule. Confidence is medium only because exact aggregate-index requirements vary by query shape; the code-level defect itself (mismatched caps, arbitrary 500-doc sample, fully swallowed error) is unambiguous.

findings.title: Category performance panel is hardcoded to four seed category ids and ignores the categories collection
findings.detail: CATEGORY_META hardcodes exactly `perfumes | clothing | books | islamic`, and categoryPerformance returns `Object.entries(CATEGORY_META).map(...)` (line 176) — it iterates the hardcoded map, not the totals actually accumulated from `p.categoryId` (line 173). Category ids are admin-authored slugs: saveCategory writes `setDoc(doc(db,'categories', slug), { id: slug, ... })` with `slug = slugify(values.name)` (admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:71,89). The four literals only match because scripts/seed.ts:269-272 seeds those ids. The panel also uses lifetime `soldCount` (units, not revenue) and ignores the 12M/30D/7D range selector sitting next to it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates "Dates & Gifts" (id `dates-gifts`) and it becomes the best seller, then deletes the seeded `books` category. Dashboard still lists Perfumes/Clothing/Books/Islamic; Books shows 0% for a category that no longer exists, and the top-selling real category is never displayed at all. On any store not built from the seed, all four bars read 0%.
findings.fix: Drive the panel from the live `categories` collection (useCategories, CATEGORIES_KEY) joined to the per-categoryId totals, taking label/tint from the category doc, and aggregate order line revenue over the selected range instead of lifetime soldCount.

verdict.reason: Real defect, not refutable. dashboard.ts:176 iterates the hardcoded CATEGORY_META (4 seed slugs) rather than the `totals` map accumulated from p.categoryId, so any admin-created category is invisible and any deleted seed category still renders. Categories are genuinely dynamic: saveCategory writes categories/{slugify(name)} from the reachable /categories/new route (categories.ts:71,89; CategoryFormPage.tsx:25,92,127) and deleteCategory removes them; Product.categoryId is plain `string` (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:60), and CATEGORY_KEYS (enums.ts:199) is referenced nowhere outside its own type alias, so it is not a write-side guard. There is no fallback elsewhere — categoryPerformance has exactly one consumer (DashboardPage.tsx:46). Worse than described: `max` at line 175 is computed over ALL totals including unlisted categories, so a real non-seed best-seller silently shrinks every displayed bar. Not cosmetic and not a UI change: the render is already `cats.map(...)` keyed by c.key (DashboardPage.tsx:151) and handles an arbitrary-length list, so the fix is confined to the data function in dashboard.ts (derive rows from the live categories collection, as every other admin surface does via useCategories()). The secondary sub-claims are weaker — soldCount-vs-revenue is documented as intended (line 169 doc comment) and the 12M/30D/7D selector drives the separate useRevenueTrend panel — but the hardcoded category list is a genuine, fixable functional defect.

findings.title: Reports CSV export writes rounded display strings instead of numeric amounts
findings.detail: downloadReportCsv emits `formatMoneyCompact(kpis.totalRevenuePaise)` (line 259), `formatMoneyInt(b.paise)` for every trend row (line 265) and `formatMoneyCompact(r.revenuePaise)` per product (line 268). packages/shared/src/money.ts formatMoneyCompact returns `₹X.XL` / `₹X.XX Cr` — 1–2 significant decimals — and formatMoneyInt returns Indian-grouped digits with commas, which the escaper at line 252 then wraps in quotes. The CSV therefore contains currency-symbol text, not numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: Total revenue of 123456700 paise (₹12,34,567) exports as the cell `₹12.3L`, losing ₹4,567. A month bar of ₹1,23,456 exports as `"₹1,23,456"`. Opening the file in Excel/Sheets gives text columns that cannot be summed, charted or reconciled against the ledger — the export is unusable for its only purpose.
findings.fix: Export raw values (paise, or rupees as `paise/100` with 2dp) in dedicated numeric columns — e.g. `Total revenue,${kpis.totalRevenuePaise / 100}` — and keep formatted strings out of the file, or add them as a separate human-readable column alongside the numeric one.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts. Line 259 writes esc(formatMoneyCompact(kpis.totalRevenuePaise)), line 265 esc(formatMoneyInt(b.paise)) per trend bar, line 268 esc(formatMoneyCompact(r.revenuePaise)) per product. packages/shared/src/money.ts:39-46 shows formatMoneyCompact truncates to 1-2 decimals with a Cr/L/K suffix and formatMoneyInt rounds to whole rupees with Indian comma grouping and a leading ₹; the escaper at line 252 then quotes anything containing a comma. The example verifies exactly: 123456700 paise -> 1234567 rupees -> >=1e5 -> (12.34567).toFixed(1) -> the cell "₹12.3L", losing ₹4,567. The path is reachable (ReportsPage.tsx:100 wires the Export button to downloadReportCsv); there is no other numeric export of report data, no server-side re-export, and no test pinning the formatted output. Refutation fails on convention too: every other admin CSV export writes raw paise integers with Paise-suffixed headers (OrdersListPage.tsx:45 TotalPaise, PaymentsListPage.tsx:57 AmountPaise, AffiliateListPage.tsx:83 Pending/Confirmed/LifetimePaise, ProductsListPage.tsx:101 PricePaise, ReturnsListPage.tsx:65 AmountPaise) - reports is the lone outlier. Not a KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item and not cosmetic: this is file serialization, not rendering (ReportsPage.tsx:129/166/191 keep their own formatMoneyCompact calls for display and need no change). Real, functional, and fixable by emitting the raw *Paise integers.

findings.title: "Skip" on Create Profile writes only a device-local pref; `customers.profileSkipped` is never written and the flag is never cleared on sign-out
findings.detail: `_skip()` calls `AppPrefs.setProfileSkipped()` (SharedPreferences, device-wide, not per-uid) and nothing else. The `profileSkipped` field that scripts/seed.ts:422 seeds and packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:116 declares is written only as `false` by `_defaultCustomer` (auth_repository.dart:215) — no code anywhere ever sets it true, so it is a field nothing writes. AppPrefs also has no clear-on-sign-out: `AuthProvider.signOut()` (core/services/auth_provider.dart:64) just calls FirebaseAuth.signOut, and the log-out handler in profile_screen.dart:372 does no prefs cleanup.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer A signs in on a shared/handed-down phone and taps Skip (`profileSkipped=true` on the device). They log out; customer B signs in with a different number. Splash (splash_screen.dart:53-56) reads `complete=false, skipped=true` and sends B straight to Home with a blank profile — B is never asked for a name, and Profile shows "Your account". Meanwhile admin/web see `profileSkipped: false` for both, so they cannot distinguish a skipped profile from an abandoned one.
findings.fix: Persist `profileSkipped: true` on `customers/{uid}` in `_skip()` (the field is allowed by the update rule) and read it from the doc in splash; if the local pref is kept, key it by uid and clear it in the sign-out path.

verdict.reason: Verified as a real defect, though the reporter's failure scenario is somewhat overstated. Confirmed: create_profile_screen.dart:63-66 `_skip()` does only `AppPrefs.setProfileSkipped()` + navigate — no Firestore write. app_prefs.dart stores `profileSkipped` as an un-namespaced device-wide bool with no remove/clear helper. A repo-wide grep for `profileSkipped` finds it declared in packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:116, seeded in scripts/seed.ts:422, and explicitly listed in the owner-writable `onlyFields` allowlist in firebase/firestore.rules:134 (so it was designed to be client-written), yet the only writers are `_defaultCustomer` (auth_repository.dart:215) and web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:38, both writing `false`. Nothing sets it true on any surface — web's "Skip for now" (create-profile/page.tsx:122) is a bare router.replace('/') that persists nothing. AuthProvider.signOut() (auth_provider.dart:64) is FirebaseAuth.signOut only; the log-out handler at profile_screen.dart:372-374 does no prefs cleanup; there is no other clear-on-sign-out. splash_screen.dart:53-56 really does route on `complete || skipped`, and app_router.dart:139-145 has no profile-completeness guard and no server-side re-check. Correction to the claim: on the sign-in path otp_screen.dart:101-104 routes on ensureCustomerDoc()'s profileComplete (ignoring the pref), so a new customer B IS shown Create Profile right after OTP; the stale flag only leaks on a later cold start (kill app at Create Profile, relaunch → splash sees complete=false/skipped=true → Home, never prompted again). Still a genuine cross-account device-local state leak plus a declared/rules-allowed field that nothing ever writes, so admin/web cannot distinguish skipped from abandoned. Fixable within the architecture rules (direct owner write, already permitted by rules); not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and not cosmetic.

findings.title: Pull-to-refresh during an in-flight page load silently drops the first page and leaves the cursor mid-catalogue
findings.detail: `_refresh()` clears `_items`, nulls `_cursor` and resets `_hasMore`, then awaits `_loadMore()`. But `_loadMore` opens with `if (_loading || !_hasMore) return;` (line 78), so when a prefetch triggered by `_onScroll` (line 71-75) is still in flight, `_refresh`'s call is a no-op and the RefreshIndicator completes with an empty grid. The still-running prefetch captured `var cursor = _cursor` at line 88 BEFORE the reset, and on completion does `_items.addAll(gained); _cursor = cursor;` (lines 98-99), repopulating the list from where the old cursor left off.
findings.failure_scenario: Catalogue has 90 published products. User scrolls the 'All products' grid; the prefetch for page 2 (products 31-60) fires and `_loading` is true. Mid-flight the user pulls to refresh. `_items` is cleared but `_loadMore` bails. The in-flight page then lands: the grid now contains only products 31-60 and `_cursor` points at product 60, so products 1-30 are permanently missing from the list and further scrolling appends 61-90 after them. A second pull-to-refresh is required to recover.
findings.fix: Make `_refresh` cancel/ignore in-flight work: bump a generation counter in `_refresh`, capture it in `_loadMore`, and discard the result in the `setState` at line 96-102 if the counter changed. Also drop the `_loading` early-return for the refresh path (or `await` the in-flight future before resetting).

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading app/lib/features/catalog/product_list_screen.dart in full plus app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart. _loadMore (line 78) hard-bails on `_loading`, and _refresh (112-120) has no way to bypass it, so a refresh issued while an _onScroll prefetch (71-75) is in flight clears _items/_cursor/_hasMore and then does nothing. The in-flight call captured `var cursor = _cursor` at line 88 before the reset and, guarded only by `mounted`, commits `_items.addAll(gained); _cursor = cursor;` at 97-99 — repopulating the cleared list with page N+1 and restoring the pre-refresh cursor. Because productsPage orders by FieldPath.documentId with startAfterDocument (catalog_repository.dart:40-59), the skipped earlier documents are never re-fetched; they stay missing from the grid until a second pull-to-refresh. No guard exists elsewhere: _refresh is referenced only at line 154 and the RefreshIndicator is not disabled while loading; there is no request-generation token in the class. Reachability is real, not theoretical — with maxCrossAxisExtent 210 a wide screen shows 4-5 columns, so 30 items put the `maxScrollExtent - 600` prefetch threshold only a few hundred pixels from the top; on a phone a fling back to the top during a slow Firestore page does it. Not cosmetic (wrong dataset + corrupted cursor, not styling), not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and fixable without any UI change via a generation counter checked before the setState at line 97. Confidence is medium only because it is a timing race whose window depends on network latency; the code defect itself is unambiguous. Minor correction to the claim: with _items empty and _loading true the build returns _GridSkeleton (line 141-142) rather than an empty grid, which makes the failure even quieter than described.

findings.title: Payment-gateway settings default to disabled in the app but enabled on web — a partially configured settings doc hides wallet and online payment only in the app
findings.detail: `fetchSettings` reads `walletEnabled: (g['walletEnabled'] as bool?) ?? false` (line 181) and `onlinePaymentEnabled: (g['onlinePaymentEnabled'] as bool?) ?? false` (line 182), and the `StoreSettings` defaults used when the fetch throws are also `false` (lines 21-22). The web reads the same doc with the opposite fallback: `onlineEnabled = gateway?.onlinePaymentEnabled ?? true` and `walletEnabled = gateway?.walletEnabled ?? true` (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:117-118), documented there as 'A missing settings doc means "everything on"'. checkout_screen.dart:250 carries that same comment ('missing settings ⇒ everything on') while the code does the opposite. Only `onlinePaymentEnabled` has an accidental rescue (`|| s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty`, line 254); the wallet has none.
findings.failure_scenario: `settings/paymentGateway` exists but predates the wallet toggle (or `_loadSettings` throws once on a flaky first load, falling back to `const StoreSettings()`). On web the customer sees the 'Use wallet balance' switch and can spend their ₹500 wallet; in the app the wallet card never renders (`walletEnabled = false && ...`) and `draft.useWallet` is force-reset to false by the post-frame callback at line 279-282, so the same customer cannot spend their wallet at all and is charged the full amount.
findings.fix: Change the fallbacks in `fetchSettings` and the `StoreSettings` field defaults for `walletEnabled`, `onlinePaymentEnabled` (and `codEnabled`, already true) to `true`, matching the web's documented 'missing settings ⇒ everything on' contract.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. checkout_repository.dart:181-182 uses `?? false` for walletEnabled/onlinePaymentEnabled while the adjacent codEnabled on line 179 uses `?? true`, and web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:116-118 uses `?? true` for all three with the comment "A missing settings doc means 'everything on'". The app's own comments state the same intent while the code does the opposite (checkout_screen.dart:175 "Fall back to the defaults in [StoreSettings] (everything on)" and :250 "missing settings => everything on"), so this is an oversight rather than a deliberate fail-closed policy. It is not rescued elsewhere: only onlineEnabled gets `|| s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty` (checkout_screen.dart:254), and in the fallback path razorpayKeyId is '' so online is disabled too; the wallet has no rescue and is actively force-off (draft.useWallet reset at :279-282, null wallet balance passed to computeSummary at :289), so the customer cannot spend wallet balance at all and pays the full amount. Reachability does not depend on the speculative "legacy doc" half of the claim: _loadSettings() runs once in initState with no retry (checkout_screen.dart:160-176), so one transient read failure of settings/paymentGateway (reads are App-Check-gated at firebase/firestore.rules:48 and clients send an invalid token) leaves the session COD-only with no wallet, diverging from web. Not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, not cosmetic (it changes the amount charged), and the fix is two default values in the data layer with no UI change. Confidence is medium only because seed.ts:180, bootstrap-real.ts:114 and admin savePaymentGateway all write the full gateway doc, so on a healthy install with a successful fetch the divergence never surfaces.

findings.title: Applied coupon discount is a frozen snapshot — editing quantities after applying shows a wrong discount and can make placeOrder hard-fail
findings.detail: `CouponRewardBanner`'s Apply writes `AppliedCoupon(code: best.code, discountPaise: best.discountPaise, ...)` (lines 87-92) where `best.discountPaise` was computed by `listAvailableOffers` against the subtotal at that instant; `CouponScreen._applyOffer` does the same (coupon_screen.dart:69-73). Nothing recomputes it when the cart changes — `CheckoutDraft.coupon` is a plain field (checkout_draft.dart:13) and `computeSummary` only clamps it with `.clamp(0, subtotalPaise)` (checkout_repository.dart:196). The app makes this trivially reachable because the Bag screen renders the quantity steppers and `CouponRewardBanner`/`CouponRow` in the same scrolling list (bag_screen.dart:110-115), so applying and then editing quantities is a two-tap sequence on one screen. `placeOrder` re-derives the discount from the live cart and throws `failed-precondition` if the minimum is no longer met (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:143-145, 187).
findings.failure_scenario: Customer with a ₹1,200 bag taps Apply on 'SPIN200 · ₹200 off · min cart ₹1,000'. Still on the Bag screen, they decrement a ₹400 item to bring the bag to ₹800. The bag total and the checkout summary still show '−₹200' and the pay bar still reads 'Place order · ₹600'. Tapping it calls placeOrder, which rejects with 'Your cart does not meet this coupon’s minimum.' — an error toast with no indication that the coupon is the problem and no way forward except guessing to clear the coupon. A percent coupon shows the wrong amount instead (10% applied at ₹1,000 stays '−₹100' after the cart grows to ₹5,000, while the server charges −₹500).
findings.fix: Store only the coupon code/metadata in `CheckoutDraft` and recompute `discountPaise` from the current `subtotalPaise` on every build (re-running the same `offers.dart` math for the applied code), clearing the coupon with a toast when the cart drops below its minimum.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end and could not refute it. AppliedCoupon.discountPaise is written once from listAvailableOffers against the subtotal at tap time (coupon_apply.dart:87-92, coupon_screen.dart:69-73, and also the CF applyCoupon path at checkout_repository.dart:251-255). CheckoutDraft.coupon (checkout_draft.dart:13) has no cart observer — the only writers are the two Apply surfaces and the two manual clear buttons; reset() only runs post-order. Every consumer merely clamps: computeSummary (checkout_repository.dart:195-197), the Bag summary (bag_screen.dart:241) and the Bag pay bar (bag_screen.dart:349). It is trivially reachable: bag_screen.dart:110-115 puts CouponRewardBanner/CouponRow in the same ListView as _CartLineCard, whose stepper calls cart.increment (bag_screen.dart:211-213). The server does re-derive from live lines and throws failed-precondition (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:143-145 and :187). Two caveats that weaken but do not kill the claim: (1) the reporter's "no indication the coupon is the problem, no way forward" is wrong — checkout_screen.dart:131 surfaces the server message verbatim and the × clear chip is on the same screen, so the min-not-met case is recoverable; (2) web has the identical frozen snapshot (web checkout page.tsx:103, bag page.tsx:53), so the app is mirroring web, not deviating. What still stands as a real, non-cosmetic defect is the percent-coupon divergence: the client quotes a discount from a stale subtotal while placeOrder/createRazorpayOrder charge one computed from the live cart, so the displayed pay-bar amount can differ from the amount actually charged. The fix is state logic (recompute or invalidate the coupon when subtotalPaise changes), not a UI change, so it is not excluded as cosmetic and is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list.

findings.title: CartProvider resets _inFlight to 0 while a write is in flight, underflowing the counter and permanently disabling snapshot suppression
findings.detail: `_onAuthChanged` unconditionally does `_inFlight = 0;` (line 227) without waiting for outstanding `_flush` calls. Any `_flush` already past its `_inFlight++` (line 180) still runs its `finally { _inFlight--; }` (line 198), taking the counter to -1. `_busy` is defined as `_inFlight > 0 || (_debounce?.isActive ?? false)` (line 74), so from that point on a write in flight leaves `_inFlight` at 0 and `_busy` false. The whole optimistic-write design depends on `_busy` being true during a write to ignore the stale server echo (lines 238-241); with the counter offset by -1 that protection is silently off for the rest of the process's life, and `_maybeReconcile`'s `!_busy` guard (line 214) also misfires.
findings.failure_scenario: User taps '+' on a bag line (immediate `_flush`, `_inFlight == 1`), then signs out from Settings before the write returns. `_onAuthChanged` zeroes `_inFlight`; the in-flight flush settles afterwards and decrements it to -1. The user signs back in (or the write settles after the sign-in `_onAuthChanged`). Now every subsequent '+' tap runs with `_busy == false`, so the pre-write `customers/{uid}` snapshot is applied over the optimistic state: the quantity visibly jumps back to the old value for a moment on every tap, and a debounced multi-tap sequence can end up reconciled to a stale value.
findings.fix: Track outstanding writes with a generation/epoch token instead of resetting the counter — e.g. bump an `_epoch` in `_onAuthChanged` and have `_flush` skip its `_inFlight--`/reconcile work when its captured epoch is stale, or guard with `_inFlight = _inFlight < 0 ? 0 : _inFlight` and never reset it from outside `_flush`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real defect. app/lib/core/services/cart_provider.dart:227 blanket-zeroes _inFlight on auth change, while _flush's finally at line 198 decrements unconditionally — it never compares its captured uid to _uid and _onAuthChanged never bumps _gen or uses an epoch, so any flush past line 180 when auth changes drives the counter to -1. The window is genuine: CartRepository.replace (app/lib/features/cart/data/cart_repository.dart:38) returns the Firestore set(merge:true) future, which resolves only on server ack and is unbounded while offline. The error path doesn't save it either — after sign-out the write throws permission-denied, gen == _gen still holds (no _gen bump), getOnce also throws, and the finally still runs. CartProvider is a process-lifetime singleton (app/lib/main.dart:34, `late final CartProvider _cart = CartProvider(_auth)`), never recreated on sign-out/sign-in, so with _inFlight at -1 every later _flush increments to 0 and _busy (line 74) stays false for the whole write; _debounce is cancelled at line 178 so it doesn't cover the gap. Consequence is functional, not cosmetic: the pre-write snapshot is applied over the optimistic lines (238-245), a following tap computes setQty from the reverted quantity so a user edit is lost and the stale value is what the next debounced flush persists; _suppressedSnapshot also never gets set so _maybeReconcile (206) stops covering cross-device changes. No sibling handles it (wishlist_provider has no in-flight counter), and it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Fixable by guarding the decrement with a captured epoch rather than resetting the counter.

findings.title: App tax invoice omits delivery and COD surcharge, so the printed figures never add up
findings.detail: The invoice card renders line items, then only a deduction line (invoice_screen.dart:179-183) and a tax line (invoice_screen.dart:184-186), then 'Total paid' (invoice_screen.dart:193-206). `order.deliveryPaise` and `order.codSurchargePaise` are parsed in the model (order.dart:229-230) but are never rendered anywhere in the app. The web invoice for the same order DOES render a Delivery row (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:78-83), so the two surfaces print different invoices for the same document.
findings.failure_scenario: COD order: subtotal Rs 500, delivery Rs 49, COD surcharge Rs 20, no tax, total Rs 569. The app invoice lists 'Item x 1  Rs 500.00' and then 'Total paid  Rs 569.00' with Rs 69 completely unexplained; the same order viewed on the web shows the Rs 49 delivery row.
findings.fix: Add the missing rows to the invoice card (delivery when `order.deliveryPaise > 0`, COD charge when `order.codSurchargePaise > 0`), matching the web invoice's row set so both surfaces reconcile to Total paid.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:160-206 renders only line items, the combined deduction line, tax, then 'Total paid' (order.paidPaise = amountPaidPaise || totalPaise, which DOES include delivery + COD). order.deliveryPaise / codSurchargePaise are parsed at app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:229-230 but a repo-wide grep shows they are never rendered anywhere in the app outside checkout_screen.dart:746-752 — order_detail_screen.dart only prints 'Paid via X'. The amounts are real and reachable: scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:113 sets standardFeePaise Rs 49 / codSurchargePaise Rs 20 / freeDeliveryOverPaise Rs 1499, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:288-302,501 writes both onto the order doc, so any order under Rs 1499 or any COD order shows an unexplained gap between the itemised rows and the total. Both other renderings of the same document include Delivery: web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:78-83 and the server-generated authoritative tax invoice functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:48. No guard, fallback or server-side re-render supplies the missing rows, and nothing in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list covers it. This is a completeness/correctness gap in a tax document (charged amounts not itemised), not cosmetic styling, and the data is already on the model. One correction to the claim: the COD surcharge is also omitted from the web invoice and from the generated PDF (invoice.ts:46-50 prints Subtotal/Delivery/GST/Total), so only the Delivery row is a genuine app-vs-web mismatch; the COD omission is a shared gap.

findings.title: App shows a spinnable wheel for campaigns outside their startsAt/endsAt window, so 'Spin now' always fails
findings.detail: `activeCampaign()` filters only on `status == 'active'` (spin_repository.dart:21-26). `executeSpin` additionally rejects the spin when `now < startsAt || now > endsAt` with `failed-precondition` (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:57-59). Nothing ever flips a spin campaign's `status` — functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts contains only `couponExpirySweep`, and the `flashSaleStatusFlip` mentioned in functions/src/index.ts:71 is not implemented or exported. The admin explicitly models this state: admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:73-75 derives the labels 'Scheduled' (startsAt in future) and 'Ended' (endsAt past) for campaigns whose stored `status` is still 'active', and `createCampaign` (spinner.ts:113-118) will happily write `status:'active'` with a future `startsAt` when 'Activate immediately' is ticked.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates a campaign starting next Monday with 'Activate immediately' ticked → `status:'active'`, `startsAt` = next Monday. Today a customer opens Spin & Win: the wheel renders, the copy says 'You have 3 free spins today', and 'Spin now' is enabled. Tapping it calls `executeSpin`, which throws `failed-precondition`, and the customer just gets an error toast — with no way to succeed. The same happens indefinitely after `endsAt` passes, because nothing ever moves the status off 'active'.
findings.fix: Filter the window client-side in `activeCampaign()` (drop campaigns whose `startsAt > now` or `endsAt < now`) so the screen falls through to the existing 'No spins available right now' state, and/or add a scheduled function that flips `spinCampaigns.status` to 'ended' past `endsAt`.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; I could not refute it. (1) Client read has no window filter: app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:21-26 queries spinCampaigns where status=='active' only, and app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_campaign.dart never parses startsAt/endsAt, so the model cannot gate on the window. (2) No UI guard: app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:231 computes canSpin = hasData && spinsLeft > 0 && !_spinning; the button (line 252) and the centre-hub tap target (line 295) are both enabled, and the only handling of a server rejection is an error toast (lines 73-77). Entry is unconditional from profile_screen.dart:73. (3) The server does reject: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:57-59 throws failed-precondition when now < startsAt || now > endsAt. (4) Nothing ever flips status: functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts exports only couponExpirySweep (index.ts:58); flashSaleStatusFlip appears only in a comment (index.ts:71), never implemented or exported. Admin's sole status writer is setCampaignStatus, called only by CampaignDetailPage.tsx:253-259 as a manual active<->paused toggle — nothing ever writes 'ended'. (5) The state is reachable and eventually inevitable: admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:110-118 writes status:'active' with an arbitrary startsAt when 'Activate immediately' is ticked (CreateCampaignPage puts no min on the start-date input), and deriveSpinStatus (spinner.ts:67-78) explicitly renders 'Scheduled'/'Ended' for campaigns whose stored status is still 'active'. Even with a sane start date, every campaign passes endsAt (seed camp_1 ends 20 days out) and then stays 'active' forever, so the app keeps showing a live wheel plus "You have N free spins today" with a Spin button that always errors. Not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and not cosmetic: it is a functionally dead action. The fix is a data-layer window check in the repository (compute-on-read, the same pattern the architecture rules mandate for coupon expiry), which falls through to the existing "No spins available right now" empty state. The web has the identical gap (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:52), but that is a mirrored defect, not a justification.

findings.title: Notification deep links of type 'url' are a silent no-op — the admin's "Custom URL" broadcast option produces a dead card
findings.detail: `_onTap` switches on `n.deepLinkType` and handles only `product`, `category`, `home`; `default: break; // url / none — no in-app destination` (lines 167-183). The admin panel offers `url` as a first-class deep-link type (`DEEP_LINK_TYPES` in admin/src/features/notifications/api/notifications.ts:118-123, with a "Enter a URL to link to" validation at NotificationCreatePage.tsx:81) and `adminSendBroadcastNotification` persists it verbatim as `deepLink: {type:'url', target:'https://…'}` (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:55-58). The app model parses it correctly (app_notification.dart:55-62) but nothing consumes it — the whole card is a `GestureDetector` with `onTap` (notifications_screen.dart:196), so it looks tappable and does nothing. `url_launcher` is not used anywhere for this.
findings.failure_scenario: Marketing sends a broadcast "Diwali sale — see the lookbook" with a Custom URL deep link. Every app customer taps the notification card; the row just turns from unread to read and nothing opens. The campaign link is unreachable from the app.
findings.fix: Handle `case 'url'` by launching the target with `url_launcher` (`launchUrl(Uri.parse(target), mode: LaunchMode.externalApplication)`), guarding against malformed/non-http targets, or remove `url` from the admin's deep-link options.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end and could not refute it. (1) Admin genuinely exposes the type: admin/src/features/notifications/api/notifications.ts declares DeepLinkType = 'home'|'product'|'category'|'url' and DEEP_LINK_TYPES includes { value: 'url', label: 'Custom URL' }; admin/src/features/notifications/routes/NotificationCreatePage.tsx renders that list (line 201) and sends the chosen deepLink via sendBroadcast (line 98). (2) The CF persists it verbatim: functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts validates deepLink as {type: string, target: string|null} (line 16) and writes `deepLink: deepLink ?? null` onto both the broadcast doc (line 45) and every customers/{uid}/notifications row (line 57) — no filtering of type 'url'. (3) The app parses it: app/lib/features/notifications/data/app_notification.dart lines 51-62 sets deepLinkType/deepLinkTarget and even coerces a legacy bare-string deepLink to type 'url'. (4) Nothing consumes it: `grep -rn deepLink app/lib` returns only the model plus notifications_screen.dart:166-167; _onTap handles product/category/home and ends with `default: break; // url / none — no in-app destination` (lines 181-182) while the whole card is a GestureDetector with onTap (line 196), so the row looks tappable and only flips read state. Refutation attempts that failed: no FCM/push tap handler or router redirect handles it anywhere in app/lib; the web surface does not handle deep links at all (web/src/app/(shop)/account/notifications/page.tsx has no deepLink or router usage), so "mirror the web" does not excuse it — the app already implements product/category/home, leaving 'url' the lone gap; it is not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list; and it is not cosmetic — the fix is functional and one line (launchUrl(Uri.parse(target), mode: LaunchMode.externalApplication)), with url_launcher: ^6.3.0 already in app/pubspec.yaml and already used exactly that way in app/lib/features/support/help_centre_screen.dart:202, so no new dependency and no UI change is required. Only caveat: impact is bounded to campaigns that actually use the Custom URL option, but the path is real, reachable and dead.

findings.title: markAllRead reads the whole unread set and commits one batch — >500 unread rows makes the badge impossible to clear
findings.detail: `markAllRead` does an unbounded `.get()` of every `read == false` doc and puts one `batch.update` per doc into a single `WriteBatch` (lines 40-49). Firestore caps a batch at 500 writes, so with 501+ unread rows `batch.commit()` rejects with INVALID_ARGUMENT and *no* row is marked read (batches are atomic). The failure is invisible: it is invoked fire-and-forget from `dispose()` (notifications_screen.dart:36) and from the "Mark all read" tap (notifications_screen.dart:107) with no `catch`, so the Future error is unhandled and the user sees nothing. `all(uid)` (line 29) is likewise an unbounded read of the entire inbox with no `limit`, since inbox rows are never deleted (rules forbid client delete, firestore.rules:170).
findings.failure_scenario: A long-standing customer accumulates 600 unread broadcast/order notifications. They open the inbox and tap "Mark all read"; the commit is rejected, every row stays unread, and the home bell dot plus the profile unread pill are stuck at 9+ forever — repeating the action can never succeed.
findings.fix: Chunk the updates into batches of ≤450 docs (and/or query with `.limit(450)` in a loop) and add a `.catchError` so failures are at least logged; add a `limit` to `all()` (e.g. newest 100 with paging).

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the mechanism. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:40-49 does an unbounded `.get()` of `where('read', isEqualTo: false)` and puts one `batch.update` per returned doc into a single `_db.batch()`, then commits once. There is no chunking, no `limit()`, and no `catch`. Firestore's Commit cap is 500 writes, so 501+ unread rows make the commit fail atomically and leave every row unread.

Nothing elsewhere mitigates it:
- No other surface flips these rows in bulk. The web has the identical unbounded pattern (/home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/notifications/page.tsx:74-76, only with `.catch(() => {})`), so it fails the same way — it is not a fallback.
- No server-side re-check or CF path exists; the only inbox writer is functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts, which only creates rows.
- Rows are never removed: firestore.rules:163-172 sets `allow create, delete: if false` for customers/{uid}/notifications, and no CF or sweep deletes or TTLs them, so the inbox only grows.
- The per-row `markRead` (line 52) still works, so it is not a hard block, but the "Mark all read" tap (notifications_screen.dart:107) and the on-dispose call (notifications_screen.dart:36) would both silently no-op forever, leaving the home bell dot (home_screen.dart:216) and profile pill (profile_screen.dart:327) stuck.

The codebase itself demonstrates the correct convention: functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:50-62 explicitly chunks at 450 per commit ("Per-user inbox writes, batched (≤450/commit)") for exactly this cap. The app repository just never got the same treatment, so the fix is trivial and local (chunk at ~450 and await each commit).

Caveats that lower confidence rather than refute it: it is not a crash (an unawaited Future error surfaces as an uncaught async error, not an app crash), and the trigger threshold is high — since the only inbox writer is admin broadcasts, a user needs 501+ broadcasts received without ever opening the inbox. That makes it a long-tail rather than everyday failure, but it is deterministic once reached and permanently unrecoverable from the client.

findings.title: Content page detail ignores `published`, so unpublished/draft policy pages still render
findings.detail: `watchPage(id)` maps on `d.exists` only and never checks `published` (lines 27-30), while the list query filters `where('published', isEqualTo: true)` (line 17). ContentPageScreen consequently renders any `content/{id}` doc it is handed, and its own "Not available / This page is no longer published" empty state (content_page_screen.dart:80-84) is unreachable — it only fires when the doc is deleted, and admin content pages are created-then-edited, never deleted (admin/src/features/settings/api/content.ts writes `published: false` for drafts, line 134-149). Firestore rules allow any authenticated client to read every `content` doc (firestore.rules:49), so drafts are fetchable. The web deliberately resolves pages only from the published list (`useContentPageBySlug` → `useContentPages`, web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:91-95) and shows "It may have been unpublished".
findings.failure_scenario: Admin unpublishes the Refund Policy while drafting a new version.
