A customer with the page open (live stream) keeps reading the withdrawn text, and anyone navigating to /content/{id} — a route reachable from a stale back-stack entry — renders the unpublished draft as if it were live policy.
findings.fix: Filter in `watchPage`: `.map((d) => d.exists && (d.data()?['published'] == true) ? ContentPage.fromDoc(d) : null)` so the existing "no longer published" empty state does its job.

verdict.reason:
The core code facts check out and no guard exists anywhere else on this path.

- /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/settings/data/content_repository.dart:27-30 — watchPage(id) maps `d.exists ? ContentPage.fromDoc(d) : null` with no published check, while watchPages() (line 17) filters `where('published', isEqualTo: true)`. The class doc comment on line 6 explicitly states "Only `published == true` pages are customer-visible", so the omission contradicts the file's own stated contract.
- /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/settings/data/content_page.dart:71 parses `published`, and grep shows the field is never read anywhere in app/lib — dead on the model.
- /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/settings/content_page_screen.dart:33 re-streams content/{id} by id (the screen takes only pageId, not the already-filtered list item), so the list's published filter does not carry over. Its empty state "This page is no longer published" (lines 80-84) can never fire for an unpublish.
- No server-side re-check: firebase/firestore.rules:49 is `match /content/{docId} { allow read: if hasAppCheck(); }` and hasAppCheck() returns true unconditionally (line 41), so drafts are readable.
- Admin can genuinely unpublish a live page: admin/src/features/settings/routes/ContentPageTab.tsx:338 is a published Toggle saved via saveContentPage (api/content.ts:134-152), merging `published:false` onto the existing doc.
- Cross-surface mismatch is real: web resolves pages only from the published list (web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:91-95, useContentPageBySlug → useContentPages), so unpublishing removes it there but not in the app.

Two parts of the claim are overstated but do not rescue it: (a) the empty state is not fully unreachable — deleteContentPage (admin/src/features/settings/api/content.ts:197-203) does delete non-system pages; (b) the "stale back-stack / direct navigation" angle is weak — /content/:id (app_router.dart:309-314) is only pushed from the published-filtered Settings list (settings_screen.dart:179), and notification deep links have no 'content' case (notifications_screen.dart:167-183). The surviving, genuine scenario is the live one: a customer with a policy page open when an admin unpublishes it keeps reading the withdrawn text indefinitely, because the stream still emits the doc.

Not cosmetic (content-visibility/data correctness, fixed in the repository, not the UI) and not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items. One-line fix: gate on the already-parsed `published` flag in watchPage. Severity is low-to-moderate given the narrow entry point.

findings.title: "Skip for now" on Create profile persists nothing — the user is forced back to it on every sign-in
findings.detail: The Skip button's only action is `router.replace('/')`. It writes nothing, so `customers/{uid}.profileComplete` stays false. Sign-in routing is driven purely by that flag: authActions.ts:88-90 returns `needsProfile: !profileComplete`, and signin/page.tsx:72 does `router.replace(needsProfile ? '/create-profile' : '/')`. The `profileSkipped` field exists in the seeded doc (lib/customerDoc.ts:38), in the shared type (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:116) and in the rules' allowed-update list (firestore.rules:134) — but a grep across web/, app/lib, functions/src and admin/src shows nothing ever writes it to Firestore. The app solves the same problem locally (app/lib/core/services/app_prefs.dart:25, honoured at splash_screen.dart:54); the web has no equivalent.
findings.failure_scenario: New customer verifies their OTP, taps "Skip for now", shops as a guest-named account. They sign out and back in the next day: verifyOtp returns needsProfile=true and they land on /create-profile again. Every subsequent sign-in repeats this, forever, with no way to dismiss it permanently.
findings.fix: Have Skip write `{ profileSkipped: true, updatedAt: serverTimestamp() }` to customers/{uid} (already permitted by the rules) and change the signin route condition to `needsProfile && !customer.profileSkipped`.

verdict.reason:
Verified in code; I could not refute it.

1) The button really is inert: /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(auth)/create-profile/page.tsx:121-127 — `onClick={() => router.replace('/')}` and nothing else. No Firestore write, no local storage, no state change.

2) Nothing else compensates. Routing is driven solely by `profileComplete`: web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:89-99 (`ensureCustomerDoc` returns only `profileComplete`), web/src/components/auth/authActions.ts:88-90 (`needsProfile: !profileComplete`), web/src/app/(auth)/signin/page.tsx:72 (`router.replace(needsProfile ? '/create-profile' : '/')`). No middleware, layout guard, or auth-store hook re-checks or remembers a skip — grep for 'create-profile' across web/src hits only signin/page.tsx:72 plus comments.

3) `profileSkipped` is genuinely write-dead. Defined in packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:116, seeded false in web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:38, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:214 and scripts/seed.ts:422, and explicitly whitelisted for owner updates in firebase/firestore.rules:134 — yet no surface (web/, app/lib, functions/src, admin/src) ever sets it true. The rules whitelist is strong evidence the persistence was intended and never implemented; the Flutter app implements the same product behaviour with device-local prefs (app_prefs.dart:25, honoured at splash_screen.dart:54 `complete || skipped`), so web is the odd one out.

4) Reachability holds, though not by the exact path claimed. A brand-new *web* customer never sees this page: register/page.tsx:84 collects the name up-front and calls `completeProfile` before routing to '/'. The page is reached when someone signs in with profileComplete==false — realistically a user who signed up in the Flutter app and skipped there (the app writes the shared users/{digits} directory at auth_repository.dart:113-116, so that number passes the web signin existence gate), or a user whose register-time `completeProfile` write failed (it only toasts, then still router.replace('/')). Those users get /create-profile on every web sign-in and Skip never stops it.

5) Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not an architecture-rule artifact (a plain owner-field write already permitted by rules — no Cloud Function needed), and not cosmetic: the fix is persisting `profileSkipped: true` and having ensureCustomerDoc/needsProfile honour it.

Caveat (hence medium, not high): impact is a repeated nag at sign-in (one extra tap), not a blocked or broken flow, and the reporter's stated scenario (new web customer) is inaccurate — the real trigger is an app-created or partially-written account.

findings.title: Wallet top-up accepts any amount above ₹0 while the server rejects anything under ₹100
findings.detail: `submitTopUp` validates only `Number.isFinite(rupees) && rupees > 0`; the numeric input is free-form (line 136 strips non-digits but imposes no bounds). The callable enforces `MIN_TOPUP = 100_00` and `MAX_TOPUP = 100_000_00` (functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:20-31) and throws `failed-precondition` with the real message before Razorpay is ever opened. The client's `catch` (line 79-81) discards `e` entirely and toasts the fixed `WALLET_CF_MSG` = "This goes live once the rewards/wallet service is deployed."
findings.failure_scenario: Customer types 50 in the Add money field and presses Add money. topUpWallet throws "Minimum top-up is ₹100." The UI instead tells them the wallet service is not deployed — so they stop trying rather than entering a valid amount. Same for any value over ₹1,00,000.
findings.fix: Mirror the server bounds client-side (reject <₹100 / >₹1,00,000 with the specific message, as the withdraw screen already does for its minimum) and surface the callable's own message in the catch: `const m = (e as {message?:string})?.message; toast.error(m && !m.startsWith('INTERNAL') ? m : WALLET_CF_MSG)`.

verdict.reason: Real defect, confirmed by reading all four relevant files. web/src/app/(shop)/account/wallet/page.tsx:59 validates only `!Number.isFinite(rupees) || rupees <= 0`, and the free-form input at line 136 only strips non-digits (no min/max, no maxLength). functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:20-31 enforces MIN_TOPUP=100_00 / MAX_TOPUP=100_000_00 and throws HttpsError('failed-precondition', 'Minimum top-up is Rs.100.') before the Razorpay order is created, so the checkout modal never opens. The client's catch at line 79 is a bare `catch {` with no error binding, so the server's real message is unreachable and the user always sees WALLET_CF_MSG ('This goes live once the rewards/wallet service is deployed'), i.e. a recoverable input error is reported as a backend outage. No guard exists upstream: callTopUpWallet (web/src/components/wallet/actions.ts:39-47) passes amountPaise straight to the callable. Two sibling surfaces prove this is an omission rather than an intentional pattern: web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:59-62 pre-checks `belowMin` with the comment 'Mirrors the server's minimum so the request isn't rejected round-trip', and app/lib/features/wallet/wallet_screen.dart:344-345,380 enforces `rupees >= 100 && rupees <= 100000` with the comment 'mirrors the topUpWallet server bounds' plus a 'Minimum Rs.100' hint. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not an architecture-rule artifact, and not cosmetic — it is a validation/error-routing logic gap fixable by mirroring the server bounds (and/or surfacing the HttpsError message).

findings.title: Withdrawal errors are swallowed into a misleading "service not deployed" toast
findings.detail: `confirm()`'s catch is `catch { toast.error(WALLET_CF_MSG) }` — the HttpsError is not inspected. `requestWithdrawal` throws four distinct user-facing `failed-precondition` messages (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:36-47): affiliate not active, "You already have a withdrawal in progress.", amount exceeds balance, and below minimum, plus "Choose a valid bank account." The client pre-validates only balance (line 55) and minimum (line 60); `affiliate.hasPendingWithdrawal` is never checked anywhere in web/src, so that branch is unreachable client-side and always surfaces the wrong text.
findings.failure_scenario: Affiliate requests ₹2,000, admin has not yet processed it, so `affiliate.hasPendingWithdrawal` is true. They come back and request ₹1,000. The server correctly refuses with "You already have a withdrawal in progress." but the screen says "This goes live once the rewards/wallet service is deployed." — the customer believes the feature is broken and files a support ticket.
findings.fix: Extract the existing `errMessage(e, fallback)` helper from components/auth/authActions.ts:109 and use it here; additionally disable the Confirm button with an inline note when `affiliate.hasPendingWithdrawal` is true.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, and stronger than claimed. web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:69-71 uses a bare `catch { toast.error(WALLET_CF_MSG) }`, discarding the HttpsError. requestWithdrawal is actually deployed (functions/src/index.ts:32), so "This goes live once the rewards/wallet service is deployed." (actions.ts:29) is wrong for every server rejection. The pending branch is reachable and unguarded on web: `hasPendingWithdrawal` exists in packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:39 but appears nowhere under web/src; it is set true at request (requests.ts:88) and cleared only by admin approve/reject (withdrawals.ts:80,112). Because the confirmed balance is deliberately NOT deducted until approval (documented at requests.ts:8), the page still shows the full withdrawable balance, so the client's overBalance/belowMin/bank/amount>0 pre-checks all pass and the request always reaches the server's "You already have a withdrawal in progress." — the misleading toast is the guaranteed outcome, not an edge case. The Flutter app handles this properly (affiliate_withdraw_screen.dart:154 message, :380 disables submit), and web already has the correct pattern available (errMessage(e, fallback) in checkout/page.tsx:35 and components/auth/authActions.ts:109). Not cosmetic: the fix is error-handling logic (inspect the FunctionsError message / add the pending guard), not a design change. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item. Only nit: the client also validates bank presence and amount>0, which does not change the conclusion.

findings.title: Applied discount is frozen at apply-time, so changing cart quantities makes the displayed total diverge from what is charged
findings.detail: draft.coupon.discountPaise is captured once — from callApplyCoupon (page.tsx:152, bag/page.tsx:53) or from bestOfferForCart (page.tsx:92) — and computeSummary is then fed that fixed number (page.tsx:130-137) no matter how the subtotal changes. Nothing re-runs it: the bag page lets the user change quantities with the coupon banner still shown (bag/page.tsx:90-91), and the checkout auto-apply is guarded by the one-shot `autoTried` ref. The server always recomputes the percentage against the live subtotal (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:171, 191).
findings.failure_scenario: Customer applies EID15 (15%, no cap) on a ₹1000 cart → discountPaise ₹150 stored. They go back to the bag and raise quantities to ₹4000, then check out: summary still shows −₹150 and To pay ₹3850, while placeOrder computes −₹600 and charges ₹3400. The reverse (shrinking the cart below minCartValuePaise) makes placeOrder throw and blocks checkout entirely.
findings.fix: Recompute the coupon whenever subtotalPaise changes — re-run bestOfferForCart/callApplyCoupon for the applied code on subtotal change, or store the coupon rule (type/percent/cap/min) instead of a precomputed paise amount and derive the discount inside computeSummary.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. draft.coupon.discountPaise is written once (web/src/app/(shop)/bag/page.tsx:53; checkout/page.tsx:92,103,152) into the in-memory useCheckoutDraft store (components/checkout/checkout.ts:163) and is never re-derived: no effect anywhere in web/src invalidates or recomputes it on cart change, the checkout auto-apply is doubly guarded (`if (draft.coupon) return` at page.tsx:87 plus the autoTried ref), and the bag page keeps the coupon banner + OrderSummary live while QtyStepper edits quantities (bag/page.tsx:90-91). computeSummary (checkout.ts:101) only clamps via Math.min(discountPaise, subtotalPaise), which rescues flat coupons but lets a stale percent discount through in both directions. The server is independent and authoritative: placeOrder calls computeCouponDiscount(couponCode, subtotalPaise) (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:347-349), recomputing the percentage against the live subtotal (:171, :191) and throwing failed-precondition on an unmet minimum (:143, :187) with no catch/fallback. Shrinking the cart is the harmful direction: 15% frozen at 600 on a 4000 cart, cart reduced to 1000, UI CTA says "Place order · 400" while the server discounts 150 and opens Razorpay for 850 (res.amountPaise, page.tsx:183-192) — charged amount diverges from displayed total; or placeOrder hard-fails and dead-ends checkout. Percent coupons are supported and creatable in admin (features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx:29). Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item; the offers.ts header comment states the intent that client and server discounts MATCH, so this is a bug against stated intent, not an accepted trade-off. The fix is logic (re-derive the discount when subtotal changes), not a cosmetic/UI change.

findings.title: Cart lines cache the price from the moment of "Add to bag" and are never revalidated against the product doc
findings.detail: CartLine stores pricePaise/mrpPaise snapshotted in ProductDetail.handleAdd (web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:131) and subtotalPaise() (cart.ts:134) sums those cached values; the line is persisted verbatim into customers/{uid}.cart (cart.ts:97) and survives indefinitely across devices and sessions. Neither the bag page nor the checkout page ever re-reads products/{id}. The server prices every line from the live product/variant doc (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:61-72, 89), so the subtotal the customer sees is only correct until the admin edits the price or the variant's offer.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer adds a perfume at ₹899 and leaves it in the bag. Admin raises offerPricePaise to ₹1199. Next visit the bag and checkout still show ₹899 and "Place order · ₹899", but placeOrder prices the line at ₹1199 and the order/Razorpay charge is ₹300 higher than the figure on the button, with no warning or confirmation step.
findings.fix: Refresh cart line prices from products/{id} when the bag/checkout mounts (one getDoc per distinct productId, or a small batched read), show a "price updated" notice when a line changes, and block placement until the user acknowledges.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on every leg. CartLine.pricePaise is captured at add-time (web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:131), persisted verbatim into customers/{uid}.cart (web/src/lib/cart.ts:97) and rehydrated by the auth bridge (cart.ts:151-162); subtotalPaise (cart.ts:134) sums the cached value. Neither web/src/app/(shop)/bag/page.tsx nor web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx reads products/{id} — bag imports only useCart and renders line.pricePaise*qty (line 188); checkout's only Firestore reads are addresses/coupons/settings, and it feeds the same cached subtotal into computeSummary (lines 45, 130-138). The server reprices independently from the live doc/variant in priceLines (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:53-93, lineTotalPaise at line 89), and the PlaceOrder zod schema (lines 29-33) accepts only {productId, variantId, qty} — the client never sends an expected total and the server has nothing to compare against, so there is no mismatch guard on either side. Consequence is a money defect, not cosmetic: for COD the order is created at the higher server price with no confirmation; for Razorpay the order is already placed (stock decremented, wallet debited, coupon burned) before createRazorpayOrder charges o.totalPaise-o.walletUsedPaise (line 666), and the checkout page silently adopts res.amountPaise (line 212). No comment anywhere documents snapshotting as intentional, it matches none of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items, and the Flutter app caches identically (app/lib/features/cart/data/cart_line.dart:78) so no other surface compensates. Fix is data logic (revalidate lines on bag/checkout mount, or have placeOrder verify a client-supplied expected subtotal), not UI.

findings.title: Order detail hides the Return CTA for the whole order as soon as any single item has an active return
findings.detail: `const rb = returnBadge(items)` (line 68) uses `items.find(...)` over ALL items (web/src/components/account/orders.ts:232), returning the first item with an active return status. The render then does `order.status === 'delivered' && (rb ? <status badge> : rw?.open ? <Return item link> : ...)` — the per-order badge unconditionally replaces the per-item Return action. The return page itself is per-item and would still accept the remaining items.
findings.failure_scenario: Delivered order with 2 items. Customer returns item A; the CF stamps only item A with `returnStatus: 'requested'`. Reopening the order detail, `returnBadge` finds item A and renders "Return request in progress", and the "Return item" link disappears. Item B — still `returnStatus: 'none'` and inside the window — has no entry point from the order detail page, even though it is fully returnable.
findings.fix: Render the badge and the Return CTA independently: show the badge when `returnBadge(items)` is non-null AND still show the "Return item" link when `hasReturnableItem(items) && rw?.open` (that helper is already exported and currently unused).

verdict.reason:
The claim holds up, and the surrounding code shows the rest of the stack is explicitly built for the partial case — only the order-detail gate isn't.

1. /home/h/barkath/web/src/components/account/orders.ts:231-238 — `returnBadge(items)` does `items.find(x => ACTIVE_RETURN.includes(x.returnStatus))`, i.e. it is order-level and fires as soon as ANY one item is requested/under_review/approved/completed.
2. /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:233-258 — `order.status === 'delivered' && (rb ? <badge> : rw?.open ? <Link .../return> : <closed pill>)`. The badge branch is first, so the "Return item" link is unconditionally replaced once one item is stamped. There is no `hasReturnableItem` in the condition.
3. The return page is per-item and would still accept the remaining items: /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:79-82 filters `eligible = items.filter(returnStatus === 'none' || 'rejected')`, line 125 shows an item picker when `eligible.length > 1`, and line 117 only shows "Every item in this order already has a return in progress" when `eligible.length === 0`. That empty-state branch is currently dead from any in-app navigation, because the detail page hides the link before it can be reached.
4. The intended helper already exists and is dead code: `hasReturnableItem` (orders.ts:241-243) is exported but has zero call sites anywhere in the repo (grep over web/admin/functions/app). The CF even references it by name — functions/src/returns/requests.ts:62 "A rejected item is eligible again (mirrors the web hasReturnableItem)" — and the server-side guard at requests.ts:64 rejects only per-item (`it.returnStatus`), not per-order, so the backend happily accepts item B.
5. No alternative entry point: /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/page.tsx has no return CTA at all, so the detail page is the only navigational route to /return. Only a hand-typed URL reaches item B.

Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not an architecture-rule artefact, and not cosmetic — a fully returnable line item becomes unreachable from the UI, which is a lost user flow rather than a styling issue. The fix is a condition change (fall through to the link when `hasReturnableItem(items)` is true, alongside the status badge), not a redesign.

findings.title: Return submission discards the Cloud Function's error message, so every failure reads as a transient glitch
findings.detail: `requestReturn` is `try { await httpsCallable(...)(payload); return true } catch { return false }` — the HttpsError code and message are dropped on the floor. The caller (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:109) maps `false` to "We couldn't submit your return just now. Please try again." The CF raises four distinct, permanent, non-retryable conditions: `permission-denied: Not your order`, `failed-precondition: Only delivered orders can be returned`, `failed-precondition: The 3-day return window ... has closed`, and `failed-precondition: A return is already in progress for this item`. Note `cancelOrder` in the same file (line 219-226) does propagate `e.message`, so the pattern already exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer submits a return for an item that already has a pending request (reachable via the OrderCard "Return" link plus a stale `?itemId=` deep link). The server returns `failed-precondition: A return is already in progress for this item.`; the UI says "Please try again", so the customer taps Submit repeatedly and each attempt fails identically with no explanation.
findings.fix: Return `{ ok: boolean; message?: string }` from `requestReturn` (mirroring `cancelOrder`) and surface `message` in the toast, falling back to the generic copy only when no message is present.

verdict.reason:
Verified in code and could not refute it.

1. /home/h/barkath/web/src/components/account/orders.ts:313 is exactly as claimed — `try { await httpsCallable(functions,'requestReturnOrReplacement')(payload); return true } catch { return false }`. The HttpsError code/message are discarded. It has exactly one caller, /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/return/page.tsx:103-110, which maps `false` to the single toast "We couldn't submit your return just now. Please try again." There is no other surface (no global callable-error interceptor, no server-side re-check that informs the user) that recovers the reason.

2. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/returns/requests.ts does throw four distinct permanent conditions: `permission-denied: Not your order.`, `failed-precondition: Only delivered orders can be returned.`, `failed-precondition: The 3-day return window for this order has closed.`, `failed-precondition: A return is already in progress for this item.` — plus `not-found` and two `invalid-argument` cases. All read as a transient glitch on the client.

3. The reachability is stronger than the reporter's stale-deep-link scenario. The client-side gate `returnWindow(order, returnSettings?.windowDays)` uses the admin-configured window, which is seeded to 7 days (scripts/seed.ts:208, scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:117, admin StorefrontTab default '7'), while the CF hard-codes `RETURN_WINDOW_MS = 3 days`. So for any order delivered 4-7 days ago the return form renders as open, the customer fills it in, the CF rejects with "The 3-day return window ... has closed", and the UI tells them to try again — an unrecoverable retry loop on a routine path. The reporter's `?itemId=` path is also real: `preItemId` bypasses the `eligible` filter (selectedItem falls back to `items.find(...)`, and `showPicker` is false whenever preItemId is set), so an ineligible item can be submitted.

4. Not covered by the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and not an architecture-rule intentional. The fix is functional error propagation, not styling, and the codebase already establishes the exact pattern one function above: `cancelOrder` (orders.ts:219-226) returns `{ ok, message }` and its caller renders `res.message || 'Could not cancel this order.'` (orders/[id]/page.tsx:82). Minor corroboration: the doc comment on line 312 claims the caller shows CF_UNAVAILABLE_MSG, which it does not — the error path was never thought through.

findings.title: Cancelling an order never releases the coupon it consumed — the spin coupon stays 'used' and the promotional redemption counters are never decremented
findings.detail: `placeOrder` consumes the coupon at checkout.ts:566-614: a personal coupon is flipped to `status:'used'` with `usedOnOrderId`, and a promotional coupon gets `usesCount` incremented plus `customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{couponId}.count` incremented (the exact counters `computeCouponDiscount` reads at lines 149 and 153 to enforce `maxUsesTotal` / `maxUsesPerUser`). `performCancellation` restores stock, refunds the wallet, and reverses the affiliate commission — but contains no reference to `coupons`, `couponUsage`, or `appliedCoupon` at all. The order's `appliedCoupon` field (checkout.ts:510) carries `couponId` / `userCouponId`, so the information needed to reverse it is right there on the document being updated at line 146.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer wins a 20%-off spin coupon, applies it to a ₹3,000 order, then cancels two minutes later (status is still 'accepted', so `cancelOrder` allows it). Stock is restored and the wallet is refunded, but `customers/{uid}/coupons/{id}.status` stays 'used' — the app's Coupons screen and web rewards page show it under Used and it can never be applied again. The customer has lost the prize with nothing to show for it. For a promotional coupon with `maxUsesPerUser: 1`, the cancelled order still burns the customer's single allowance: `computeCouponDiscount` line 153 will throw 'You have already used this coupon' on their next attempt.
findings.fix: In `performCancellation`, read `o.appliedCoupon` from the order snapshot (already loaded at line 46) and, in the write phase, restore `customers/{customerId}/coupons/{userCouponId}` to `status:'active'` with `usedAt/usedOnOrderId` cleared, and decrement `coupons/{couponId}.usesCount` and `customers/{customerId}/couponUsage/{couponId}.count` by 1.

verdict.reason:
Verified end to end and could not refute it.

Consumption (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts): line 510 stamps `appliedCoupon: { code, couponId, userCouponId, discountPaise, source }` on the order doc; lines 567-573 flip the personal coupon `customers/{uid}/coupons/{userCouponId}` to `status:'used', usedAt, usedOnOrderId, usesCount +1`; lines 604-614 increment `coupons/{couponId}.usesCount` and `customers/{uid}/couponUsage/{couponId}.count`. Those are exactly the values the guards read: `computeCouponDiscount` rejects on `usesCount >= maxUsesTotal` (149-151), on `userCouponUses(uid, doc.id) >= maxUsesPerUser` -> 'You have already used this coupon.' (152-155), and on `c.status !== 'active'` for personal coupons -> 'This coupon has already been used or expired.' (186).

Reversal: I read all of /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/cancel.ts (165 lines). `performCancellation` restores variant/product stock, credits the wallet with a ledger row, cancels pending commissions and decrements `affiliate.pendingBalancePaise`, then updates the order at line 146 — and contains zero references to `coupons`, `couponUsage`, `appliedCoupon` or `userCouponId`. A repo-wide grep for `couponUsage|usedOnOrderId|usesCount` hits only spin/execute.ts, checkout.ts, shared types, the admin coupons UI, seed.ts and e2e specs — no reversal surface anywhere.

Ruled out the usual escapes: no Firestore trigger exists (`grep -rln "onDocumentUpdated|onDocumentWritten" functions/src` returns nothing); the admin cancel path funnels through the same `performCancellation` per the file header, so both paths leak; the path is reachable since `cancelOrder` allows CANCELLABLE = ['accepted','packing','packed'] (checkout.ts:627) and a new order is 'accepted' (checkout.ts:491); it is not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items and no comment frames the non-release as deliberate anti-abuse; it is not cosmetic since the defect is server-side state, with the 'Used' tab only the symptom; and the wallet refund does not compensate because only `amountPaidPaise` is returned, so the coupon's discount value is destroyed.

The data needed to fix it is on the document already being written at cancel.ts:146 (`o.appliedCoupon.couponId` / `.userCouponId`), though the extra reads would have to be hoisted above the writes like the existing ones. Real, fixable, and consistent with the file's stated intent of reversing everything the order consumed.

findings.title: Approving a return refunds the customer but never reverses the affiliate commission that was already confirmed at delivery
findings.detail: `affiliate/commissions.ts:10-14` states the design explicitly: 'Commission clears at delivery rather than after commissionClearanceDays ... Returns are handled by the return flow, which is the case the clearance delay was protecting against.' But `adminApproveOrderRequest` contains no reference to `commissions` or to `affiliate.*` anywhere — it updates the request, the customer wallet, and the order (`refundedPaise`, `paymentStatus`, `items[].returnStatus`) and stops. Since returns are only possible on delivered orders (`returns/requests.ts:39`), and delivery is exactly the moment `confirmCommissionsForOrder` moves the commission from `pendingBalancePaise` into `confirmedBalancePaise` (the withdrawable balance, commissions.ts:129-133), every approved return leaves the affiliate holding withdrawable commission on merchandise that has been refunded. The `commissions` doc's `cancellationReason` field (commissions.ts:88) is written as null at accrual and never set by any code path other than cancel.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer C (referred by affiliate A, 5% rate) orders a ₹20,000 item. On delivery, A's ₹1,000 commission moves to `affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise`. Within the 3-day window C requests a return; the admin approves it and ₹20,000 is credited back to C's wallet. A's ₹1,000 remains withdrawable, A submits `requestWithdrawal` and the admin pays it out. The business has refunded the full order value and additionally paid ₹1,000 of commission on a sale that no longer exists.
findings.fix: In the approve transaction, read the `commissions` docs for `r.orderId` before the writes (query outside the transaction as `cancel.ts:37-40` does) and debit the affiliate's `confirmedBalancePaise` / `lifetimeEarningsPaise` by the pro-rata share of the returned line (refund amount ÷ eligible merchandise value × commissionPaise), stamping the commission row with a `returned`/partial status and a `cancellationReason`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. adminApproveOrderRequest (functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:14-132) writes only orderRequests, the customer wallet + walletTransactions, the order doc and the legacy item doc — no reference to `commissions` or `affiliate.*`. Returns require status 'delivered' (returns/requests.ts:39), and delivery is precisely when orders/status.ts:97-100 calls confirmCommissionsForOrder, moving the commission into affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise/lifetimeEarningsPaise (commissions.ts:128-133). The only reversal path, performCancellation (orders/cancel.ts:71-75), explicitly filters to status==='pending' commissions and is unreachable after delivery, so it cannot cover returns. No compensating surface exists: firebase/firestore.rules:86-89 makes `commissions` CF-only-write (allow write: if false); grep across admin/src, web/src, app/lib, packages shows only read queries; affiliate/requests.ts:39-40 gates withdrawals purely on confirmedBalancePaise and approveWithdrawal (withdrawals.ts:78-82) simply decrements it without re-deriving from non-returned orders; scheduled/sweeps.ts does not touch commissions. The commissions.ts:11-14 header asserts "Returns are handled by the return flow" — that handling is simply not implemented, so cancellationReason/status:'cancelled' is never set on a return. Money-moving, server-side, fixable, and not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list. Only imprecision: returns are per-line-item while the commission row is per-order, so a correct fix must prorate rather than reverse the whole row.

findings.title: applyCoupon drops the free_shipping flag, so a free-shipping coupon shows ₹0 saved and the checkout screen keeps charging delivery
findings.detail: `computeCouponDiscount` returns a `waiveDelivery` flag for `discountType === 'free_shipping'` on both the promotional path (line 176) and the personal path (line 202), and `placeOrder` threads it into `summarise` at line 419 so the server genuinely zeroes `deliveryPaise` (line 286). But `applyCoupon` destructures only `{ discountPaise, label }` at line 314 and returns only those two fields at line 315. Both clients store exactly what comes back and nothing else — `web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:152` does `draft.set({ coupon: { code, discountPaise: res.discountPaise, label: res.label } })`, and `app/lib/features/checkout/coupon_screen.dart:46-52` does the same — so neither client's local summary can waive delivery. free_shipping is a first-class type in both writers: `admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx:30` offers it in the discount-type picker, and `spin/execute.ts:99,126` issues personal coupons with `discountType: 'free_shipping'`.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer wins a 'Free delivery' spin coupon (SPIN-XXXXX, discountType 'free_shipping'). At checkout they enter the code; applyCoupon succeeds and the toast says 'Coupon SPIN-XXXXX applied', but discountPaise is 0, so the order summary still shows 'You saved ₹0' and Delivery ₹49, total ₹1,049. They press Place order; the server applies waiveDelivery and creates the order for ₹1,000 — and for razorpay, `createRazorpayOrder` opens the gateway for ₹1,000, not the ₹1,049 the screen displayed. The coupon looks broken and the displayed total never matches the charged total.
findings.fix: Return `waiveDelivery` (and ideally the whole `CouponResult`) from `applyCoupon` at line 315, and have the web `computeSummary` / app `CheckoutDraft` honour it when deriving `deliveryPaise`, mirroring `summarise` at checkout.ts:286.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:314-315 — applyCoupon destructures and returns only {discountPaise, label}, dropping the waiveDelivery flag that computeCouponDiscount sets for discountType 'free_shipping' (line 164-166/176 promo, line 202 personal) and that placeOrder does honour (line 347 -> summarise line 418 -> deliveryPaise zeroed at line 286). No client-side fallback exists: web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:68-72 defines AppliedCoupon as {code, discountPaise, label} and computeSummary (line 89, freeDelivery derived only from subtotal/threshold) has no waive concept; app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:66-71 and computeSummary at 187-200 are identical, and its applyCoupon (246-254) reads only discountPaise/label. The non-CF offers path is equally blind — web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:44-45,59-60 and app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:56-68 compute a discount only for 'flat'/'percent', so a free_shipping offer is listed with the headline 'Free delivery' but discountPaise 0, and applyOffer stores that 0. Reachable in production: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:126 issues personal coupons with discountType 'free_shipping', admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx:30 exposes the type, and scripts/seed.ts:704 seeds FREESHIP. Not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item and not an architecture-rule exemption (this is a CF-owned money path). The consequence is functional rather than cosmetic: the client charges standardFeePaise while the server creates the order with deliveryPaise 0, so the checkout total never matches placeOrder's amountPaise or the Razorpay amount computed in createRazorpayOrder (line 666). Fix is logic-level — return waiveDelivery from applyCoupon and thread it through both computeSummary implementations. Only caveat: the mismatch under-charges rather than over-charges, and the 'You saved Rs.0' label alone would be cosmetic.

findings.title: reviews update rule is gated on isAdmin() only — any sub-admin can publish or reject reviews
findings.detail: `allow update: if hasAppCheck() && isAdmin() && ...hasOnly(['status','moderatedBy','moderatedAt','updatedAt','helpfulCount'])`. Unlike every other admin-written collection in this file (settings/categories/products/coupons/… all use `canWrite('<module>')`, and the comment at lines 15-19 states this was deliberately tightened because 'a sub-admin with only dashboard.view could rewrite the GST rate'), the reviews rule never consults `can('reviews', …)`. `isAdmin()` is true for ANY doc-holder whose claim is `sub_admin`, regardless of modulePermissions, and it does not even check `adminDoc().status == 'active'` — so a suspended sub-admin still passes.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose matrix has only `dashboard: view` (or one who has been suspended via suspendSubAdmin but whose custom claim has not been revoked) calls updateDoc on reviews/{id} with `{status:'approved', helpfulCount: 9999}` — the rule accepts it and a 1-star or abusive review is published on the storefront (web ProductDetail.tsx:387 and app reviews_repository.dart:19-21 both read `status == 'approved'` publicly).
findings.fix: Change to `allow update: if hasAppCheck() && can('reviews','edit') || can('reviews','approve')` (mirroring the `canWrite()` pattern used for the other direct-write collections), which also picks up the `adminDoc().status == 'active'` check.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. firebase/firestore.rules:113-115 gates the reviews update on isAdmin() (line 12: claim role == 'super_admin' || 'sub_admin') instead of canWrite('reviews'), so it consults neither modulePermissions nor adminDoc().status — unlike settings/categories/products/coupons/etc. (lines 48-59) which all use canWrite(), per the deliberate tightening documented at lines 15-19. 'reviews' is a genuine module key (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:258, admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:41), so canWrite('reviews') is the intended gate and was simply missed. There is no server-side re-check: moderation is a direct client transaction in admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:32-66 (no Cloud Function), so the rule is the only boundary, and approved reviews are publicly readable (rules:99, web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:387). Mitigations I checked do not close it: the UI transaction also writes products/{id} for the rating aggregate (which canWrite('products') would block for a dashboard-only sub-admin), but a raw updateDoc on reviews/{id} alone bypasses that entirely; and suspendSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts) revokes tokens/disables the user, shrinking but not removing the suspended-admin window that can()'s status=='active' check would cover. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, not UI/cosmetic, and the fix is a one-line swap to canWrite('reviews') that leaves the legitimate flow (super-admin, or sub-admin with reviews permissions) working. Minor overstatements in the claim: stockAdjustments (rules:213-217) is also isAdmin()-only, so reviews is not literally the only exception, and the helpfulCount field is not written by any customer surface, so the real escalation is the status field.

findings.title: stockAdjustments audit ledger accepts writes from any admin with no inventory permission check
findings.detail: `allow create: if isAdmin() && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid();` — the only constraint is that the forger stamps their own uid. There is no `can('inventory', …)` gate and no `adminDoc().status == 'active'` check, even though `inventory` is a real MODULE_KEY (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:257) and the collection is described in the rule's own comment as the append-only stock-adjustment ledger. The ledger is the audit trail read back by admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:150 `getStockHistory()`, and it is written client-side by addLedger (inventory.ts:129-144) with fully client-supplied `before`/`delta`/`after`/`reason`/`adminName`.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin with only `dashboard: view` (or a suspended one whose claim is still live) writes `stockAdjustments/{newId}` with `{productId:'p1', before: 500, delta: -480, after: 20, reason:'Damaged', adminUid: <self>, adminName:'Someone Else'}`. The Stock History panel for p1 now shows a fabricated 480-unit write-off that no real stock movement backs, and because `update, delete: if false` it can never be removed.
findings.fix: Gate the create on the inventory module: `allow create: if can('inventory','create') && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid();` — matching how the paired stock mutation is already gated server-side via requireModule.

verdict.reason:
Verified at /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:213-217: `match /stockAdjustments/{id} { allow read: if isAdmin(); allow create: if isAdmin() && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid(); allow update, delete: if false; }`. isAdmin() (line 12) inspects only the `role` claim — no module permission, no status. Every other admin-direct-write collection in the same file is gated with canWrite(<module>) (lines 48-59), and the helper's own comment (lines 15-19) states the intent explicitly ("Previously every one of these accepted any admin, so a sub-admin with only dashboard.view could rewrite the GST rate"). stockAdjustments is that same pattern and was missed; can() is also the only place `adminDoc().status == 'active'` is enforced in rules, so a suspended admin with a live claim passes too (functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:21 blocks suspended only on the CF path).

Refutation attempts, none of which hold:
- Written by another surface? grep over the whole repo finds only admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:129 (addLedger) and :150 (getStockHistory). So tightening the rule to can('inventory','edit') breaks nothing: the only legitimate writer runs right after the adminAdjustStock callable, which already does requireModule(req,'inventory','edit') (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26), so that caller provably holds the permission.
- Server-side re-check? None. The stock mutation is CF-protected, but the ledger doc is a raw client batch.set with client-supplied before/delta/after/reason/adminName, never reconciled against the callable's returned results, and `update, delete: if false` makes forged rows permanent.
- Intentional per architecture? The comment at inventory.ts:64 ("stays a client write: it is history for this screen, not the source of truth for stock") justifies it being a direct write, not a permission-free one — the architecture rule says direct writes must be gated by security rules, as every peer collection is.
- Not a KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item, not UI/cosmetic.

Severity is moderate rather than critical (auditLogs via writeAudit remains the CF-only tamper-proof trail; impact is admin-visible history poisoning, not stock or money movement), but it is a real one-line-fixable defect: create should be `can('inventory','edit') && request.resource.data.adminUid == uid()`.

findings.title: Changing a category tint fans out writes to products, which a categories-only sub-admin is denied
findings.detail: `fanOutCategoryTint` (called from CategoryFormPage.tsx:141 whenever an existing category's tint changes) reads every product in the category and commits `batch.update(d.ref, { categoryTint: tint })` against the `products` collection. firebase/firestore.rules:51 gates products writes on `canWrite('products')`, but this action lives entirely inside the Categories module. Additionally the batching loop commits in chunks of 400 sequentially, so a partial failure leaves some products with the new tint and the rest with the old one.
findings.failure_scenario: Sub-admin granted `categories: edit` but not `products: edit` opens a category, changes its tint and saves. `saveCategory` succeeds (categories rule passes) but the first `batch.commit()` is rejected with permission-denied, so the category doc says one tint while every product card still renders the old `categoryTint`, and the surfaced error makes it look like the whole save failed.
findings.fix: Move the fan-out into a Cloud Function guarded by `requireModule(req,'categories','edit')` (it is a cross-document denormalisation, which is exactly the CF criterion), or have readers derive `categoryTint` from the category doc instead of denormalising it onto every product.

verdict.reason: Tried to refute and could not. Verified chain: (1) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:113-122 does a purely client-side `getDocs(products where categoryId==X)` + `batch.update(d.ref, { categoryTint: tint })` on the products collection; its comment ("admin is a trusted, rules-gated writer, so no Cloud Function is needed") predates the granular rules. (2) CategoryFormPage.tsx:141 calls it AFTER `saveCategory` already committed, inside a try/catch whose only handler is `toast.error('Could not save the category.')` and no navigate — so on denial the category IS saved but the operator is told it failed. (3) grep for "products" in /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules returns exactly one line (51): `allow write: if canWrite('products')` — no field-scoped exemption for categoryTint, no categories alternative. (4) `products` and `categories` are independent MODULE_KEYS (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:253-272) and SubAdminFormPage.tsx:210 toggles them independently with only "enable at least one module" as a constraint; admin has no route-level module guard (only sidebar filtering), so the page is reachable by a categories-only sub-admin. (5) No server-side compensation: functions/src/index.ts:9-15 explicitly documents that the `onCategoryTintChanged` trigger was intentionally removed in favour of this client batch. (6) No read-side fallback: web/app read `product.categoryTint` and fall back to a hardcoded hex (ProductCard.tsx, FlashSaleCard.tsx, ProductDetail.tsx), never to the category doc; the only self-heal is re-saving each product (ProductFormPage.tsx:214), which needs products rights anyway. The fix is a rules/CF change (scope products update to `canWrite('categories') && onlyFields(['categoryTint'])`, or move the fan-out into a callable with `requireModule('categories','edit')`) — not a UI change, so the cosmetic exclusion does not apply. Caveats weakening parts of the claim: the "partial failure leaves some products updated" sub-claim is wrong for the permission case (the first batch is rejected, so nothing is written; it only applies to >400-product categories with a mid-loop transient error), and the same cross-module pattern exists at admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:35 (reviews module directly updates the product rating aggregate), so the root cause is arguably a rules-model gap of which this file is one instance.

findings.title: Three of five walletTransactions writers omit `title`, which the web wallet history renders directly
findings.detail: The web wallet history passes `title={tx.title}` with no fallback. `title` is required by the shared `WalletTransaction` type and is written by functions/src/wallet/adjust.ts:66 and by the order-payment/spin-reward rows in checkout.ts:582,596 — but NOT by functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:98 (top-up), functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:116 (cancellation refund) or functions/src/spin/execute.ts:143 (spin cashback), all of which write only `description`. The Flutter app tolerates this via `WalletTransaction.displayTitle`'s source-derived fallback (app/lib/features/wallet/data/wallet.dart:71) and admin does `t.title || cap(t.source)` (CustomerProfilePage.tsx:370); only the web renders the raw empty string. The spin cashback row additionally stores `balanceAfterPaise: 0` regardless of the real balance.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer tops up ₹500 on web, then cancels an order and gets a wallet refund. Their web Transaction history shows two rows with a blank bold title line and only a date subtitle, while the same two rows read 'Added to wallet' and 'Refund · #BRK-48231' in the Flutter app.
findings.fix: Add a `title` to the topup, cancellation-refund and spin-cashback writes (mirroring adjust.ts), and compute `balanceAfterPaise` in execute.ts from the read balance plus the cashback; optionally add the app's source-derived fallback on the web too.

verdict.reason:
Every element of the claim checks out, and I could not find any mitigating path.

1. `title: string` is a REQUIRED (non-optional) field on the shared contract — /home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:162 — so omitting it is a data-contract violation, not a styling choice.

2. Three of five runtime writers omit it entirely (I read the full `tx.set(...)` object literals, no spread, no helper that injects it):
   - /home/h/barkath/functions/src/wallet/topup.ts:97-101 — writes `description: 'Wallet top-up'`, no `title`, and no `orderShortId`.
   - /home/h/barkath/functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:115-126 — `description: \`Refund for cancelled order …\``, no `title`, and no `orderShortId` either (so the web subtitle degrades to just the date).
   - /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:142-147 — `description: 'Spin & Win cashback'`, no `title`.
   The other writers DO set it: functions/src/wallet/adjust.ts:66, functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:582 and :596, and functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:92.

3. Nothing backfills it. There is no Firestore trigger on `walletTransactions` (grep for onDocument/onWrite over functions/src returns nothing), and the web read path does a raw cast with no defaulting: /home/h/barkath/web/src/lib/useCollection.ts does `snap.docs.map((d) => d.data() as T)`. The page then passes `title={tx.title}` unguarded (web/src/app/(shop)/account/wallet/page.tsx:188) into TxRow, which renders `{title}` directly — `undefined` renders as nothing, leaving an empty bold line above the date. scripts/seed.ts:536 DOES write a title, which is why seeded demo data hides the bug — only real top-ups/cancellations/spins expose it.

4. The cross-surface asymmetry is real: app/lib/features/wallet/data/wallet.dart `displayTitle` has an explicit source-derived fallback ("Added to wallet", "Refund · …") and admin does `t.title || cap(t.source)`; only web has none.

Not cosmetic: the fix belongs in the three Cloud Functions (write the missing required field), not in UI. And the secondary finding is purely a data-integrity bug with no UI component at all — functions/src/spin/execute.ts:114 increments `wallet.balancePaise` by the cashback, yet line 144 hardcodes `balanceAfterPaise: 0` in the immutable ledger row, so the ledger's running-balance column is corrupt for every spin cashback (checkout.ts:596 computes the real balance for the equivalent row). Also not covered by any KNOWN+INTENTIONAL item.

findings.title: Review moderation writes the products doc, so a sub-admin with only the reviews module gets permission-denied and nothing is moderated
findings.detail: `moderateReview()` runs one transaction that updates `reviews/{id}` and then `tx.update(pRef, { ratingCount, rating })` on `products/{productId}`. firestore.rules gates the two collections on different modules: `match /reviews/{id}` update needs `isAdmin()` (line 113) but `match /products/{id}` write needs `canWrite('products')` (line 51), and 'reviews' and 'products' are distinct keys in ModulePermissions (packages/shared/src/enums.ts). Because a Firestore transaction is all-or-nothing, the denied product write aborts the review status update too — so the approve/reject buttons silently do nothing for any sub-admin who has reviews permission but not products.
findings.failure_scenario: Super-admin creates a sub-admin with modulePermissions.reviews.approve = true and products = all false. That sub-admin opens /reviews and clicks Approve on a pending review: the transaction fails with PERMISSION_DENIED on products/{id}, the review stays 'pending' forever, and the customer's review never appears on the product page.
findings.fix: Move review moderation behind a Cloud Function guarded by `requireModule(req,'reviews','approve')` that updates both docs with the Admin SDK (matching how returns/orders are handled), or make the product-aggregate write conditional and repair the aggregate server-side.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. moderateReview() (admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:37-65) writes reviews/{id} and products/{productId} in a single Firestore transaction. firestore.rules:113 gates the review update on isAdmin() while the only products rule (firestore.rules:51) gates writes on canWrite('products'); 'products' and 'reviews' are separate, independently-toggleable keys in MODULE_KEYS (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:253-273) and the sub-admin permission matrix is generated directly from MODULE_KEYS with no coupling (admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:60-72). The /reviews route and nav entry are gated on the 'reviews' module only (navConfig.tsx:53, router.tsx:79), so a reviews-only sub-admin can reach the page; the transaction then fails atomically on the products write and the review never leaves 'pending', so it never appears on the product page (web reads require status=='approved'). No server-side fallback exists: no Cloud Function touches reviews or ratingCount (grep of functions/src is empty), unlike inventory which correctly routes its product mutation through the adjustStock callable and only client-writes the stockAdjustments ledger. Not one of the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL items and not cosmetic. Minor corrections to the report: it is not silent (ReviewsListPage.tsx:52-70 toasts "Could not approve the review."), and pending->rejected still works since that transition never touches the product doc; the break is on approve (and on un-approving an approved review).

findings.title: products.soldCount is never incremented on order placement, so popularity sort and the dashboard category chart are permanently zero
findings.detail: The storefront's popularity sort ranks by `b.soldCount - a.soldCount`, the admin dashboard's category-share chart sums `p.soldCount` (admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:173), and firestore.indexes.json declares two composite indexes ordered by `soldCount DESC`. The field is initialised to 0 by admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:156,201,287 and set to non-zero only by scripts/seed.ts:380. `placeOrder` decrements `stock` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:437,440) but never touches `soldCount`, and no other function or trigger writes it.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin adds 30 products through the panel and the store sells hundreds of units. On the storefront, 'Sort: Popularity' returns products in arbitrary (all-zero, stable-sort) order forever, and the admin dashboard's 'top categories' bars all render at 0% — while seeded demo products still show plausible values, hiding the bug.
findings.fix: Increment `soldCount` by the line quantity for each product inside the placeOrder transaction (and decrement it in performCancellation / on an approved return), alongside the existing stock decrement.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. A repo-wide grep for soldCount (all file types, excluding node_modules) finds only readers and zero-initialisers: web/src/components/catalog/ListingView.tsx:100 (sort), admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:173 (category chart), admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:156/201/287 and scripts/add-back-to-school.ts:129 (all set 0), packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:103 (type), firebase/firestore.indexes.json:7,13 (two composite indexes ordered soldCount DESC), and scripts/seed.ts:380 (the only non-zero value). There are no occurrences at all under functions/ or app/. The placeOrder transaction in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:437,440 already writes the very same product doc on every sale (tx.update(snap.ref, { stock: FieldValue.increment(-l.qty), updatedAt })) but omits any soldCount increment; the only other product mutation in functions, the admin inventory adjuster at functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:86, builds its update map from stock/variants only. No order-status trigger or scheduled job writes it. The code path is definitely reachable and not cosmetic: 'popularity' is both an exposed sort option (ListingView.tsx:15) and the default state (useState<SortKey>('popularity'), line 65), so every listing page defaults to an all-zero comparator; categoryPerformance is consumed live at admin/src/features/dashboard/routes/DashboardPage.tsx:46 and normalises with Math.max(1, ...totals) so all bars render 0%. It is not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list, and it is not an architecture-rule exemption — a cross-document sales counter is exactly the counter case the rules assign to Cloud Functions, and the owning transaction already exists. Fix is server-side (add soldCount: FieldValue.increment(l.qty) to the existing checkout tx.update), not a UI change. Only mitigating factor: seeded demo data has plausible non-zero values, which masks the bug in dev — which is the reporter's own point.

findings.title: walletEnabled is accepted by adminAllocateAffiliate and never persisted — the allocate screen's toggle is a no-op
findings.detail: The schema at line 20 accepts `walletEnabled: z.boolean().optional()` but line 23 destructures only `{ uid, commissionRate }`, and the `ref.update` at lines 32-42 writes no wallet-access flag anywhere on the customer doc. admin/src/features/affiliate/routes/AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:115 renders an 'Enable affiliate wallet access' Toggle bound to that value and line 55 sends it; the confirm dialog at line 130 even promises '…and affiliate wallet access'.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin turns the 'Enable affiliate wallet access' toggle OFF and allocates. The confirmation text says wallet access is withheld, but the customer doc gets the standard affiliate map with pending/confirmed/withdrawn balances and the customer's affiliate wallet works exactly as if the toggle were ON. Nothing in the system can ever read the flag back.
findings.fix: Either persist it (`affiliate.walletEnabled: walletEnabled ?? true`) and honour it in the withdrawal/commission paths, or drop the field from the schema and remove the toggle from the allocate screen.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end. functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:20 declares walletEnabled in the zod schema, line 23 destructures only {uid, commissionRate}, and the ref.update at lines 32-42 writes affiliate/role/updatedAt with no wallet-access flag in either the new-affiliate or merge branch. Nothing anywhere reads such a flag: AffiliateInfo (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:27-40) has no wallet field; a repo-wide grep for walletEnabled finds only the unrelated global paymentGateway setting (settings.ts:49, PaymentGatewayTab, web checkout/page.tsx:117, app checkout_repository.dart:181, seed/bootstrap) plus the admin allocate page itself; the app's affiliate wallet/withdraw path gates solely on affiliate.enabled (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_models.dart:44) and firestore.rules has no affiliate wallet gate; adminRevokeAffiliate only flips enabled:false. Because zod objects are non-strict, the field did not need to be declared to be accepted — its presence in the schema is evidence of dropped intent, not deliberate ignoring. Not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and the route is reachable. It is not merely cosmetic: the value is sent to a CF that validates then discards it, and the confirm dialog (AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:130) tells the admin wallet access is withheld when it is not; the fix is server-side persistence plus enforcement, no UI change required. Mitigating only in that the toggle defaults to true, so the off-path is the silently broken one.

findings.title: UPI / Card selection on the Payment screen is a no-op — the choice is never passed to the Razorpay checkout
findings.detail: `_method` is initialised to `'upi'` (line 45) and mutated by both `_methodCard` handlers via `setState(() => _method = value)` (line 417), which only repaints the selection ring. `_openCheckout` builds the Razorpay options map at lines 127-137 with `key`, `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, `name`, `description`, `prefill`, `theme`, `retry` — `_method` is never read, and no `method` map or `prefill['method']` is supplied. The field is not sent to `placeOrder` either (lines 81-88). It is therefore a two-option control that changes nothing about the payment flow.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer taps the 'Card · Visa · Mastercard · Amex' row (the ring moves to Card), then taps 'Pay ₹1,299'. The native Razorpay sheet opens on its own default landing tab with every method enabled — UPI included — exactly as it would have had they left 'UPI' selected. The user's explicit choice has no effect on what they are shown.
findings.fix: Pass the selection through to Razorpay: add `'method': {'upi': _method == 'upi', 'card': _method == 'card', 'netbanking': false, 'wallet': false}` (or `'prefill': {..., 'method': _method}`) to the options map in `_openCheckout`, so the selected instrument is the one the gateway opens on.

verdict.reason: Verified: in app/lib/features/checkout/payment_screen.dart, `_method` is referenced only three times — declared at line 45 ("display selection within Razorpay"), read at line 413 for the selection ring, and written at line 417 in the tap handler. A repo-wide grep finds no other consumer. The `_razorpay.open({...})` map (lines 127-137) sends key/order_id/amount/currency/name/description/prefill/theme/retry only, and `_prefill()` (lines 141-155) returns just name/email/contact, so neither `method` nor `prefill['method']` is supplied. `placeOrder` (lines 81-88) gets `draft.paymentMethod` ('razorpay'/'cod'), not `_method`. Server side does not compensate: `createRazorpayOrder` in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts posts only `{amount, currency, receipt, notes}` to the Razorpay Orders API, imposing no method restriction. The screen is reachable — checkout_screen.dart:831 pushes Routes.payment whenever paymentMethod == 'razorpay' && payablePaise > 0. Web has no equivalent selector (its /checkout/payment page just redirects), so there is no shared-behaviour justification. This is not in the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list and is not cosmetic: the fix is passing the chosen method into the Razorpay options (e.g. prefill['method']), with no UI change needed. Genuine dead-control defect.

findings.title: "Download invoice" on the order-success screen is a dead button claiming the order service is not live
findings.detail: The button's only handler is `toast.message('Your invoice will be emailed once the order service is live.')` — no navigation, no callable, no download. The order service is deployed (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts exists, and the site already ships an invoice screen at web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx), so the message is a stale placeholder from the pre-deploy era — the same era as the CF_UNAVAILABLE_MSG constant in checkout.ts:24, which is now unused.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer places a COD order, lands on /checkout/success, clicks "Download invoice" → a toast says invoicing is not live yet. No invoice is fetched or downloaded, even though /account/orders/{id}/invoice would render it.
findings.fix: Link the button to /account/orders/{orderId}/invoice (the placed draft would need to carry orderId alongside shortId, which placeOrder already returns), or remove the button.

verdict.reason:
I tried hard to refute this and could not.

Verified at /home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/success/page.tsx:67-74: the "Download invoice" button's entire onClick is toast.message('Your invoice will be emailed once the order service is live.'). No router push, no Link wrapper (contrast the sibling "Track order" button, which IS wrapped in <Link href="/account/orders">), no callable, no download.

Refutation attempts and why each fails:
1. "Handled elsewhere / not really dead" - no. The screen is reachable (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:214 router.push('/checkout/success') right after a successful placeOrder), and this button is the only invoice affordance on it. Every other surface links to a working route: web/src/components/account/OrderCard.tsx:91 and web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:226-228 both render "Download invoice" as <Link href={`/account/orders/${order.id}/invoice`}>, and that page (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx) renders a full invoice from order data immediately - it only gates order.invoiceUrl (the PDF) behind delivery. So the success screen is the one place the same label does nothing.
2. "The message is accurate - invoices really are emailed later" - no. There is no mail infrastructure at all: grep for nodemailer/sendgrid/sendMail/sendEmail across functions/src returns zero hits. And the order service demonstrably IS live - the user only reaches this screen because the deployed placeOrder callable succeeded; functions/src/orders/invoice.ts is exported at functions/src/index.ts:24. The toast is a stale pre-deploy placeholder, same vintage as the now-unused CF_UNAVAILABLE_MSG at web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:24 (grep finds only its definition and a doc comment - no consumers, unlike the still-used twin in components/account/orders.ts:20).
3. "Known + intentional" - not on the list (OTP mock, IFSC mock, referral retro-link, App Check). Nothing in the file marks it deferred; the comments there document the StrictMode snapshot logic, not a stub.
4. "Purely cosmetic" - no. It is a control that performs no action; the fix is behavioural, not visual.

The fix is small and local: web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:212 already receives res.orderId (placeOrder's return type at checkout.ts:202 is { orderId, shortId, amountPaise, paymentMethod }) but discards it - PlacedOrder (checkout.ts:147-151) carries only shortId/amountPaise/arrivesBy. Adding orderId to PlacedOrder and wrapping the button in <Link href={`/account/orders/${placed.orderId}/invoice`}> reuses the existing working invoice route with no backend work.
